117. **Rejected for the performance round (owner).** Each item was considered and is out, with the reason: raising `LIMIT` to make recursion faster (it moves the overflow, §17.112); lexical handler semantics (changes §5.5 to copy Effekt); multi-shot `resume` (v0 has none, §5.5); an `Async` colour or `@suspends` annotation (suspension is inferred, §17.111); `@inline`, `@pure`, `@hot`, `@noinline` (the compiler knows; an annotation an agent must remember is a cost paid on every path); per-call-site specialisation and monomorphisation (unbounded, nondeterministic code size); relying on an engine's proper tail calls (not portable); wrapping or unchecked arithmetic by default or under `--release` (D001/D003 are the semantics); dropping contract checks by build mode (§7.2: only `proved` removes a check); JS exceptions for control flow or stack switching (§13.3); a global handler-environment register (R01 §4.5); pipeline fusion before builders are measured; a user-facing builder or mutable array; a benchmarking service in this round; a single "language speed" score. Performance: none. Changed: none. Impact: none.

118. **M4 and M5 carry the direct lattice and research/10 ranks 7–10 (owner; M4-LIR, M4-OPT, M5).** Decision: the facts of §17.111–§17.113 are backend-independent: the LIR computes them from the same Core (the §17.107 snapshot), and the two backends' `--dump direct` outputs must agree (a parity test in M4-TEST). M4's acceptance (§14.3) gains: direct calls and frame reuse in the LIR for direct regions, scalar `Int`/`Float` unboxed at internal boundaries, `stats()` counters (frames, boxes, `Dup`/`Drop`) in every benchmark record, at least 2× over the all-frame/all-box baseline on `fib`, `countdown` and `nbody`, and the §17.98 proved-check removal deleting the predicate's computation as well as its `Check`. M5's acceptance gains the paired unique/shared workloads (`rbtree` with and without a retained version) reporting the reuse hit rate, and the §17.109 M5 envelope as its exit bar. Ordering: nothing in §17.111–§17.116 edits an M0–M3 crate, `runtime/js` or `std` before the M3 gates (`docs/plans/m3-completion-and-m4.md` §4); `bench/`, fixtures, ports and methodology start now; after the gates WS-P1, WS-P3, WS-P4 and WS-P6 run in parallel, WS-P2 after WS-P1, WS-P5 after WS-P4; every optimisation lands with a semantics test and a benchmark delta (plan §5). Why: research/10 §4 and §8; a fact computed twice from one IR is a parity test for free. Performance: the M4 and M5 ceilings of §17.109. Changed: §14.3 (M4, M5 acceptance). Impact: M4-LIR, M4-OPT, M4-TEST, M5; plan §4.

119. **`Fs.memory` composes with `Dir.subdir` and `Fs.rooted` exactly like the host (bugs1, research/ws7 gap 4).** Question: `with Fs.memory([("data/a.txt", …)]) { with Fs.rooted(Dir.subdir(Fs.root(), "data")) { Fs.read_text("a.txt") } }` fails with `this directory has no host access`, as §10.2 specified, so the §15.6 narrowing pattern cannot be tested against the fake; the store is handler state that `Fs.rooted` cannot reach. Decision: a memory `Dir` is a runtime object `{store, prefix}` over one mutable map from path to bytes, created by a std-private external `fs_memory_root(files) -> Dir` when `Fs.memory(files)` is evaluated, and **`Fs.memory(files)` is `rooted(fs_memory_root(files))`**: the memory handler has no state and no clauses of its own; every clause is the host's, over the `fs_*` and `file_*` externals, which dispatch on the `Dir`'s kind. Consequences, each the host's behaviour: (1) the store belongs to the handler value, as `rooted(dir)`'s `dir` does, so every `Dir` derived from its root by `subdir` and every handler installed over any of them share it, two installations of one `Fs.memory(…)` value share files, and a fresh `Fs.memory([…])` expression is a fresh store (the old per-installation reset was an artefact of handler state); (2) a write through any handler over the store is immediately visible through every other, and `with_file` writes through on each `write_chunk` (a body that fails leaves what it wrote, as on the host; the old "written back on return, not at all if it fails" sentence goes); (3) `Dir.subdir(d, name)` succeeds iff `prefix/name` is a directory, which in memory means some key starts with `prefix/name/`; a key equal to it is `not a directory`, nothing is `no such directory`, mirroring the host's `statSync`; `Fs.write` into a directory that does not exist fails as the host's does (there is no `mkdir` operation on either side); `Fs.list` returns the immediate children, files and implied directories, sorted, as today; `Fs.exists` is true for a file key or an implied directory; `read` of a directory fails. A memory `Dir` carries no grants, so no `[permissions]` check applies: its authority is the data it was built from, and `sakura test` needs no `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`. `fs_detached_root` is retired; `fixtures_dir("")` (no package) returns an empty memory root. The escape check is unchanged: a memory `Dir` is still scoped to the `with` that produced it. Why: a fake that cannot compose the way the real handler does cannot test the code that composes; one clause set over one dispatching capability makes the fake identical by construction instead of by maintenance. Rejected: a Sakura-level `Dir` representation (it would make `Dir` constructible and put the host/memory distinction in the type); the store as handler state with the runtime reaching back into another handler's instance; a public `Dir.memory` (user code must not construct capabilities, §6.2). Performance: a memory read is one hash lookup after a prefix join, and a write no longer rebuilds a persistent `Map`; tests get faster, nothing else changes. Changed: §10.2. Impact: requires change in `runtime/js` (memory kind in `Dir`, `fs_memory_root`, dispatch in `fs_*`/`file_*`) and `std/fs` (`memory` as `rooted`, docs, `std/INDEX.md`); `tests/semantics/std_fs_with_file.sak`'s memory cases re-blessed to host semantics and a new `fs_memory_rooted.sak` running §15.6's narrowing under the fake; routed to Opus (bugs1) as `docs/plans/performance-r1.md` §6 WS-FS, which may land before the M3 gates as a bug-fix-class change confined to the fs section of the runtime and `std/fs`.

120. **Gate 2 exemptions: `V9001`, `V8020`, runtime-constructed `D` codes (M3 gate audit, REQUESTS 2026-10-18; round 7).** Question: every registered code is constructed, but `V9001 internal_error` and `V8020 spec_frozen` have no `tests/ui` fixture, and `D004`, `D030`, `D031`, `D091` are constructed by `runtime/js`, which the gate's `grep … crates` never sees. Decision: gate 2 becomes a **two-way** check, every registered code constructed and every constructed code registered, over `crates`, `runtime/js` and `runtime/rt`. The fixture rule applies to codes a program can provoke from source alone. Exempt from it, each with the test that covers it instead: `V9001` (a compiler bug by definition; a fixture would be a test of the test; its construction is covered by the registry check), `V8020` (needs a git baseline: `cli.rs::frozen_specs_compare_with_git_head`), and runtime-limit defects (`D092 rc_overflow`, `D094 context_escaped`, `D096 heap_exhausted`: `sakura_rt`'s and `sakura_lir`'s own tests, e.g. `rc_overflow_is_D092`). `V9999` stays the unregistered sentinel; `W8001` stays skipped by milestone. `D092`, `D094`, `D096` (constructed by `sakura_lir/src/interp.rs` since `57ae00d`) and `W7002` (constructed by `sakura_verify`, §17.105) are registered in WS9, not at M4 integration, because the two-way check otherwise fails today. Rejected: a forced-failure test for `V9001` (an environment variable that makes a phase panic is a backdoor in the binary for one assertion). Changed: plan §4 gate 2. Impact: `sakura_diagnostics::codes` (four registrations), the gate text; routed to WS9.

121. **Gate 8 mechanism: `// fmt: exempt <reason>` and `fmt_clean` (M3 gate audit, REQUESTS 2026-10-18; round 7).** Question: `sakura fmt --check` over `tests/` cannot pass: `tests/fmt/*.sak` are formatter inputs, `tests/ui/V00xx` fixtures are parse errors, and four semantics fixtures keep a non-canonical layout to cover grammar productions; no exemption mechanism exists and CI never runs the check. Decision: the audit's proposal is endorsed with five amendments. (1) `// fmt: exempt <reason>` is a **harness directive** like `// mode:`, read only by the fixture harness's `directives()`; `sakura fmt` itself has no off-switch, so an agent cannot dodge the formatter in a program. (2) The directive is accepted only under `tests/semantics/` and `tests/ui/`; a `std/` or `examples/` file carrying it fails `fmt_clean`. (3) The reason names the grammar productions the layout covers (`// fmt: exempt covers Block NEWLINE rule`). (4) `fmt_clean` skips `tests/fmt/` entirely and a `tests/ui` fixture whose `expect:` holds a `V00xx` parse code; every other `.sak` under `std/`, `examples/`, `tests/semantics/` and `tests/ui/` must be formatted. (5) `fmt_clean` is a `sakura_cli` integration test, so gate 1 and the existing CI `cargo test --workspace` run it without a workflow change; gate 8 names it. Rejected: a file-level `// sakura-fmt: off` pragma in the formatter (a tooling-surface change needing an RFC, and a dodge). Why: the four fixtures are deliberate and documented, so the exemption is data about the fixture, not a formatter feature. Changed: plan §4 gate 8. Impact: `sakura_cli` tests (`fmt_clean`, `directives()` key), four fixture headers; routed to WS9.

122. **Cassette redaction policy and `schema_version` (security review packet B; round 7).** Question: cassettes redact only `secret_headers`; ordinary `headers`, the URL, the request body and `response_headers` (`set-cookie` included) are written verbatim, and the file has no `schema_version`. Decision: (1) the §17.73 guarantee is restated precisely: a **`Secret<T>` value never reaches a cassette** unless the program calls `Secret.expose`, which `sakura audit` lists; `Http.bearer` and `Llm.anthropic` put credentials in `secret_headers`, which the recorder never reads. The URL and body stay verbatim: they are the request, a replay must match them, and a `Secret` cannot enter them without an audited exposure (`V2032` in `url"…"`, `V2031` in `Json.encode`). (2) `Http.recording` **refuses credential-shaped ordinary headers**: a request whose `headers` has a name that lowercases to `authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `x-auth-token` or `cookie` fails with `HttpError { reason: "header <name> belongs in secret_headers (Http.bearer); not recorded" }` on hit and miss alike, before any forwarding, so a plain-string token is never written and the author is told the typed path. `Http.host` and `Http.scripted` are unchanged (they are not recorders). (3) `set-cookie` in `response_headers` is stored as `["set-cookie", "<redacted>"]`; the replayed response carries that literal, so the header's presence replays and its value does not. Other response headers are the server's data and stay. (4) The first line of a cassette is `{"schema_version": "1.0", "kind": "cassette"}`, as every other JSON record carries a version (§12.2, verifier records); exchange lines are unchanged. A missing or empty file is a cassette with no exchanges and gets the header on its first append; a file whose first non-empty line has no `schema_version`, or a major other than `1`, fails `open` with `HttpError` naming the file and `sakura test --record`; the three committed synthetic cassettes gain the line. (5) `--record` exposing the manifest's `env` keys to every test in the run (WS8 deviation 5) is endorsed: the list is the operator's declared allowance, the run is explicitly online, and a per-test grant would need a `Test.recording()` switch §17.102 rejected. Why: the type system, not a denylist, is the guarantee; the denylist catches the one mistake the types cannot (a credential that was never a `Secret`) and refuses rather than redacts, because a redacted value would also have to be matched. Rejected: an allowlist of request headers (every API's custom header would need listing, and redacted values break the key); redacting URL query parameters by name (guessing); signing cassettes (a committed cassette is reviewed like any committed test data; the roadmap already says the JS host is not a sandbox). Performance: test-only path; one lowercase compare per header per recorded request. Changed: §10.4. Impact: `runtime/js` cassette section, `std/http` docs, the three `examples/*/tests/fixtures/*.jsonl`, `website/content/docs/agents/cassettes.mdx`; routed to WS9.

123. **`Task.spawn` candidates are the body's free locals; escape-check answers for the reviewer (security review packet A; round 7).** Question: for a non-lambda `Task.spawn` body the check reads only the locals the expression mentions directly, so `Task.spawn(s, make(fn() { Fs.read(f) }))` with `f` bound inside an inner `with` is not reported (`escape.rs`, §17.89 (5)). Decision: the candidate set for any task body expression is its **free locals**: every local the expression mentions, descending into lambdas nested anywhere in it (call arguments, record fields, tuples, blocks) and subtracting the binders those lambdas and blocks introduce. The checker already computes this for lambdas (`facts.captures`); the body expression is treated as the body of an anonymous lambda. The rest of §17.70 (c) is unchanged: a candidate is reported when it holds a scoped type and was bound inside a `with` deeper than the `Scope`'s binding. Answers to the packet's other questions, all "as built": `Secret<T>` is **not** scoped (it is data, not authority; it may be stored and returned, and its guards are `V2031` and the audited `Secret.expose`); deferring affinity stands (the runtime closes a `File` at the callback boundary, so a late use is `FsError`, not authority); `V6001` as the only FFI guard stands (a std `@external` is in the trusted computing base of §6.6 and listed by `sakura audit`). Why: a soundness gap that one more call layer opens is a gap, not a refinement to wait for; the fix reuses the capture analysis and adds no rule. Rejected: walking nested lambdas but keeping their parameters (false positives on `fn(f) { … }` shapes). Performance: compile-time only, one walk per spawn site. Changed: §6.3. Impact: `sakura_types/src/check/escape.rs` (`spawns`, `used_locals`), `tests/escape.rs`, a `tests/ui/V6002_spawn_nested_lambda` fixture; routed to WS9.

124. **`url"…"` interpolates through `UrlPart.from<T: Show>` (WS8 deviation 1, security review packet C; round 7).** Question: `url"…"`'s element type is `String`, which has no home-module `from`, so `Untrusted<String>` in `url"…"` is `V2001` although §4.11 and §6.4 promise an encoded component, and an `Int` or `Uuid` interpolation is `V2032`. Decision: a new std module `std/urlpart` declares `pub opaque type UrlPart = UrlPart(String)`, `pub fn from<T: Show>(v: T) -> UrlPart` (percent-encodes `show(v)` with the unreserved set `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~`, as `Url.encode_component` does today) and `pub fn to_string(p: UrlPart) -> String`; `std/url`'s `template(parts: List<String>, args: List<UrlPart>) -> Url` joins the parts. Then §4.11 applies unchanged: a `String`, `Int` or `Uuid` goes through `UrlPart.from`, an `Untrusted<T>` is unwrapped and goes through `UrlPart.from` (§17.101), a `Secret` stays `V2032`, and a `UrlPart` passes through, which is safe because the type is opaque and only `from` builds one. `Url.encode_component` stays and is implemented by `UrlPart`. Why a module of its own: the home-module rule gives a module one `from`, and `std/url`'s is the refinement intro of `Url` (`Url.from(s)`), which a declared `from` would shadow. Rejected: a checker special case letting `Untrusted<String>` pass into a `String` element for the prelude tags (a user tag with `String` elements could splice, and `Int` would stay rejected); a refinement `Component = String where is_encoded(it)` (its `from` checks, it does not encode). Performance: `show` of a `String` is the identity; one encoding pass per interpolation, as today. Changed: §4.11, §10.3. Impact: `std/urlpart` (new), `std/url`, `std/INDEX.md`, `docs/llms.txt`; the std test "template percent-encodes interpolated values" and a `tests/semantics/url_untrusted_component.sak`; routed to WS9.

125. **WS8 deviations reviewed (plan §7, WS8 items 1–6; round 7).** Decision: endorsed as built, with two spellings and one rewrite. (1) `TypedBody::unwrapped` beside `conversions`: endorsed; item 1's `url` gap is closed by §17.124. (2) `Untrusted<Html>` in `html"…"` rendering the escaped text of its shown form (`Html(&quot;…&quot;)`): endorsed; `Html` is opaque and not `Schema`, so the value arises only from `Untrusted.of(html"…")` in a test, the invariant "never markup" holds, and a special case would buy nothing. (3) The public std names `Cassette`, `Http.cassette(path)`, `open`, `replaying` : endorsed, with the spelling rule that `open` is written `Cassette.open(c)` or `c.open()` (the home-module form, §4.9) and never `Http.open(c)`, which reads as opening a connection; `std/llm` and `std/INDEX.md` use that spelling. (4) `Llm.replay`'s miss reason: the `V3003` rule is **not too strict**. §5.3 as written allows `try … catch` over a body whose row ends in a declared parameter when the arm names an explicit tag; checked on the binary with the std shape (`fn offline<T, e>(call: fn() -> T ! {Console | e}) -> T ! {Console, Fail<LlmError> | e} { try { inner(call) } catch { ProviderError(status, reason) => fail ProviderError(status, "{reason}; record it with Llm.recording") } }` checks and runs). Only a bare `try` (a `Result`) over such a tail is `V3003`, by design (§17.45). `Llm.replay` therefore rewrites its miss as above so the reason names both `Llm.recording` and `sakura test --record`, as §17.102 says. (5) The `test_env` builtin and the re-blessed `m1`/`m2` snapshots: endorsed. (6) `llm_extract` keeping both tests: endorsed. Why: every deviation is sound; (4) was a reading error, and the rule's wording in `V3003` already says "without `catch`". Changed: §10.7. Impact: `std/llm` (one `try … catch`, call spelling), `std/INDEX.md`; routed to WS9.

126. **Indexed update: `List.set` with a contract, path copy, in place when unique (WS-B sieve finding; round 7).** Question: there is no mutable array and no `List.set`, so `bench/programs/sieve` rebuilds the whole list once per prime, and any agent porting an array algorithm hits the same wall. Decision: `std/list` gains `pub fn set<A>(xs: List<A>, i: Int, x: A) -> List<A> requires 0 <= i && i < len(xs)` (an out-of-range index is `D020` at the call site, as `Path.of`'s `requires` is; `sakura verify` discharges it where the bound is provable), backed by a runtime builtin that copies one root-to-leaf path of the 32-way trie (O(log32 n), the old version intact). On native the same reuse rule as `List.push` applies (§8.1): when the refcount is one the leaf is written in place, and a forced copy in a loop is `W8001`. `Map.set` already exists; `xs[i] = v` sugar is **not** added (`var xs; xs = List.set(xs, i, v)` is the §8.1 idiom, and `V2040` catches the forgotten reassignment). Why: §17.103 forbids a hidden O(n) per use, and a persistent `set` keeps value semantics (§8.1) with no new type. Rejected: an `Array` resource or effect (aliasing semantics would contradict §8.1 and make memory a capability); exposing §17.116's transient builders (never a Sakura value); `set` returning `Option<List<A>>` (an allocation and an unwrap per write in the hot loop, for a bound the caller already checked); `List.update(xs, i, f)` (one `get` and one `set`; add it when a bench shows the double path walk). Performance: `sieve` drops from one full pass per prime to O(n log log n) sets of O(log32 n) each; `bench` records before and after and the gap to the JS control is the measure of the native in-place path later. Changed: §10, §13.4. Impact: `runtime/js` (`list_set`), `std/list`, `std/INDEX.md`, `docs/llms.txt`, `bench/programs/sieve` (Sakura port rewritten; the hand-JS control keeps its array); routed to WS9.

127. **The package name is the manifest's `name` (WS-B observation; round 7).** Question: `sakura_analysis` names every user package `main` (`PackageInput { name: "main" }`, `module_of`), so `import <manifest name>/x` is `V1005` while §9 says the first segment is the current package's name; `bench compile`'s corpus imports `main/gen/m<i>`. Decision: **a bug**, not a design change. The package name is `sakura.toml`'s `name`; a file run without a manifest (`sakura run file.sak`) is package `main`. `import <name>/x` resolves; under a named manifest `import main/x` is `V1005` with the note "this package is named `<name>`". The qualified module in JSON records (`"module": "<package>::<path>"`) follows, and snapshot paths are `<module>` inside the package as §5.8 says (D's 2026-10-18 request: the runner drops the package segment). Why: `docs/llms.txt` teaches agents §9; a compiler that contradicts it makes every agent-written import wrong. Rejected: amending §9 to `main` (a dependency's own modules would then collide with the application's). Performance: none. Changed: §9. Impact: `sakura_analysis` (`module_of`, `PackageInput`), `sakura_cli` (passes the manifest name; test runner snapshot path), fixtures whose JSON pins `main::` re-blessed, `bench/programs/*` imports; routed to WS9.

128. **M3 is complete pending review; M4 L3, V3, R4, W1 and C1 start before gate 10 signs (owner's cadence question; round 7).** Question: L1, L2, R1–R3, V1 and V2 have landed; L3, V3, R4, W1 and C1 wait on "the M3 gates", but gate 10 is the owner's human review and may take days. Decision: M3 is **complete pending review** on the commit where gates 1–9 and 11 pass after WS9 lands (the audit re-run of the gate report's follow-up 8), and L3, V3, R4, W1 and C1 may start then. Gate 10 stays open until the owner signs the packet, and until then the **reviewed surfaces are frozen**: `sakura_types/src/check/escape.rs` and the `V6001` part of `decls.rs`; the cassette code (`runtime/js` cassettes section, `std/http`'s `Cassette`/`recording`/`replaying`, `std/llm`'s `recording`/`replay`); the template conversion (`check/expr.rs` `template`, `lower/expr.rs` `untrusted_value`) and `std/url`, `std/urlpart`. WS9's own items (§17.122–§17.125) are the exception, because they are what the owner reviews; "changes requested" on the packet becomes a WS9b with the same freeze. The roadmap says "M3 complete pending the owner's security review (gate 10)" and flips to complete with the signed packet's commit. Why: gate 10 reviews rules, not integration; backend work does not touch the rules, and the freeze keeps the reviewed code identical to the signed code. Rejected: waiting (idle agents for a review that changes nothing they would build on); declaring M3 complete (the plan's gate 10 would be fiction). Changed: none here; plan §3.5, §4. Impact: plan text; `website/content/docs/roadmap.mdx` wording when the re-audit lands.

129. **ABI open questions P8–P12 and LIR errata L1–L12 (M4-RT `4f8c69e`, M4-LIR `57ae00d`; round 7).** Decision: P8 (results and caught errors travel in the task's return register, read first by the parent's resume block; `env` on the entry call only, kept in a slot when needed later; `frame` a transient borrow; a task's result a generic word) is endorsed and L3 confirms it from the LIR side. P9 (outcome numbers `ok 0, fail 1, defect 2, cancelled 3, pending 4, exit 5`, a defect's value its `D` number) is endorsed, with the amendment that W1's `run`/`outcome` exports carry the message and site too, because §12.2's defect record needs them. P10 (`4 ok_handle`: payload starts `kind, slot, generation`; a stale, duplicate or older-epoch completion retires the handle) is endorsed and binds the M4-WASM host. P11 (the runtime also queues a `complete` that arrives while the guest runs) and P12 (cancellation and finalizer semantics as written) are endorsed. M4-RT folds P8–P12 into the normative sections as ABI **1.0.2** and keeps the questions as history, as §17.108 did for E1–E12. L1, L3, L4, L5, L6 (M5 may mark builtin parameters borrowed), L7, L9 (constants per use in the interpreter; W1 may cache pure constants at module start, not observable), L10, L11 and L12 are endorsed as read. **L2: keep E2** with both conditions: `TupleGet` projects through the object's row kinds, and `Eq`/`Ord`/`Hash`/`Show` of tuples are row-blind, so `(3, 3)` built in generic and in monomorphic code is one value; this answers P5 (the LIR never coerces a tuple at an instantiation site). Rejected: all-word tuples (an `IntBox` per scalar element on every tuple built anywhere is the hidden per-use cost §17.103 forbids; the branch per generic read is paid only by generic code, and monomorphic reads have none). **L8** (`Unit`-typed Core temporaries represented as generic words) is endorsed as the LIR's reading, and the `sakura_core` fix (REQUESTS 2026-10-18 "give them their real type") joins **C1**, the after-the-gates `sakura_core` item. The `Snapshot::from_json` recursion-limit bug (REQUESTS 2026-10-18, deep `if`/`match` nesting) is a WS9 bug fix: `serde_json::Deserializer::disable_recursion_limit` under `serde_stacker`, with an explicit nesting bound checked in `Module::check` so hostile input is still an error, and `program(50)` joins the LIR corpus. Performance: P8 saves a slot per frame; L2 keeps monomorphic projection one load. Changed: none here (the ABI is normative). Impact: `runtime/rt/ABI.md` 1.0.2, `sakura_lir` (none), `crates/sakura_core_snapshot` (WS9), C1's scope.

130. **Trusted construction: an opaque type is `Schema` only in its declaring module (WS9.10 re-audit, security packet C; round 8).** Question: opaque types derive every constraint (§4.2, §17.10), so `Query<R>`, `Html` and `UrlPart` are `Schema` and `Json.decode` builds them from any JSON with no diagnostic and no audit site. Confirmed on `a843e60`: a `Query` decoded inside `type Report = { title: String, q: Query<Row> }` ran `select name from users where 1=1 --`; `{"Html":"<script>evil()</script>"}` decoded into `Html` rendered the script through `html"…"`; `{"UrlPart":"a&b=c"}` decoded unencoded. Every path that builds a value from data goes through the same `Schema` bound (`Json.decode`, `Sql.query<R: Schema>` rows, `Llm.generate<T: Schema>`, `Cli.parse`, `Tool.of`'s synthesized `f$Args`, and `property` parameters, whose generator `arbitrary` is schema-driven, with no obligation raised today), so each is the same hole; `File { id, … }` and `Cassette` are forgeable the same way. Decision: (1) **Two kinds of private construction.** A type whose invariant is a **predicate over its representation** is a refinement (§4.3): it decodes, because decoding runs the predicate. A type whose invariant is **how the value was produced** (a literal's text, escaping, encoding, a handle the runtime issued) is `pub opaque`, and nothing outside its module builds one from data. In the checker: `holds(T, Schema)` for an opaque ADT is false when the body being checked is not in `T`'s declaring module (the `constructors_visible` test `V1006` uses); inside it `Schema` derives structurally as today, because the module owns the invariant as it owns the constructors. `Eq`, `Ord`, `Hash` and `Show` are unchanged: they consume a value and never build one. A `T: Schema` bound is discharged where `T` is concrete, so `decode_any<T: Schema>` called with `T = Query<Row>` from user code fails at that call, `Report` above is `Schema` nowhere but `std/sql`, and `Tool.of(f)` on a `@tool fn f(q: Query<Row>)` fails at the rewritten `Tool.from` call. A `property` parameter's type gets a `Schema` obligation at its annotation; `sakura test --contracts` skips a `pub fn` whose parameter types are not all `Schema` in its module and names the parameter in the summary (no new code; the function's own `test` blocks still run). (2) **`V2033 opaque_not_schema`** (TYPE): "`Query<Row>` is opaque outside `std/sql`, so it is not `Schema`: a value comes from its module's constructors (`sql"…"`), not from data"; when the opaque type is a field of the required type the note names the path (`Report.q: Query<Row>`). Its own code, as `V2031` is, because the fix is specific and an agent reads the code before the message. (3) **No decoder opt-in in v0.** A program that has the representation in data decodes the representation and calls the module's checked constructor, one visible line at the boundary: `Html.text(s)` or `Html.untrusted(u)` (and `Html.raw(s, @trust("…"))` for stored markup, which `sakura audit` lists), `UrlPart.from(s)`, `Uuid.parse(s)`, `Decimal.parse(s)`. `UrlPart` does not "decode by encoding": a decoder that transforms the data it is given hides the boundary, and `from` is the same one call in the open. (4) **Std.** `Query<R>`, `Html`, `UrlPart`, `Prompt`, `File`, `Cassette`, `Tool<e>`, `Router<e>` stay opaque and have no JSON form outside their modules. `Uuid` becomes `pub type Uuid = String where is_canonical(it)` (as `Path` did, §17.54): `parse` lowercases then validates, `from_canonical` is the generated `from`, `to_string` stays as the coercion, `Random.uuid()` is unchanged, and `{ id: Uuid }` decodes with the check; `Show` prints the bare text. `Decimal` becomes `pub type DecimalRepr = { whole: Int, frac: List<Int> }` plus `pub type Decimal = DecimalRepr where is_canonical(it)` (`whole` the floor, `frac` digits 0–9 without a trailing zero): its JSON form is the record it already has today, so `examples/secrets`'s `Request.post_json(url, amount)` is unchanged; a predicate that leaves the contract subset falls to a `@total` helper. (5) **Audit and manifest: nothing new.** The rule is a compile error, so there is no site to list; a module decoding its own opaque type is its own construction and is read with its constructors. Why: §9 promised that a `Query` comes only from `sql"…"` and an `Html` only from escaping code; a constraint derived for free gave data a constructor the module never wrote. Rejected: splitting `Schema` into encode and decode constraints (every std signature changes, and the checker cannot tell which a bound is for); `V2032` with a note (the precedent of `V2031` is a code per explanation); a declared codec attribute now (speculative until a std type needs a form a refinement cannot express, §16.17; `Decimal` as `"12.34"` is the candidate); decoding an opaque type as `Untrusted<T>` (an `Untrusted<Html>` is still an `Html` after `trust`); a std generator `gen.html` or `gen.query` (code composes one with `gen.map(gen.string(8), Html.text)`). Performance: one visibility test per obligation on an opaque ADT; nothing at run time. Changed: §4.2, §4.3, §4.4, §7.4, §9, §10.3, §16.17. Impact: `sakura_types` (`adt_holds`, a `property` obligation), `sakura_diagnostics` (`V2033`), `sakura_cli` (`--contracts` skip), `std/uuid`, `std/decimal`, `std/INDEX.md`, `docs/llms.txt`, snapshots that pinned `Uuid("…")`; the security packet part C; routed to Opus as plan WS10 (gate 10 fix).

131. **A manifest may not name its package `std` or `main` (`V8002`; WS9 item 8 deviation 4; round 8).** Decision: `sakura.toml` with `name = "std"` or `name = "main"` is rejected when the manifest is read, `V8002 reserved_package_name` (PACKAGE phase), naming the file and the line: `std` is the standard library and `main` is the package of a file run without a manifest (§9, §17.127), and a user package under either name would make an `import std/…` or `import main/…` mean two things. Why: §17.127 made the manifest's name the first import segment, so the name space must stay unambiguous. Rejected: silently renaming (an import written against the manifest would then be wrong). Changed: §9 (one clause). Impact: `sakura_analysis` manifest loading, `sakura_diagnostics`, a `cli.rs` test and a `tests/ui` fixture; routed to WS10 item 6.

132. **`std/INDEX.md` and the website std listing follow the formatter's row order (WS9 deviation 6; round 8).** Question: the std reformat (§17.121 item 6) sorted effect rows as §12.5 states (alphabetical, `Fail<…>` last) in 35 files, and `std/INDEX.md` and `website/content/docs/stdlib.mdx` still show the hand-extracted order. Decision: the source is the truth and the formatter's order is the canonical one; **Sol regenerates** `std/INDEX.md`'s "Signatures" section and the website's std signatures from the formatted source, by hand as the INDEX header says, until `sakura doc --index` exists (then the index is generated and gate 5 diffs it). Changed: none. Impact: `std/INDEX.md`, `website/content/docs/stdlib.mdx`; routed to Sol.

133. **`sakura fmt`: an `if` with an `else` breaks every branch or none (std reformat observation; round 8).** Question: the formatter leaves `if String.contains(unreserved, c) { out = out + c } else {` with a multi-line `else` (`std/urlpart.sak`), so one branch is inline and the other a block, and the condition and the first statement read as one line. Decision: §12.5's "single-statement blocks stay on one line when they fit" applies to an `if` only when **every** branch of that `if` fits on one line (an `else if` chain counts as one `if`); otherwise each branch is a block with its statements on their own lines, `else {` and `} else if … {` on the `}` line as today. Why: the rustfmt rule; a reader scans branch heads, and a mixed layout hides one. Rejected: a width-only rule (the mixed form fits within 100 columns and is still the problem). Changed: §12.5. Impact: `sakura_fmt` (one layout rule), its corpus and `props`; a std reformat of the files it changes, with no hand edits (`fmt_clean` stays green); routed to WS10 item 7.

134. **`List.set` on the JS backend stays a path copy; in-place update when unique is the native reuse path (WS-B sieve, 34×/91× after `7ced139`; round 8).** Decision: deferred to the performance round with the measure in place. §17.126 stands: the JS backend has no reference counts, so "provably unique" there would be a static last-use analysis, which is M4-OPT/M5 territory (§17.109's reuse hit rate, §17.118's paired unique/shared workloads); the matched `sieve` ratio is recorded in `bench/README.md` as exactly the gap the native in-place path must close, and no JS special case is added before that path exists. Changed: none. Impact: `bench/README.md` notes the ratio as the §17.126 measure; nothing else. Amended by §17.149: ownership facts computed in Core authorise in-place update on the JS backend too, with the persistent operation as the fallback.
135. **A field assignment on a `var` of a refined type is `V2034`; rebuild through `T.from` or `T.validate` (WS10 question, REQUESTS 2026-10-18; round 9).** Question: `type Pos = PosRepr where it.n > 0; fn f(p: Pos) -> Pos { var x = p; x.n = -1; x }` checks and returns a `Pos` with `n = -1`, and since §17.130 made `Decimal` a refinement, `var x = d; x.frac = [5, 0]` builds a non-canonical `Decimal` outside `std/decimal`, which `opaque` used to forbid. Analysis: §8.1 says `x.n = v` on `var x` is sugar for `x = PosRepr { ..x, n: v }`, and a record update yields the base type, so the desugared statement assigns a `PosRepr` to a `var` of type `Pos`, which no other spelling of the program may do; the checker's `Stmt::Assign` arm (`check/expr.rs`) walks the field path and checks the value against the last field's type without looking at the types on the path. The hole is in the sugar, not in refinements. Decision: (1) **Rule.** In `x.f1.….fn = v`, when the type of `x` or of any proper prefix `x.f1.….fk` is a refined type (§4.3), the statement is rejected with **`V2034 refined_field_assignment`** (TYPE), naming the first refined prefix and its declaration: "`x.n = …` rebuilds `x` as a `PosRepr`, but `x` is a `Pos` (`PosRepr where it.n > 0`); a field assignment would skip the predicate". The rule holds in every module, the declaring one included: a refinement's invariant is its predicate, which `from` runs, so the declaring module has nothing to gain from a privilege (an opaque type's module owns the constructors, which is why §17.130 (1) privileges it). A refinement over a refinement is named at the outermost one and the rebuild nests (`Pos2.from(Pos.from(PosRepr { ..x, n: v }))`). Whole reassignment of a refined `var` is unchanged (`x = next(x)`; `d = Decimal.add(d, y)` in a loop), as is a field assignment on a plain record whose field is refined (`r.total = Decimal.add(r.total, y)`: the prefix `r` is a record and the value is checked against `Decimal` as today). (2) **Fix.** One `suggested` fix of impact `local` that rewrites the statement to `x = Pos.from(PosRepr { ..x, n: -1 })` (for a prefix, `r.total = Decimal.from(DecimalRepr { ..r.total, frac: [5, 0] })`). It is not `machine_applicable` because it adds a `from` site, a trusted introduction that `sakura audit` lists (§4.3); the message names `Pos.validate(…)?` as the spelling for data. (3) **Loops.** An accumulator that changes a field of a refined value per iteration pays one visible predicate per iteration through `from`, or keeps the base type inside the loop and enters the refinement once after it; both are the program's choice and neither is hidden. Why: §4.3's soundness argument is that a validated value cannot be invalidated later, and this sugar was the one statement that could; §17.103 forbids a hidden check at a use site, and re-checking silently at the assignment would be exactly that (the predicate's cost per assignment; `Decimal.is_canonical` walks `frac`), with a `D010` blamed on a statement that names no `from` and that no audit lists. Rejected: re-checking at the assignment (above); inferring `var x = p` at the base type (a `var` holding a refined value and reassigned whole is common and sound, and a silently widened `var` fails later where a `Pos` is expected); letting the sugar retype the `var` (a `var` has one type, §8.1); a `Pos { ..x, n: v }` update form that re-checks (it is `Pos.from(PosRepr { ..x, n: v })` with the audit site hidden); `V2001` with a note (the fix is specific, and `V2031`/`V2033` set the precedent of a code per explanation). Performance: none at run time; one type-definition lookup per field on the path at check time. Changed: §4.3, §8.1, `docs/llms.txt`. Impact: `sakura_types` (`check/expr.rs`, the `Stmt::Assign` arm resolves each prefix's type and stops at a refined one), `sakura_diagnostics` (`V2034` and its explain page), `tests/ui/V2034_refined_field_assignment.sak` (WS10's `Pos` program) and `tests/ui/V2034_refined_prefix_assignment.sak` (`r.total.frac = [5, 0]` through `Decimal`), `tests/semantics/refined_var_rebuild.sak` (whole reassignment in a loop, the `from` rebuild, a refined field on a plain record, and an `expect-defect D010` rebuild that violates), `sakura test --std` and the examples unchanged (no std or example file assigns a field of a refined `var` today; `tests/semantics/records.sak` assigns fields of plain records and stays green), one sentence in `website/content/docs/tour/types.mdx`; routed to **Opus as plan WS11**.
136. **Peak-RSS gate: the Node block is confirmed by a second group, the Bun verdict is advisory until the noise study clears it (WS-A measurement `99e1826`/`066a938`, WS-P1 deviation 7, WS-P3 deviation 6; round 9).** Question: §17.110 makes peak RSS up by more than 25% an immediate block on every lane. Astra measured unchanged `824a876` builds: for `shapes`/Sakura n=50000 the five-process maxima of three groups vary 2.2% on Node and 33.8% on Bun (individual Bun peaks 205–332 MB), individual peaks spread more than 25% in 16 of 168 Node cells and 9 of 168 Bun cells, and Astra kept the maximum-based block on both engines with medians printed as diagnostics. In the same window the gate caught a real regression: `binary_trees`/Node 198 → 291 MB after WS-P3 was a dead ANF temporary in direct twins (§17.138), not noise. Decision: the gate stays maximum-based and stays a block, with two amendments. (1) **Confirmation, as for time.** On Node a maximum rise above 25% in a cell is confirmed by one automatic second group of five fresh processes of that cell in the same job (the mechanism §17.110 already prescribes for the 10% time block); the block needs both groups' maxima above the baseline maximum by more than 25%, and a single crossing is a warning annotation carrying the `rss` diagnostic rows (base and head maxima, medians, counts). (2) **Bun is advisory.** On Bun the same crossing, confirmed or not, is a warning annotation and never a block, until Astra's unchanged-commit noise study (at least ten groups of five on the reference machine with load recorded, and on `macos-latest`, over every cell the §17.110 selection rule picks) shows that rule (1) would have produced no false block on Bun; that result amends this entry and turns the Bun block on. The emitted module and `runtime/js` are the same files on both engines, so a memory regression in the compiler or the runtime shows on Node, whose peaks are the stable measurement; Bun's peak is dominated by JSC's heap sizing under a changed allocation rate, which the unchanged-build swings (304–402 MB in WS-P1's runs) demonstrate. Baselines stay human-blessed (§17.110); the harness never reruns until green, and the confirmation group's samples are retained in the artefact like every other. Why: a block that fires on unchanged code is either ignored or rerun until quiet, and both end the gate; a block confirmed by an independent group on the engine whose measurement is stable keeps what caught `binary_trees`. Rejected: a wider Bun margin (a number from one cell); a median gate (Astra's evidence: the median also crosses on selected cells and hides a peak-only regression); more processes per cell everywhere (double cost for a tail statistic that converges slowly); dropping the gate (it found a real bug within a day); a quiet-host precondition (a CI runner has none; the reference machine's load is already recorded for the bless review). Performance: none at run time; one extra group per crossing in CI. Changed: §17.110 (pointer), plan `performance-r1.md` §3.4. Impact: `bench/harness` compare and the confirmation group (WS-B, Opus) with fixtures (a Node first-group-only crossing warns, a confirmed crossing blocks, a Bun crossing warns); `bench/README.md` "Peak RSS" section and the noise study (Astra); `bench.yml` only if the timing confirmation lives there (Sol).
137. **Z3 5.3.1 and cvc5 1.4.2 are installed in the required Rust CI jobs, and a skipped verify test in CI is a failure (round 9).** Question: `sakura verify`'s CLI tests (`verify_reports_the_scale_acceptance`, `verify_warns_w7002_on_a_vacuous_obligation`) and `sakura_verify`'s `tests/live.rs` skip with a message when the pinned Z3 is not on `PATH`, and no CI job installs it, so the §14.3 M4 acceptance program has never run in CI. Decision: (1) the existing `Rust (ubuntu-latest)` and `Rust (macos-latest)` jobs of `ci.yml` install the pinned solvers before `cargo test --workspace --locked`: the Z3 5.3.1 and cvc5 1.4.2 release archives for the runner's OS and architecture, downloaded from the projects' GitHub releases with their sha256 pinned in the workflow, unpacked outside the checkout and added to `GITHUB_PATH`, cached with `actions/cache` keyed on tool, version, OS and architecture; the versions are written once in the workflow's `env`, and the tests' pin check (`SolverKind::pinned`) is the cross-check, because a mismatch fails the tests with the solver's reported version. No separate job and no change to `ci-required`: the tests already live in the workspace run that `ci-required` needs; the point is that they stop being skippable. (2) `has_z3()` in `cli.rs` and `z3()` in `live.rs` **fail instead of skipping when the `CI` environment variable is set** (GitHub sets `CI=true`), so an install step that breaks cannot silently restore today's state; locally the skip and its message stay. (3) Both operating systems, because §17.106 requires statuses to be deterministic across machines and the two runners are the cheapest cross-machine check of that; a Z3 or cvc5 upgrade is a design entry first (§17.106) and a workflow edit second. cvc5 is included because M4-VERIFY's acceptance (plan §3.1) says a cross-check agrees on every `unsat` in the corpus and `live.rs` already performs it when cvc5 is present. Why: a test that never runs in CI is documentation; the acceptance of M4's verification half must execute on every pull request that can break it. Rejected: a separate non-required `verify` job (red without blocking is the state being left); nightly only (verification changes land through pull requests); building Z3 from source (minutes per run, and the release binaries are the pinned artefact); the compiler downloading a solver (plan §3.5: nothing is downloaded). Performance: compile and check latency unchanged; about a minute per job on a cache miss. Changed: none in the design text; plan §3.1 M4-TEST. Impact: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Sol), the two guards in `crates/sakura_cli/tests/cli.rs` and `crates/sakura_verify/tests/live.rs` (Sol), a gate-report note that `W7002` is now exercised through the CLI in CI; acceptance: a master run whose logs show the three tests running on both runners, and a deliberate run with the install step disabled failing them.
138. **`binary_trees` peak RSS after WS-P3: a dead one-use ANF temporary in direct twins; fixed by adjacent producer–consumer inlining in direct emission, the gate unchanged (Astra `be5ec42`, WS-P3 deviation 6; round 9).** Finding (Astra): the direct `run$d` holds `r_1 = bottom_up$d(t_1)` (the stretch tree) live after its only use `r_2 = check$d(r_1)` until the frame returns, so 65,535 dead nodes (6.8 MB) survive the first scavenges, V8's allocation-site pretenuring then sizes the old generation for them, and the peak lands at 291 MB against 196 MB for CPS and 153 MB for hand JS; inlining the bind as `check$d(bottom_up$d(t_1))` brings five peaks to 154–165 MB at the same time, and last-use clearing (`r_1 = undefined`) does the same. Decision: **endorsed as routed to WS-P2**, the next owner of `emit.rs`. The mechanism is general, not a benchmark special case: in a direct twin, a one-use ANF bind whose value is a reference (not a scalar) and whose single use is an argument of the **immediately following** bind is emitted inline in that argument position. Adjacency is what makes it free: every other argument of the consumer is an atom (ANF), so evaluation order, the order of possible defects, blame spans, `Check` binds (never crossed: a `Check` between the two breaks adjacency) and the gauge prologue and epilogue are untouched. A one-use temporary that is not adjacent to its consumer is cleared at its last use (`r = undefined` after the consuming statement) only if WS-P2 measures a remaining regression once the inlining lands; it is not added speculatively. The CPS body is unchanged (its lifetimes are the frames'). The gate stays: no `--max-old-space-size`, no forced GC, no re-bless of the 198 MB baseline, no `binary_trees` exemption; the WS-P3 block closes when `bench compare` of the full unchanged configuration is green on the reference machine (Astra remeasures). Astra's second observation, that a `Tree` costs 104 bytes per node as a tagged record with a fields array against hand JS's 40, is a representation question for the LIR and the next performance round, not for this fix: Astra writes it up (`research/10-evidence/record-representation.md`: the JS object shapes, the LIR layout table's equivalent, what `Show`/`Eq`/`Schema` need from the representation) and a later round decides; nothing in the ABI changes now. Why: the lifetime fix removes a dead root the hand-written program never had and makes direct code no worse than CPS on memory, which is what §17.112 claimed; the representation change is a different decision with ABI cost. Performance: `binary_trees`/Node peak back under the baseline plus 25% with the WS-P3 time unchanged (40.5 against 40.2 ms in Astra's diagnostic build). Changed: none. Impact: `crates/sakura_codegen_js/src/emit.rs` (WS-P2, Opus); a `tests/semantics` fixture pinning blame and defect order across an inlined bind (`direct_inlined_bind_blame.sak`: the producer defects, then a variant where the consumer defects, each `expect-defect` with the span the un-inlined form reported); an emitted-JS snapshot of `research/10-evidence/micro.sak` showing the inlined form; the full-suite remeasure and a `bench/deltas.md` row (Astra). **Amended (round 11, §17.156 (4)):** the consumer must be a call, never an allocation (an allocation consumer kept `binary_trees` at 257–290 MB); the snapshot is the regression test's program, since `micro.sak` has no adjacent one-use reference bind.
139. **After the in-flight work: M4 remainder, the performance close-out and M5 preparation, in that order (round 9).** Question: with M3 complete pending gate 10, M4's R1–R3, L1–L3, V1–V3 and C1 landed, W1/R4 landing and WS-P2, WS-P4 and WS-P6 in flight (WS-P5 after WS-P4), what runs next and in what order. Decision: the pace stays "develop properly toward a stable version", with no beta push; the order is (a) WS11 (§17.135) and the solver CI change (§17.137) now, independent of everything; (b) W2, the whole corpus and the twelve examples on WASM with identical traces and host-import coverage, as soon as W1 is on master, with M4-TEST's parity matrix in `ci.yml`; (c) L4, the LIR's direct facts agreeing with `--dump direct` (§17.118), direct calls and frame reuse in direct regions and unboxed scalars at internal boundaries, after WS-P2 has settled `direct.rs`; (d) the performance round close-out when P2, P4, P5 and P6 are in (full-suite remeasure, the §17.109 JS acceptance, an owner-blessed baseline, the §17.136 harness change); (e) M4-OPT (`--layout=niche`, the proved-check removal deleting the predicate's computation, the 2× all-frame/all-box bar on WASM) after W2's parity; (f) the WASM lane in `bench` and the §17.109 M4 envelope; (g) M5 preparation as research only (Perceus reuse over the LIR's `Dup`/`Drop`, a Cranelift survey, the record representation of §17.138, `W8001`), feeding a design round that writes the M5 plan. Gate 10 is the owner's and lifts the §17.128 freeze whenever it is signed. Why: parity before optimisation (M4-OPT measures against a corpus that must already agree on both backends), measurement before M5 (the M4 envelope is M5's baseline), and nothing starts on a surface another in-flight workstream is editing. Changed: plan `m3-completion-and-m4.md` §2 (WS11), §3.1 (M4-TEST), §3.7 (new). Impact: the plan routes each item with owner, paths, dependencies and acceptance.

140. **The agent DX programme: an agent must be able to learn, write, check and ship Sakura from the toolchain alone (owner request 2026-10-18; research/11; round 10).** Question: the owner asks for "proper skills and stuff, in the website etc, so agents can easily understand the language, and whatever else is needed". Decision: a programme of nine workstreams, routed by `docs/plans/agent-dx.md` (DX0–DX8), in this order: DX0 correct every agent-facing surface that contradicts the built compiler (§17.141); DX1 one portable Sakura skill generated from the compiler's own sources and tested in CI (§17.142); DX2 `sakura new`/`init` write agent instructions and `sakura setup` installs client adapters (§17.143); DX3 generated error-code reference pages (§17.144); DX4 a tested cookbook (§17.145); DX5 the agent evaluation pilot, offline parts in CI, paid runs owner-approved (§17.146); DX6 the first release and installers, prepared and awaiting owner authorisation (§17.147); DX7 editor support; DX8 playground and Linguist, deferred behind their prerequisites (§17.148). Principles that every workstream obeys: (1) **one source, mechanical adapters**: the language guide is `docs/llms.txt`, the std surface is `compiler/std/INDEX.md` and the std sources, the diagnostics are `sakura_diagnostics::codes::REGISTRY`, the examples are `compiler/examples/`; the skill, the error pages, the cookbook and the website mirrors are generated from them by one generator and CI fails on a stale regeneration; nothing agent-facing is hand-maintained twice. (2) **Compiler-matched**: every bundle states the commit and compiler version it was generated from, and the CLI embeds its own copy (as it embeds `docs/llms.txt`), so an agent with the binary has the matching skill without the network. (3) **Executable**: every complete Sakura code block that an agent may copy is a fixture the CLI harness checks, and fragments are labelled; no advertised sample is skipped. (4) **Nothing publishes or escalates by itself**: scaffolding writes only project-local files, never global dotfiles; no workflow publishes a binary, package, extension or plugin without the owner's explicit run; paid model calls need an approved budget. (5) **Measured, not assumed**: the pilot measures discovery and activation of the skill, not only its content, because research/11 §2 shows a skill that is not invoked is a cost without a benefit. Why: a language for agents is adopted through the agent's first ten minutes, and research/11 §1 found that today those minutes meet stale status claims, no skill, no scaffolded instructions and no release. Rejected: a second language reference beside `docs/llms.txt` (two references drift; the skill links the guide and adds the workflow, the pitfalls and the repair table); a Sakura-specific MCP docs server (the compiler MCP's `docs_query` already ranks the guide, the std index and the registry); fine-tuning or training data before the docs-and-tools loop is measured (research/11 §5). Performance: none at run time; the generator runs in CI. Changed: §14.3 gains the programme's pointer. Impact: Opus codes (generator, CLI, harness, eval runner, release workflow, VS Code client), Sol does the mechanical parts (mirrors, adapters, CI wiring, website routes, ports), Astra authors prose and designs the experiment; the plan names paths, dependencies and acceptance per workstream.

141. **DX0: the agent-facing surfaces say what the compiler does today, before anything else is built (research/11 §1, §6 "very high / S"; round 10).** Decision: the following are fixed first, each by reading the source, never by guessing: (1) MCP `compiler_info.features` advertises `backends: ["js"]` and `verify: false` while `sakura build --target wasm` and `sakura verify` exist; it reports what the running binary provides, derived from the same facts `sakura --help` uses (a `backends` list, `verify: true` with the solver status it finds, `test_execution`), and `docs/mcp.md` and `website/content/docs/agents/mcp.mdx` stop calling the transport, options and `compiler_info` fields unsettled; `frozen_specs` is documented as optional on `check_patch`/`apply_patch`, and the design's `--tools` export and HTTP transport (§11.2) are labelled **planned** wherever the pages mention them. (2) `docs/llms.txt`'s status section still says the performance work is planned and WASM is M4-future; it states what landed (direct code, `--dump direct`, `--no-direct`, `--target wasm`, proved arithmetic) and what did not. (3) Root `AGENTS.md` says no workspace or toolchain exists; it points at `compiler/rust-toolchain.toml` and the three workspace checks as checks that *do* run today. (4) `website/lib/source.ts`'s llms preamble says the M3 std is not built; the llms-txt page calls `prompt` both implemented and future and `doc --search` planned; the diagnostics page says no phase-7 code is named while the verify page documents `W7002`; `STABILITY.md` is re-read against the same list. Each fix is one sentence of truth, not a rewrite. Acceptance: an `mcp.rs` test asserts `compiler_info` against the build's actual capabilities (a build with the WASM backend compiled in reports it); a doc test greps the agent pages for "planned"/"future"/"not yet" beside a feature the CLI test suite exercises; website `fmt:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build` on the touched files; every local link checked. Why: research/11 §1 calls the contradiction an onboarding defect, and an agent that reads `verify: false` never runs `sakura verify`. Rejected: waiting for the skill to carry the corrections (the skill links these pages). Performance: none. Changed: none in this document (§11.2's `--tools`/HTTP stays as design, labelled planned by the pages). Impact: Astra audits and writes the sentences, Sol applies them, Opus changes `compiler_info` (`sakura_mcp/src/lib.rs`); plan DX0.

142. **DX1: one portable `sakura` skill, generated from the compiler's sources, embedded in the CLI, mirrored on the website (research/11 §2–§3; round 10).** Decision: **Format.** Agent Skills `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter `name: sakura`, a `description` that names the triggers: `.sak` files, `sakura.toml`, effects, holes, Sakura diagnostics; `license`; `compatibility` naming the CLI; `metadata` with `version`, `sakura-compiler-version`, `sakura-compiler-git` and `sakura-edition`), a body under 500 lines and about 2,000 tokens, and `references/` loaded on demand; no `scripts/`, no `allowed-tools`, no hooks (the CLI already is the deterministic tool; a guide must not grant anything by loading). **Content of the body**, in this order: identify the compiler (`sakura --version`, `sakura prompt`); the one-screen cheat sheet against TypeScript/Rust transfer (explicit signatures, `!` rows and their omission for pure functions, positional calls, binding annotations instead of call-site generics, explicit non-prelude imports, `var` rebinding for `List.set`/`Map.set`, the `n == 0` guard idiom); the numbered loop (retrieve signatures with `sakura doc`/`symbol_query` → write signatures and holes → `check --json` → fill holes → `test --json` → `build` → report), with the CLI fallback when MCP is absent; four short complete examples (`Fail` recovery, a local handler, a refinement entry check, a deterministic fake effect); the error→cause→repair table seeded from `tests/ui` and extended from the pilot's actual failures (`V3001` local handler versus widening, `V2050` unfinished code, `V8020` change the implementation not the frozen task); the completion rule (no holes, independent tests pass, no contract or permission widened, audit/verify reported as evidence, never as certification). **References** are generated: `references/language.md` is `docs/llms.txt` verbatim; `references/stdlib.md` from the std sources through the `doc` machinery (indexed by module and task, full signatures; the hand-regenerated `std/INDEX.md` is replaced by this generator's output, closing its own "until `sakura doc --index` exists" note); `references/diagnostics.md` from the registry; `references/recipes.md` from DX4's recipes; `assets/` carries the DX2 templates. **Source and generator.** The authored body lives at `skills/sakura/SKILL.md` (a new top-level directory, recorded as an amendment to ADR 0002); a workspace tool `compiler/tools/agent_docs` (beside `tools/sakura_eval`) links `sakura_diagnostics` and the std loader and writes the references, the DX3 pages, the DX4 pages and the website mirror deterministically; `cargo run -p agent_docs -- --check` fails CI when any output is stale. The CLI embeds the bundle (every file as a string, like `LLMS_TXT`), and `sakura setup` (§17.143) writes it; the bundle's `metadata` is filled at build from the crate version and the git commit, so the binary always carries its matching skill. **Serving.** `website/public/skills/sakura/` is a committed byte-identical mirror (raw `SKILL.md` starts with the frontmatter, relative links work, nothing wraps it), beside `sakura-skill.zip` and `sakura-skill.sha256` and a content-only `manifest.json` with the compiler version, per-file SHA-256 hashes and ZIP SHA-256, without a Git commit (commit provenance is filled only at release/build time); the immutable URL of any revision is the repository's raw file at that commit (Git already is the versioned archive; the site never hosts per-commit copies); after the first release the ZIP is also a release asset. The agents landing page and `llms.txt` index link the skill, the install paths (`.claude/skills/sakura/`, `.agents/skills/sakura/`, `.cursor/skills/sakura/`) and the provenance. A Claude plugin and marketplace catalogue wrap the same files later (DX8, after the bundle is stable). **CI test** (`sakura_cli/tests/agent_docs.rs` over `compiler/tests/agent_docs/`): every complete code block in the body and references carries a fixture id and a mode (`check`, `test`, `run`, `wrong:<code>`, `fragment`, `hole-step`); unclassified fences fail; positive samples `check --json` to exit 0 with no error and no unexpected hole, `test`/`run` samples run offline with fakes and cassettes, wrong/fixed pairs assert the code and span then check the fixed program; frontmatter, relative links, JSON/TOML snippets, ZIP layout, checksums and mirror byte-equality are validated; no fixture may be skipped silently. Why: research/11 §3 (one source, several adapters; drift is the failure mode) and the Agent Skills specification's progressive disclosure; embedding in the binary is the only synchronisation that needs no network and no version negotiation. Rejected: a hand-written skill per client; a `scripts/` directory (the CLI is the script); a versioned archive on the site (Git); serving the skill through the `/docs/*.md` transformation (it wraps and rewrites); a `sakura doc --index` flag added only for the generator (the generator links the library). Performance: none at run time; the embedded bundle adds a few hundred kilobytes to the binary. Changed: §12.1 gains `sakura setup` through §17.143. Impact: Astra authors `SKILL.md` and the table, Opus writes `agent_docs` and the harness, Sol the mirror, ZIP, checksum and website links; plan DX1.

143. **DX2: `sakura new`/`init` write agent instructions; `sakura setup` installs the skill and client adapters, project-locally and opt-in (research/11 §4; round 10).** Decision: (1) `sakura new <kind> <name>` and `sakura init` also write, when absent, `AGENTS.md` (the research/11 §4 template prose, about 300 tokens: check the compiler version and read `sakura prompt`; use the `sakura` skill when installed; look up APIs with `sakura doc` or `symbol_query`; run `check --json`, `fmt --check`, `test --json`; finish holes before the final build; freeze specs for repairs; `explain CODE`; never widen contracts or authority to pass; verify `compiler_info.workspace_root` before trusting the MCP server) and `CLAUDE.md` containing the import line `@AGENTS.md`; existing files are never touched (`init` keeps its current rule: an existing `sakura.toml` is a usage error). (2) A new command, `sakura setup [--client claude|codex|cursor|all] [--apply]`, works in an existing project (it reads `sakura.toml`), prints what it would write and writes only with `--apply`: the embedded skill into `.claude/skills/sakura/`, `.agents/skills/sakura/` or `.cursor/skills/sakura/` per client; the MCP entry into `.mcp.json` (Claude), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), merging only the Sakura-owned `sakura` entry into an existing file and printing a patch instead when the file cannot be parsed; `.cursor/rules/sakura.mdc` for Cursor; `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` as in (1). It never edits `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or any file outside the project, never pre-approves a server, never starts one. (3) **The workspace-root convention**: the generated Claude and Codex entries run `sakura mcp serve` with no `--root`; the server resolves its root as the nearest ancestor of its working directory that holds `sakura.toml` and reports it in `compiler_info.workspace_root`; the Cursor entry passes `--root ${workspaceFolder}` because Cursor documents that variable; no snippet ever contains a developer's absolute path. A client started outside the project gets a usage error from the server naming the directory it searched, not a silently wrong root. (4) `sakura new` still does not run `git init` (§17.63). Acceptance: scaffold tests cover the four templates with the two new files, existing-file preservation, `setup` on a fresh scaffold, `setup` twice (idempotent), each client's file merged into an existing one, a malformed existing config (patch printed, nothing written), a path with spaces, and `mcp serve` started from a subdirectory and from outside the project; a documented smoke run per client (research/11 §4's list) recorded in the plan with versions, by hand, before the agents landing page advertises the command. Why: research/11 §4 (small canonical instructions, exact client formats, no global side effects) and the `init` constraint (it is not an updater, so a separate command is the accepted behaviour). Rejected: `init --agents` (`init` refuses an existing manifest); writing global client configuration; a cross-client root variable; a launcher script. Performance: none. Changed: §12.1 (`sakura setup`, `new`/`init` outputs). Impact: Opus (`sakura_cli/src/new.rs`, a `setup.rs`, `sakura_mcp` root resolution), Sol (adapter templates under `skills/sakura/assets/`, the website quickstart), Astra (the template prose); plan DX2, after DX1's embedded bundle.

144. **DX3: an error-code reference page per registered code, generated from the registry, with the `tests/ui` fixture as the wrong program (research/11 §6; round 10).** Decision: `agent_docs` renders `website/content/docs/errors/<code>.mdx` for every entry of `codes::REGISTRY` (73 today, retired codes included and marked retired): title, phase, the registry's explanation, the `tests/ui/<code>_*.sak` fixture as the wrong program with its expected JSON Lines diagnostic, and the fixed program from a sibling `tests/ui/<code>_<slug>.fixed.sak` when one exists, which the ui harness checks to exit 0 (Sol adds fixed companions code by code, most frequent first; a page without one says so visibly rather than failing the build). An index page lists codes by phase. The pages are committed MDX, so the existing Fumadocs search, the `/docs/*.md` export and `llms-full.txt` cover them with no new route, and a website build on the shallow Vercel clone needs no `cargo`. `explanation_uri` stays `sakura://explain/<code>` in the JSON record (§12.2 is a versioned contract); the website, the skill and the editor map it to `/docs/errors/<code>`, and `sakura explain` prints the URL after its text. Acceptance: the generator's `--check` fails on a code without a page or a page without a code; the ui harness runs every fixed companion; link check over the index. Why: §12.3 promised "every code has an `explain` page with a minimal pair"; generating it from the registry is the only way the promise stays true. Rejected: a JSON export plus a dynamic route (a second pipeline for the website to maintain); changing the `sakura://` scheme to HTTP (a protocol change for a presentation need). Performance: none. Changed: §12.3 (the page is generated; the URL mapping). Impact: Opus (`agent_docs` registry export), Sol (fixed companions, index page, website wiring), Astra (repair guidance in explanations that are fragments today); plan DX3, with DX1's generator.

145. **DX4: a cookbook of task recipes, each an example the harness runs (research/11 §6; round 10).** Decision: recipes live under `compiler/examples/<recipe>/` in the existing fixture shape (manifest, `src/main.sak`, tests, cassettes where needed) and are run by the examples harness like the twelve examples; `agent_docs` renders `website/content/docs/cookbook/<recipe>.mdx` and `skills/sakura/references/recipes.md` from them (source, the imports it needs, the `[permissions]` it declares, the failure branches it handles, how it is tested, and the compiler revision). First set, all offline with fakes or committed cassettes: parse and validate JSON into a refined record; a CLI over files; HTTP with retry and a cassette; a SQLite query with `sql"…"`; a router endpoint tested by calling the router; a scripted LLM tool; a budgeted agent loop; an indexed update loop with `List.set` (the §17.126 idiom, which the nbody port got wrong, §17.150). Recipes are distinct from the evaluation tasks of §17.146 (teaching a recipe must not reveal a held-out solution). Acceptance: every recipe passes its harness mode in CI; a recipe that uses an unfinished API is not published; the rendered pages regenerate clean. Why: agents copy; a copied recipe that runs is worth more than a paragraph. Rejected: prose-only recipes; recipes on the website only (they would rot). Performance: none. Changed: none. Impact: Astra writes recipes, Sol extracts and renders, Opus only where a recipe needs a missing tested example; plan DX4, after DX1.

146. **DX5: the agent evaluation pilot: offline oracles in CI, paid episodes only under an owner-approved budget (research/11 §5; round 10).** Decision: `evals/agent-dx/` at the repository root (recorded in ADR 0002), separate from `tools/sakura_eval` (a Core evaluator, not an agent benchmark): `tasks/<id>/{prompt.md, starter/, oracle/, task.json}`, `harness/`, `reports/`. `task.json` is an internal manifest documented in `evals/agent-dx/README.md` before implementation (id and revision, category, compiler revision and backend, starter hash, editable files, frozen baseline commit, oracle command, expected initial diagnostics, episode budgets, comparison eligibility); oracles are never on the agent's filesystem, and each starter commits a baseline so `--frozen-specs all --since <baseline>` has a real reference. **Tasks:** the twelve of research/11 §5 (two per category: syntax and data, diagnose and repair, holes and retrieval, small application change, deterministic effects, preserve assurance), with gold solutions validated and deliberately hollow solutions (removed tests, `.trust` shortcuts, widened permissions, leftover holes) proven rejected before any model runs. **Conditions:** baseline (no skill), guide (`sakura prompt`), skill (forced load and normal discovery, recorded separately), bootstrap (skill plus `AGENTS.md`), MCP (the best prior condition with the compiler MCP instead of the CLI, same information budget); ablations of cheat sheet, examples and repair table only on failing categories. **Metrics**, per fresh episode: pass@1 and budgeted episode success separately (repair turns never count as `k`), iterations to green (success fraction beside conditional median and p90; timeouts censored), diagnostic-fix success with specs and authority preserved, cost per accepted task (total spend over accepted tasks, undefined at zero), tokens including cached, activation and retrieval failures, unauthorised edits, termination reason. **Harness:** each episode in a disposable directory with network denied to the generated program, the toolchain pinned, the harness enforcing wall-clock and token limits itself (the compiler's budgets are soft), the provider broker outside the project holding the credentials; raw transcripts stored privately and redacted before any report is checked in. **Budget and approval:** the runner refuses to start without `--budget-usd <n>` and `--approved-by <name>`, estimates spend from the pinned prices before scheduling, stops when the cap cannot cover another episode, never retries unboundedly or escalates models; the GitHub workflow `agent-eval.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` only, runs in a protected environment whose required reviewer is the owner, takes the budget and the model identifiers as inputs, and never runs on pull requests. Pilot cap: 12 tasks × 2 conditions × 2 models × 1 episode = 48 episodes, 8 repair cycles, 12,000 output and 60,000 input tokens and 10 minutes per episode, 2 workers; a 3-sample replication (144 episodes) only after the harness is validated on a canned transcript. **Models:** one pinned Opus-family and one pinned GPT-6-Sol-family coding model as roles; the exact provider identifiers, reasoning and sampling settings, harness version and date are recorded per run and chosen at run time, never assumed here. **In CI on every PR, no secrets:** task schemas, gold and hollow oracles, the canned-transcript replay (accounting, timeouts, reporting), MCP smoke. **On demand, owner-approved:** model runs, the six-task TS/Python comparison (matched docs and tool budgets, pinned runtimes, Sakura-specific hole/effect/frozen-spec tasks scored separately), client UI smoke, held-out tasks. Twelve tasks are a diagnostic pilot, not a leaderboard; the report states per-task outcomes with raw counts and intervals, never a single score. Why: "agent-first" must be falsifiable (more independently correct changes per bounded cost, fewer repairs, no unauthorised spec changes), the Vercel and SWE-Skills-Bench results show activation and version mismatch dominate, and real models cost the owner money, so the harness makes approval a precondition rather than a convention. Rejected: a scheduled paid suite (a separate owner decision); counting repair turns as samples; a no-docs condition as the only baseline; inferring language superiority from a trained-in comparison. Performance: none. Changed: none. Impact: Opus (runner, isolation, accounting), Astra (task design, experiment protocol, report), Sol (fixtures, workflow, environment); plan DX5, offline parts after DX1 and DX2, paid runs when the owner approves.

147. **DX6: the first release is prepared end to end and waits for the owner's authorisation at every publishing step (research/11 §6; round 10).** Decision: (1) **Artifacts.** A `release.yml` triggered by a `v*` tag or `workflow_dispatch` in dry-run mode builds `sakura` for the owner-approved matrix (proposed: macOS arm64 and x86_64, Linux x86_64 and arm64 with musl, Windows x86_64), with `--locked`, the embedded std, `docs/llms.txt` and the skill from the same commit, SHA-256 sums, licence notices, and the skill ZIP; dry runs upload workflow artifacts only and create no release. A release note states the JavaScript host prerequisite (Node, the pinned major) for `run`/`test` on the JS target, and that `check`/`build`/`doc`/`mcp` need no host. (2) **Installer.** Astra evaluates `cargo-dist` first (it generates the workflow, archives, checksums, shell and PowerShell installers, a Homebrew tap formula and an npm wrapper from one configuration; uv is the precedent) against a hand-written `tools/install/` script; whichever is chosen must support a pinned version, checksum verification, platform detection, a non-interactive prefix, a plain download-and-extract path (never only `curl | sh`) and a clean failure on an unsupported target. (3) **Channels**, each prepared as a reviewed file and published only by the owner: a Homebrew tap formula in an owner-named tap with a smoke test (never assumed into core), an npm wrapper package with `bin`, `os`/`cpu` platform packages and a verified offline path (name reserved by the owner), the Claude plugin and marketplace catalogue (DX8), the VS Code extension (DX7). (4) **Versioning.** The first tag is `v0.1.0-alpha.1`; `STABILITY.md` says what an alpha promises (nothing beyond the versioned diagnostic schema and the fixture formats); the skill, the docs and the binary carry the same version. (5) **Acceptance** on a fresh host per platform: download → `sakura --version` → `new cli demo` → `check` → `test` → `build` → `mcp serve` smoke → `setup --apply` writes the skill; no published artifact is ever mutated. Why: research/11 §1 and §6: the first install is where adoption is lost, and a source build with a pinned toolchain is not an install story; publishing is the owner's act, so the work ends at a reviewed artifact. Rejected: publishing from CI on merge; a mutable "latest" release; a Homebrew core submission. Performance: none. Changed: none (`STABILITY.md` is the owner's to amend at the tag). Impact: Opus (workflow, installer logic), Sol (matrix, formula, wrapper, notices), Astra (evaluation and release docs), owner (matrix, namespaces, credentials, every publish); plan DX6, after DX2; the owner's questions are listed in the plan. **Amended (round 11, §17.157):** the matrix is the owner's GNU A→B→C (no musl); the tooling is the hand-written workflow of ADR 0003; crates.io is deferred for the alpha.

148. **DX7 and DX8: a VS Code client over the existing LSP now; tree-sitter, plugin packaging, the playground and Linguist behind their prerequisites (research/11 §6; round 10).** Decision: (1) `editors/vscode/`: a thin client that starts `sakura lsp` from the configured or `PATH` executable, registers `.sak`, surfaces diagnostics with their `/docs/errors/<code>` link, hole context on demand, formatting and quick fixes with their impact class shown; the website's highlighting grammar is converted to its TextMate grammar; tests cover stdio start, root selection, UTF-16 positions on edits, stale fixes after an edit and a missing executable; installable from source (`vsce package` locally); marketplace publication is the owner's. (2) `editors/tree-sitter-sakura/` after (1): a grammar with a corpus derived from the compiler's lexer and parser cases (holes, tagged strings, comments, the §2.4 newline rule), tested against the CST on `tests/`; useful for editors and tooling, not a second parser of record. (3) The Claude plugin and marketplace (`plugins/sakura/`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) wrap the DX1 bundle after it has been stable for one release; validated with `claude plugin validate`; the plugin version is independent of the compiler version. (4) The browser playground is **post-WASM and post-host**: it needs the checker compiled to WASM or a sandboxed checking service, a browser host with only pure effects and `Console.captured`, bounded worker execution with cancellation and no Node file or network bindings; the program-side WASM backend of M4 is necessary and not sufficient (research/11 §1). It starts after W2 parity and M4-OPT (`m3-completion-and-m4.md` §3.7 items 3 and 7) with pure examples, diagnostics and share links; nothing before. (5) GitHub Linguist is deferred until the usage threshold is met honestly; no manufactured repositories. Why: the LSP exists and is tested; the rest has prerequisites research/11 §6 lists, and an early playground that cannot run effects would teach the wrong language. Rejected: a playground over the Node host; a tree-sitter grammar as the formatter's or LSP's parser. Performance: none. Changed: none. Impact: Opus (client, grammar), Sol (packaging), Astra (setup docs); plan DX7 after DX6's executable story, DX8 as stated.

149. **Ownership facts in Core: an owned `List`, `Map` or `Set` is updated in place on every backend, with the persistent operation as the fallback (research/10-evidence/perf-gaps-r2 rank 1; WS-P6 item 7 `map_set`; amends §17.134; round 10).** Question: `sieve` copies 1,592,937 path arrays (40.8 million slots) for 398,286 writes, and in-place writes on the unchanged trie are 5.82×/11.61× faster; `map_set` on Bun is ≈5.0 against a 3.0 ceiling because every HAMT insert copies 32-wide nodes where the control mutates a JS `Map`; §17.134 deferred any JS special case until the native reuse path existed. Decision: **one policy for `List`, `Map` and `Set`, decided now, in Core.** (1) A new deterministic pass `sakura_core::opt::owned` computes, per def, an *owned* fact for the consuming argument of each owned-capable builtin (`list_set`, `list_push`, `map_set`, `map_remove`, `set_add`, `set_remove`; the table in `sakura_core::builtins` gains two columns: `fresh`, a result that shares no node with any input, true for literals with elements, `list_range`, builder results and the string-splitting constructors, false for the empty singleton, `list_push`, `list_slice` and anything the runtime does not guarantee; and `consumes`, the argument position an owned-capable builtin takes over).
