(G07) §5.5 said state is "initialized once per `with` installation"; the checker charges a state initializer's row to the `handler` expression (`expr.rs`, `row = self.seq(&rows, e)`), Core lowers the initializers as the expression's operands (`lower/expr.rs` 1994), the JS runtime's `install` copies the handler value's slots into a fresh instance and ABI §6.3 says the same; `runtime.test.js` shows two installations of one value giving `[101, 102, 1, 101]`, and `S/fs_memory_rooted.sak`'s "one handler value is one store" shares a store across installations because `Fs.memory` closes over a host-side store, not through `var` state. (G12) §4.3 says a literal coerces "where a refined type over its base is expected"; `T/refine.rs::only_literals_of_the_base_type_coerce` has `fn c() -> Option<Percent> { Some(5) }` as `V2001`: the expected type reaches the literal through a `let` annotation, a declared parameter, a field, a return position, a block tail or an arm, and not through the instantiation of a type parameter. (G18) §17.225 (9) promotes ABI.md "by reference as the annex"; its introduction says it "is not itself normative language specification"; STABILITY.md's ABI row lists what it covers (version negotiation, layouts and tags, imports and exports, outcomes, ownership, optional exports) as stable from 0.2.0; `docs/spec/README.md` names grammar and diagnostics only. (G19) §4.2 and §6.2 still called `File` an external type and a capability; §17.89 (1) and §10.2 make it `@resource pub opaque type File = { id: Int, path, mode }` (`std/fs.sak` 21); ABI §8.4's first paragraph describes `id` as the packed `(slot, generation)` and its "as built" paragraphs say the Node and native hosts issue a plain `Int` id and never reuse a slot. (G21) §5.4 and §8.4 promised finalizers on defect and cancellation without exception; ABI §8.6 says a trap cannot run guest finalizers (the host's resource ledger closes handles) and §10 says `D096` runs finalizers from a 64 KiB emergency region and skips the remaining ones when that is exhausted (`R::oom_while_unwinding` asserts the empty cleanup trace); the JS backend has no heap limit of its own (Node's out-of-memory abort ends the process). (G23) §8.6 said the others "are attached as `suppressed` in the outcome"; no `Outcome` type exists in `std/task.sak` or `std/test.sak`, neither runtime has the word, and `sakura_runtime.js` 3273 says the first failure or defect among a scope's children cancels the others and is propagated. (G24) §4.8 and §17.12 promise "valid Sakura Lang expression syntax" and print `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`; `grammar.md` has no such tokens, an uppercase name is a `TypeName` and resolves as a variant, and `S/show_format.sak` prints no non-finite value. (G01) §17.225 (9) requires a `tests/semantics` citation and says "complete at the rc"; §17.245 (6) says the rc ships what is cited and nothing waits; `docs/spec/README.md` admits a Rust test whose input is constructed in the test. Decision: **(G02) The minimum and maximum `Int` are `Int.min_value` and `Int.max_value`**: `std/int.sak` gains `pub let min_value: Int = -9223372036854775807 - 1` and `pub let max_value: Int = 9223372036854775807`, top-level `let` constants under §3's `Const` and §4.5's annotation rule (not `const`, which the grammar does not have; not `@total`, which is for functions); the binary `min(a, b)` and `max(a, b)` are unchanged and keep their `@total`. A constant is Core `FnKind::Const`, evaluated on first use: loading `std/int` never evaluates them, on WASM and native they are the exact values, and on JS reading either is `D003` at that use, as §4.1 says of every `Int` beyond ±(2^53 − 1), never silently wrong and never at load. `V0003`'s message for exactly `9223372036854775808` suggests `Int.min_value` (§17.243 (1) read with this spelling); a pattern cannot name the minimum (there is no negative literal of that magnitude), so a `match` on it uses a guard `n == Int.min_value`. §2.2 and §10.1 are reworded this round; `docs/spec/gaps.md` line 48 and `website/content/docs/stability.mdx` line 52 read `Int.min_value` (Astra, with the G13 commit of §17.260); `agents/typed-holes.mdx` names the binary functions and is right. Evidence: `S/int_min_value.sak` printing `Int.min_value`, `Int.min_value + 1`, `Int.max_value`, `Int.max_value - 1` and `0 - Int.max_value` with `expect-exit@wasm: 0` and `expect-exit@js: 70`, `expect-defect@js: D003` (the first read defects on JS), and `U/V0003_int_literal_out_of_range.sak`'s expectation gaining the suggestion. Opus, in the running session, with §17.243 (1)'s lexer commit. No owner question: an additive std surface before `v0.2.0`, no RFC. **(G01) The evidence rule.** (a) A normative sentence of the static chapter cites a `tests/ui` fixture (its expectation directives, run by `ui.rs`) or a `tests/semantics` fixture; a normative sentence of the dynamic chapter cites a `tests/semantics` fixture (run by `semantics.rs` and `parity.rs` on both shipped backends). (b) A Rust test with constructed input (`sakura_types/tests`, `rt/tests`, `vt.rs`, `heap.rs`), a JS runtime test or a host test is the citation for a sentence of the ABI annex and for a sentence about a state unreachable from checked source (stale ids, reference-count overflow, heap exhaustion, a hostile host, a trap, a failing finalizer); for a language sentence it is supporting evidence named after the fixture, never the only citation. A sentence whose behaviour cannot be observed from source without effects (how many times a pure predicate ran) is an informative implementation note, not a normative sentence. (c) "Complete at the rc" is §17.245 (6)'s scope: every sentence of both chapters is either normative with a citation under (a) or informative with a gap identifier in `gaps.md`, no chapter is missing, `gaps.md` reports the count of each, and nothing waits for a fixture; §17.225 (9) sets the citation rule and §17.245 (6) the scope rule, and they do not conflict. The brief's C rows are candidates for normative status when their cited fixture satisfies (a); P and M rows are informative with the brief's `Axx` identifier until the package lands. `spec_docs.py --check`'s rule (a labelled sentence cites a fixture) is unchanged; the citation names the harness that runs the fixture. **(G03) The count is `V2002 arity_mismatch`**, as built and registered; `V1004` is `name_case_mismatch` and codes are never reused (§17.253). A wrong number of type or row arguments on a type is an arity mismatch; §4.4 is corrected this round and §17.49 is read with `V2002`. No code moves; the spec cites `U/V2002_row_argument_count.sak` and `U/V1007_row_argument_kind.sak`. **(G04) Three statements, each its own sentence.** (1) *Equality*: `==` and `!=` on `Float` are IEEE on every backend: `NaN != NaN`, `-0.0 == 0.0`, structurally inside any container (`Some(NaN) != Some(NaN)`), and `Float.is_nan` is `f != f`. (2) *Order*: the comparison operators on two `Float`s are IEEE (every comparison with a NaN is false; `-0.0` and `0.0` compare equal); the derived `Ord` that `List.sort`, `List.sort_by` and the `Ord` of tuples, records and variants use is a total order in which every NaN is equal to every other NaN and after every other value, and `-0.0` equals `0.0`; so `NaN < NaN` and `NaN > 1.0` are false while `(1.0, 0) < (NaN, 0)` is true and `(NaN, 0) < (1.0, 0)` is false, and `List.sort` places NaNs last. §4.1's row and §4.4's `Ord` row say so this round. (3) *Keys*: `Float` is not `Hash`, nor is any type containing one, so `Map<Float, V>`, `Set<Float>` and a record key with a `Float` field are `V2032`; §4.1's "not `Ord` for `Map` keys" was the wrong constraint and reads `Hash` this round. ABI §2's `Float` row is corrected by erratum (1.4.2, wording): "`Eq` and the comparison operators are IEEE; `cmp` and `Ord` treat all NaNs as one value, last; key equality treats NaNs as one and is unreachable from checked code" (Astra, with the other 1.4.2 errata of §17.260). Evidence (A17): `S/float_special_values.sak` printing the equality, operator and `List.sort` results above on both backends, and `U/V2032_float_map_key.sak`. **(G07) Initializers run once, when the `handler` expression is evaluated; installation copies values.** A state initializer is an operand of the `handler` expression: it runs once, there, its effects belong to the enclosing function's row (not to the handler's `r`), and its value is the handler value's initial state. Each `with` copies the initial values into a fresh instance: two installations of one handler value share no state, a second installation starts again from the initial values, nested installations are distinct instances, and a child task performing the effect reaches the installing instance (§5.5). What a clause closes over (a `Map` built outside the expression, a host store named by a handle) is shared by value semantics or by the host, as any captured value is: `Fs.memory`'s shared store is the host's, not `var` state. §5.5 is reworded this round. Evidence (A21): `S/handler_state_init.sak` with an initializer that prints (`Console` in the enclosing row), installed twice and nested once, showing one print and fresh counters, beside the existing `S/handler_state.sak`. **(G12) The boundary is the expected type's reach.** A scalar literal is checked against a refinement when the refinement is the literal's expected type, and the expected type reaches a literal through a `let` annotation, a declared function's parameter, a record field, a return position, a block's tail and the arms of `if` and `match` in checking mode; it does not reach a literal whose declared parameter type is a type variable of the callee, so a constructor's payload (`Some(5)` against `Option<Percent>`) is synthesized at its base type and is `V2001`, whose message names the introduction (`Some(Percent.from(5))` at a trusted site, or `let p: Percent = 5` before the call). Nested refinements themselves are unaffected (`Option<Percent>` is a fine type; its values come from checked introductions). Pushing the expected instantiation into constructor arguments later accepts more programs and no fewer, so it is an additive 0.x change without an RFC, recorded as §16 item 23. §4.3 says so this round. Evidence (A11): `U/V2001_refined_literal_through_generic.sak` (negative: the constructor case of the Rust test and a generic function's parameter, each pinned as built; if the generic-function form is accepted as built, the sentence names constructors only) and a positive line `let p: Percent = 5; Some(p)` in `S/generic_refinement.sak` or a new `S/refined_literal_positions.sak` covering the six positions. **(G21) The finalizer guarantee and its two bounds.** The language sentence: when a task leaves a `with` body, a `try` body or a resource callback by normal return, `fail`, defect or cancellation, every finalizer registered inside runs, newest first, before the exit is delivered (`R::finalizer_order_*` on the annex side; a source witness under A26, `S/finalizer_exits.sak`, observing a `Fs.with_file` body's close through `Fs.memory` on each of the four exits). The annex states the two bounds, cited from the chapter's sentence: a WASM trap (`D090`, a runtime bug) cannot run guest code, and the host's resource ledger closes every open handle instead (ABI §8.6); heap exhaustion (`D096`) runs finalizers from the emergency region and, when that is exhausted too, ends the task without the remaining finalizers while the ledger closes the handles (ABI §10, `oom_while_unwinding`). A third bound is the process: a signal or `exit` runs the ledger at process exit and no Sakura code. The JS backend has no heap limit of its own; Node's out-of-memory abort is its process bound. §5.4 and §8.4 are reworded this round. No behaviour changes. **(G23) A scope keeps the first failure or defect and drops the rest.** When a child fails or defects, the scope cancels its siblings, joins them, and the scope's outcome is that first failure or defect in completion order (deterministic under `Task.deterministic` and on the single-threaded JS runtime); a sibling that defects while being cancelled replaces a pending failure (a defect is never discarded for a `fail`, ABI §6.4's rule for one task applied across the scope); every other outcome is discarded. No `suppressed` list exists in 0.x; §8.6's parenthetical is withdrawn this round. A later operation or test-outcome field carrying the discarded outcomes is additive and is §16 item 24, written when a program needs it. Evidence (A30): `S/scope_first_failure.sak` (two children failing with different tags under `Task.deterministic(1)`; the first's tag is caught) and `S/defect_D030_scope_sibling_defect.sak` (a failing child and a sibling that defects during cancellation: exit 70 with the defect). If a runtime differs from the sentence on either backend, the fixture pins the sentence and Opus reports the difference before changing the runtime. **(G24) `Show` is expression syntax except the three non-finite floats.** The promise is: the output of `Show` parses as a Sakura Lang expression and, with the prelude and the value's home module in scope, denotes an equal value; the exception is `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity`, the IEEE names every backend prints, which no literal spells (an uppercase name is a `TypeName`). The output is not a literal grammar and not a codec: JSON is the wire format. §4.8 says so this round; no new tokens. Evidence (A19): `S/show_float_special.sak` printing `0.0 / 0.0`, `1.0 / 0.0`, `-1.0 / 0.0` and `-0.0` alone and inside a list. **(G18) The annex is cited by version and section.** `docs/spec/README.md` gains an "ABI annex" paragraph (Astra): the annex is `compiler/runtime/rt/ABI.md` at the version its header names (1.4.0 today, 1.4.2 after this round's errata); a spec sentence cites it as "ABI 1.4.2 §6.4"; the normative annex content is what STABILITY.md's ABI row lists, which the chapters may cite; its implementation profile (§1, §1b, the allocator's classes, the counters of §10) is informative; a Rust or JS test the annex links is a citation under (G01) (b). ABI.md's introduction is amended as 1.4.2 (PATCH; or the same commit as §17.258's 1.4.1 while that erratum is open): "This document is prose, tables and byte layouts; it contains no code. It is the runtime contract STABILITY.md's ABI row names and the specification's annex (design §17.259): the language chapters cite it for runtime-defended states, and it is not itself a source of language semantics." **(G19) `File` is the `@resource` record on every backend.** Source: `File` and `Body` are `@resource` types (`File` the std opaque record of §10.2, `Body` the host's); the capabilities and the other external types are `Dir`, `Scope` and `Fiber<T>`; §4.2 and §6.2 say so this round. Representation: `File.id` is an `Int` the host issues into its own file table on JS, WASM and native, never reused by the Node host, reused with a generation on a host that reuses slots (the native rule of §8.4); ABI §8.4's first paragraph drops "on WASM `id` is the packed `(slot, generation)`" and reads "the host issues `id`; a host that reuses slots packs the generation into it" (1.4.2, Astra). The escape and closing guarantees do not depend on the representation. Why: a constant that defects at load would make the prelude unusable on JS, and a name that clashes with a `@total` std function would retire a published surface for a spelling; `V2002` is what the compiler says and what the registry's one rule allows; three sentences for `Float` say what two backends do, and a total order under `cmp` with IEEE operators is what every host language's standard library does (JS `sort` with a comparator, Rust's `total_cmp`); the handler boundary is what the checker, Core and both runtimes already agree on, and saying it removes the contradiction without a change; the refinement boundary as built is sound and the widening is additive; the finalizer bounds are the ones the annex already states, and a guarantee that names its bounds is a guarantee; a first-failure rule with no list is what both runtimes do and what the tests can observe; the `Show` exception is a fact of IEEE names on every backend; the annex is cited, not copied, so one document says each thing; `File`'s representation is a host detail. Rejected: renaming `min`/`max` to free the short names (a published `@total` surface and §17.8's list for a spelling); an eager `pub let` (the prelude defects on JS); `Int.MIN` (a `TypeName`); making `Int.min_value` backend-dependent (silently wrong); treating `V1004` as a second identity for counts (the registry forbids reuse); making `NaN == NaN` true or `<` total (IEEE is what agents and every host language expect of the operators; the derived order is where totality is needed); a lazy, per-installation initializer (its effects would belong to the clause row and a `with` could perform; Core would need a new node for no program that asked); pushing expected types through constructors now (a checker change during the freeze for a case with a one-line rewrite); an unconditional finalizer promise (`oom_while_unwinding` already contradicts it); implementing `suppressed` for the spec (a feature no program asked for, written to satisfy a parenthetical); `Float.nan`-style spellings in `Show` output (changes every snapshot that prints a NaN for no reader); promoting the whole of ABI.md to language spec (its profile numbers are not semantics). Performance: none; G02 evaluates nothing at load. Changed: §2.2, §4.1, §4.2, §4.3, §4.4, §4.8, §5.4, §5.5, §6.2, §8.3, §8.4, §8.6, §10.1, §16 (items 23 and 24), the §17 heading and preamble this round; ABI.md 1.4.2 errata, `docs/spec/README.md`, `gaps.md` and `stability.mdx` (Astra); `std/int.sak`, the `V0003` message and the fixtures named (Opus). Impact: Opus (G02 now; the fixtures A11, A17, A19, A21, A26, A30 with the chapter commits), Astra (the chapters, the README paragraph, the 1.4.2 errata), the lead (G02's answer to the running session), the owner (none of these change a shipped behaviour; §17.260 (G05) does).
260. **Round 31, the decided amendments the body and the annex never received: `MIN % -1` is `0` and only `MIN / -1` is `D001`; no static affinity, a resource cannot leave its callback and the runtime closes it there; `sakura test` always sets empty grants; one thread per instance on every backend and no cross-thread sends; `Untrusted.check(u, clause, pred)`; four `Trust` sinks including `Secret.map`; the grammar's numeric prose follows the lexer commit; nested `Option` does not survive JSON and the niche gate never asked it to; a `fail` inside a finalizer is `D093` on both backends (research/14 G05, G06, G08–G11, G13, G20, G22; §17.68, §17.70, §17.98, §17.99, §17.123, §17.159, §17.171, §17.243; round 31).** Facts: (G05) ABI §2 says `MIN / -1` and `MIN % -1` are `D001` and `func.rs` emits one `a == MIN && b == -1` check for `IntDiv | IntRem`; §17.98 (later) endorsed research/09 §6's `trem` with `MIN % -1 = 0` defined for the verifier, so today a remainder the verifier proves defined can defect at run time on WASM and native, which §17.225 (4) (c) calls a verifier soundness bug; `i64.rem_s` itself returns `0` for that pair, JS never reaches `MIN` (`D003` first), Go, Java, C# and WASM define it as `0`, Rust panics because its remainder shares the division's overflow check. (G06) §1.2 said "a resource is released exactly once", §4.2 "resources are additionally affine" and §8.4 "affine (use at most once as a whole…)"; §17.70 says affinity is not checked in v0 and the runtime closes the file at the callback boundary; §17.123 reaffirms; a `File` cannot leave its callback (`V6003`), cannot be assigned to handler state (`V6003`) and cannot be captured by a `Task.spawn` body that outlives it (`V6002`), so a use after the body returned is unreachable from checked source and the runtime's close is defence in depth. (G08) §6.2 said `sakura test` never sets `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`; §17.159 (3) made it always set, with empty `fs`, `net` and `env` grants unless `--record`; `S/fs_memory_rooted.sak`'s header says the opposite. (G09) §5.5 said native uses a per-instance lock and §8.6 that values crossing worker threads are promoted; §17.171 keeps one instance on one thread and defers promotion (§16 item 22). (G10) §6.4 wrote `Untrusted.check(u, pred)`; §17.68 and `std/untrusted.sak` 22 have `check(u, clause: String, pred)`. (G11) §6.4's first bullet gives `Secret.map` its reason; its last bullet and §2.5 listed three sinks; §17.159 (2) made `map` the fourth. (G13) `grammar.md` G09 describes separators without the rule, G10 and its informative paragraph still describe the lax lexer and call the minimum open; §17.243 (1)–(2) decided both; Opus's lexer commit is in flight (handoff item 7). (G20) §17.83 asked for nested `Some(None)` to survive JSON; §17.99 and §16 item 21 withdrew it; §17.199 (1) deferred the niche; ABI §4.3's last sentence still calls round-tripping "a precondition of enabling the niche by default"; `S/nested_options_json.sak` prints both `None` and `Some(None)` as `null`. (G22) ABI §6.4 ends "today JS lets it escape"; `R::fail_escaping_a_finalizer_is_d093` pins the Rust runtime; `sakura_runtime.js`'s `runFins` calls each finalizer and discards what it returns, so a `fail` inside one unwinds the finalizer's own inner finalizers and its continuation is dropped: neither `D093` nor an escape, a lost failure; no std finalizer fails today and user code registers none, so the state is unreachable from source. Decision: **(G05) `MIN / -1` is `D001`; `MIN % -1` is `0`.** The quotient is not representable and the remainder is; truncated remainder is defined for every nonzero divisor, as the verifier's `trem` already says. The WASM lowering drops the `MIN` test from `IntRem` (`func.rs`), the LIR evaluator and the Rust runtime's interpreter follow, the native backend with them, the JS runtime's `rem` is unchanged (`MIN` is `D003` there before any operator), ABI §2's `Int` row reads "`D001` on overflow, `D002` on a zero divisor; `MIN / -1` is `D001` and `MIN % -1` is `0`" (1.4.2), and §4.1 says so this round. A `verify` obligation for `%` has no definedness term beyond the divisor. A behaviour change on WASM and native (a defect becomes `0`), before `v0.2.0`, CHANGELOG line, no RFC (no stable contract exists; RFC 0001 starts at 0.2.0); **owner**: confirm as a numeric-semantics line at the 0.2.0 window (named maintainer review per AGENTS.md; the designer recommends it). Evidence (A18): `S/defect_D001_int_min_div.sak` (`expect-defect: D001`, `expect-defect@js: D003`) and `S/int_min_rem.sak` printing `0` on WASM (`expect-exit@js: 70`, `expect-defect@js: D003`). **(G06) The stronger wording retires.** §1.2 reads "a resource cannot leave the callback that introduced it and is closed when that callback exits"; §4.2 "resources are additionally bound to the callback that introduced them"; §8.4 drops "affine (use at most once as a whole, …)" for the escape rule (used inside the callback that introduced it, never in its result, in handler state or in a task body that outlives it; a static affine check is not part of v0; a late use is unreachable from checked source, so the runtime's close at the boundary is defence in depth, not a language rule). The spec's sentences cite `U/V6003_resource_escape.sak`, `U/V6003_route_handler_returns_file.sak` and `S/std_fs_with_file.sak` (repeated use inside the body is ordinary). **(G08) `sakura test` always sets `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`** with empty `fs`, `net` and `env` grants, so a test that installs `Fs.host()`, `Env.host()` or `Http.host()` fails closed; `--record`'s grants are §10.2's; `Test.fixtures()` keeps its own. §6.2 is reworded this round; `S/fs_memory_rooted.sak`'s header comment reads "`sakura test` sets empty grants (§17.159 (3)); a memory directory needs none" (Opus, with any commit touching the file). Evidence: CLI `test_host_handlers_fail_closed_without_record`. **(G09) One thread per instance everywhere.** §5.5's clause reads "clause execution is serial by construction: every backend runs one Sakura instance on one thread (§17.171)"; §8.6's promotion sentence reads "no value crosses threads in 0.x (§17.171 (5), §16 item 22)"; both this round. **(G10) `Untrusted.check(u, clause, pred) -> Result<T, Violation>`**, the clause a `String` the `Violation` carries; §6.4 this round; the spec cites `S/std_untrusted.sak`. **(G11) Four sinks**: `Untrusted.trust`, `Secret.expose`, `Secret.map` and `Html.raw`; §2.5 and §6.4 this round. Evidence (A14): a CLI `audit` assertion listing a `Secret.map` site with its reason beside an `expose` site (Opus; `S/secret_map_defect.sak` stays the leak witness). **(G13) The grammar follows the lexer commit.** After §17.243 (1)–(2) land, Astra rewrites G09 to the separator rule, G10 to "an integer token is in `[0, 2^63 − 1]`; `9223372036854775808` is `V0003` with `Int.min_value` suggested", replaces the informative paragraph with the decided cases (the flipped `numeric_boundaries` snapshot, `U/V0003_int_literal_out_of_range.sak`, the `V0006` fixtures) and closes the two items of `gaps.md` "Lexical boundaries", with the `Int.min_value` spelling and `stability.mdx` line 52; one commit, Opus's or the next. **(G20) No round trip.** The spec's sentence: "`None` and `Some(None)` both encode as `null`; `null` decodes as the outermost `None` of its `Option` type" (normative, `S/nested_options_json.sak`); ABI §4.3's last sentence reads "JSON wire format is unchanged by layout (`None` is `null`, `Some(x)` is `x`); nested `Option` does not round-trip through JSON on any backend (design §17.99, §16 item 21), and the niche gate asks for identical bytes between layouts and backends, not a format change" (1.4.2). **(G22) `D093` on both backends.** ABI §6.4's last sentence reads "a `Fail` inside a finalizer is the defect `D093 finalizer_failed` on every backend; the remaining finalizers run; `rt/tests/exec.rs::fail_escaping_a_finalizer_is_d093` and the JS runtime test pin it" (1.4.2); the JS runtime gains the behaviour and the test (Opus, small: `runFins` turns a `fail` that reaches the finalizer's boundary into `defect("D093", …)` and continues with the next finalizer); no source fixture exists because no source program can fail inside a finalizer, so the chapter's sentence cites the annex under §17.259 (G01) (b). Why: a verifier and a runtime that disagree on one operand pair are a soundness bug, and the defined answer is the one every standard but Rust's gives; the affine wording promised a check that was never built while the escape rules already make the promise's cases unreachable, so the honest sentence is the escape rule; the test-grant and threading sentences are two-line stale facts; the `check` signature and the sink list are what std ships; the grammar's informative paragraph must not outlive the lexer it describes; a wire format that loses a level is a fact the spec states, not a gate; a lost failure is the one outcome ABI §6.4 does not allow. Rejected: `MIN % -1` as `D001` with the verifier's `trem` made partial (the verifier would lose proofs over `%` for a case no program wants to defect on); keeping "affine" as aspiration with a footnote (the spec would cite nothing); a second `V` code for a late resource use (unreachable); keeping ABI's "today JS lets it escape" until a fixture exists (the sentence is already wrong: the failure is lost, not escaped). Performance: (G05) removes one compare from every WASM and native remainder; none otherwise. Changed: §1.2, §2.5, §4.1, §4.2, §5.5, §6.2, §6.4, §8.4, §8.6 this round; ABI.md 1.4.2 (the introduction, §2, §4.3, §6.4, §8.4; Astra, one commit, or §17.258's 1.4.1 commit while it is open); `grammar.md`, `gaps.md`, `stability.mdx` (Astra, after the lexer commit); CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` (Opus, with G05's commit). Impact: Opus (G05's lowering sites, interpreter and fixtures; G22's runtime and test; G08's comment; A14), Astra (the errata and grammar commits), the owner (G05's confirmation).
261. **Round 31, the evidence the chapters need before promotion: `V0015`, the `process` key, the pre-instantiation version read and the test-exit relay are Opus's in-flight items and cite nothing until they land; a fixture's milestone is the lowest at which it passes on both shipped backends, so the three M5 fixtures are re-tried now; a fixture is named for what it asserts; `NodeId` is a slot (research/14 G14–G17, G25, G26, A20; §17.243 (3)–(5), §17.253 (1), (3), §17.256; round 31).** Facts: `codes.txt` has no `V0015` and `invalid_utf8_source_is_a_usage_error` still asserts exit 2; `manifest.rs` deserializes `permissions.process` without validation and STABILITY.md says "planned"; `sakura_wasm_host.js`'s `instantiate` runs `readDebug` before `fresh()` but compares the version read from the exported global after instantiation, so a module of another MAJOR whose imports differ still fails with a `LinkError` first (§17.199 (4) and §17.243 (4) remain open, as the handoff's item 7 lists); `main.rs` maps a runner status other than 0 or 3 to "the test runner crashed" and exit 70, so §17.243 (5) is open; `common/mod.rs` sets `UI_MILESTONE` and `SEMANTICS_MILESTONE` to 3, `S/json_codec.sak`, `S/host_fs_env.sak` and `S/sql_cancel_committed.sak` carry `milestone: M5`, `corpus.rs` skips `json_codec` for a bare module and `m3.rs` carries its own copy of the program; `S/literal_refinement_passes_once.sak` observes equal output, not a count, and `S/row_widening.sak` instantiates a row-polymorphic callback twice, which is not §5.2 rule 4; `std/graph.sak` says "a `NodeId` is a slot without a generation; add the generation together with `remove`" while §8.3 said "slot + generation". Decision: **(G14–G17) Nothing is cited before it lands**, and each item's evidence is: (G14) `U/V0015_source_not_utf8/` (a directory fixture, one Latin-1 byte, `expect: V0015`) and the CLI test renamed to what it then pins (exit 1, the code in `--json`); (G15) `U/V8006_permissions_process_nonempty/` and a positive `permissions_process_empty/` manifest fixture (no diagnostic), with the generated table's row; (G16) the `wasm_host.test.js` case of §17.199 (4) (a module stamped another MAJOR that imports a function the host lacks reports `V8003` before any `LinkError`, stripped and unstripped), cited from the annex; (G17) `cli.rs` cases driving `sakura test --target wasm` through a runner returning 0, 2, 3 and 70 (a stale module for 2, a defect fixture for 70) and asserting the relayed status, cited by the dynamic chapter's test-runner sentence. Until each lands its sentence is informative with the brief's gap id. **(G25) A fixture's milestone is the lowest at which it passes on both shipped backends.** Opus runs the three under `semantics.rs` and `parity.rs` with the ceiling lifted locally: `json_codec.sak` (the JS codec's text on every backend) and `host_fs_env.sak` (`Fs.memory` and an unset `Env` variable) are expected to pass and become `M3`; `sql_cancel_committed.sak` becomes `M3` if its stdout is the same on JS (where the statement runs to its end first, as its header says) and WASM, else stays `M5` with the reason in its header; a fixture that fails is a REQUESTS item, never silently lowered. The harness ceilings stay 3; the chapters cite only fixtures at or under the ceiling, and `gaps.md` lists the ones above it. **(G26) A fixture is named for what it asserts.** `S/literal_refinement_passes_once.sak` is renamed `literal_refinement_undecided_passes.sak` with its comment reading "an undecided literal that satisfies its `where` is the refined value; the start-up check is one `from` call in Core (`T/refine.rs`'s conversion count, `cli.rs`'s `--dump core`)"; the chapter's normative sentences are the `D010`-before-`main` one (`S/literal_refinement_checked_at_startup.sak`) and the refined-value one (the renamed fixture), and "once at module initialisation" is an informative implementation note under §17.259 (G01) (b). `S/row_widening.sak` keeps its name (a row-polymorphic instantiation is a widening of a kind) and §5.2 rule 4's sentence cites A06's new pair, `S/closed_row_widening.sak` (`let f: fn() -> Int ! {Clock, Console} = seven`, accepted and called) and `U/V3002_closed_row_not_subset.sak` (the reverse rejected). **(A20) `NodeId` is a slot**: §8.3 reads "a slot today; a generation joins it with `Graph.remove`, which v0 does not have"; the chapter's sentence is "`Graph.get(g, id)` returns the node at `id`'s slot in `g`, `None` if the slot is empty", normative with `S/graph_basics.sak` (insert, connect, get, and `None` for an id never issued by that graph), and no cross-graph rejection is claimed. Why: a chapter that cites an in-flight commit cites nothing; a milestone label that keeps a passing fixture out of the harness is a gap the harness hides; a fixture named above its assertion is the one way a citation lies; `Graph` is what std ships. Rejected: lifting the ceiling to 5 wholesale (the native fixture would fail on the shipped backends); writing "exactly once" as normative from the Rust count (an implementation note is what it is); inventing a generation in the spec that std does not have. Impact: Opus (item 7's evidence as listed, the three M5 re-tries, the rename, A06, `S/graph_basics.sak`), Astra (the chapters' gap ids, `gaps.md`), Sol (nothing).
262. **Every web platform API on Bun's page is delivered in Sakura's shape, not JavaScript's: one typed std module per group, `Result`/`Fail<E>` for every expected failure, explicit effects with `net` the only permission touched, bounded resources, one deterministic handler per effect; the record-breaking changes land in 0.2.0 or not at all, the additive modules land before the rc, workers are experimental; a backend without a service refuses at startup; the redirect gap is fixed first (owner request 2026-10-19; research/15; RFC 0002; `docs/plans/web-apis.md`; round 34).** Facts: the owner asked that all of [Bun's Web APIs](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/web-apis) be included; Astra's `research/15-web-apis.md` inventories 49 named entries, 9 related APIs (`File`, `FormData`, `URLPattern`, the encoder/decoder and compression streams, `CustomEvent`, `DOMException`) and 8 stream reader/writer/controller classes, and its coverage claims were read against `compiler/std/INDEX.md` and `sakura_runtime.js` at `7b4f55b5`: Sakura has `Http.send/stream`, text-only `Request`/`Response` records with `List<(String, String)>` headers and six `Method` variants, a `Url` refinement whose `is_valid` checks a scheme prefix and the absence of spaces, `String.to_bytes`/`from_bytes` (strict UTF-8 only), `Bytes.len/get/from_list`, typed `Json`, `Random.bytes/uuid`, `Clock` in whole milliseconds, `Console.print/read_line`, `Log.event`, `Task.scope/spawn/join/all/race/yield_now` and `timeout`; no Base64 in std (the JS runtime has a private `base64`/`unbase64` pair for the cassette codec), no general decoder, no `Headers`, `Blob`, `Form`, stream, compression, crypto, socket, channel or worker type; `compiler/std/crypto.sak` does not exist although §6.4 mentions `Crypto.hmac`; the JS host's `fetchArgs` checks the initial URL's `host:port` against `net` and then calls `fetch` with its default `redirect: "follow"`, so a granted host can redirect the program to an ungranted one (the WASM host forwards to the same code; native has no `Http`); §8.6 has no channel type and no detached work, §16 items 13 and 22 defer bounded channels and cross-thread sends, §17.171 (5) keeps one instance on one thread; §17.206 (4) held `Bytes.concat` for a second caller; §17.253 (3) reserves `process`; RFC 0001 starts within-minor compatibility at 0.2.0 and the roadmap goes from 0.2.0 to `1.0.0-rc.1` with "no contract change" through the soak, so 0.2.0 is the one breaking window left before 1.0; `v0.1.0` is not tagged and its window is running. Decision: **(1) Capability parity, not object compatibility.** Each of the 66 entries maps to a Sakura form in RFC 0002 §1; the form is a value with typed errors, or a scoped resource under an effect; no JS interop layer, no `Async`, no event listeners (every web event is a value returned by a receive operation), no `structuredClone` (values copy; the `Schema` codec is the wire), no `ShadowRealm` (no dynamic code; isolation is a worker with `Grants.none()`), no `EventTarget` (a list of callbacks is the idiom), no mutable typed array or BYOB buffer (no caller-owned memory), no object URLs (no document). Each gap is a documented row naming the Sakura form and the reason. **(2) Modules.** `std/bytes` grows (`slice`, `concat`, Base64 strict and lenient); new `std/encoding` (`Utf8 | Utf16Le | Utf16Be | Windows1252`, `Fatal | Replace`, immutable `Decoder` state), `std/searchparams`, `std/headers` (a validated view; the record fields stay lists), `std/blob` (`Blob`, `FileData`), `std/form` (multipart with an explicit boundary and required limits), `std/stream` (`Source<T, e>`/`Sink<T, e>` as records of closures, pull-based, every buffer bounded by an argument), `std/compress` (gzip, deflate, deflate-raw, `max_out` required), `std/crypto` (tier 1 on every backend: SHA-2, HMAC, AES-GCM, HKDF, PBKDF2, ECDSA/ECDH P-256, Ed25519, X25519; tier 2 RSA/P-384/P-521/AES-CBC/CTR/KW on JS only with a typed `Unsupported` elsewhere; `CryptoKey` an opaque value over `Secret<Bytes>`; `Random` is the entropy authority and no `Crypto` effect exists), `std/websocket` (effect `WebSocket`, client only, `net` with `ws` 80 and `wss` 443, `scripted` peer), `std/urlpattern` (`:name`, `*`, `**`; regexp groups a typed error; `Router` matches through it), `std/channel` (bounded, in-instance, `Task`), `std/worker` (experimental: a second instance per `@worker` entry, `Schema` messages, grants a subset of the parent's, 16 live workers, `inline()` test handler, in-process topics for `BroadcastChannel`). `Url` stays the refinement; `UrlParts` is the WHATWG-parsed record, non-ASCII hosts a typed `Idna` error until punycode lands. **(3) 0.2.0 changes, once.** `Request.body` and `Response.body` become `Payload = Empty | Text(String) | Bytes(Bytes)`; `Method` gains `Options` and `Trace`; `Request.redirect: Follow | Manual | Error`; `Clock` gains `monotonic_micros`; `Task` gains `cancel(f)` (consumes the fiber; a later `join` is `D095`) and `cancelled(s)`; `std/task.every` (serialized ticks, skipped ticks counted); `Console.alert/confirm/prompt`; `Json.render`. These are on `main` before the 0.2.0 preparation commit or they wait for the owner; nothing breaking lands after that tag. Everything after 0.2.0 is additive and enters the inventory as stable at 1.0.0; `std/worker` is experimental and off the 1.0 contract (owner question 1 of the RFC). **(4) The redirect fix is phase 0** and lands in whichever release is next: at most 20 hops, each hop's `host:port` checked against `net` (and `Http.scoped`'s list) before it is fetched, `authorization` and `secret_headers` dropped on a cross-origin hop, a refused hop the ordinary `HttpError`. **(5) A backend without a declared effect's service refuses at startup, exit 75, naming the effect and the target**, as the empty-`net` rule does; this replaces native's `D091` at first use for `Http`, `Serve` and `Llm` and applies to `WebSocket`. Pure modules run everywhere because std is Sakura and their externals live in the JS runtime and in `runtime/rt`, shared by WASM and native; crypto on WASM is a `hosted` import in 0.2.0 (a non-JS embedder gets a link-time refusal, never a fallback). **(6) Limits are arguments**, never defaults that hide: decompression output, multipart parts and bytes, stream buffers and tee lag, channel capacity; WebSocket messages 16 MiB and 64 queued; workers 16; redirects 20; patterns 4 KiB and 64 groups. **(7) Determinism**: identical bytes on every backend except compressed output and randomized ECDSA/PSS signatures, which no fixture prints; every effect has a scripted or captured handler. Why: the owner wants the whole surface, and the surface is useful only if an agent can call it under the manifest, test it offline and trust the same answer on every target; copying JS semantics would import aliasing, exceptions and event loops that §1, §5 and §8 reject; one breaking window is what RFC 0001 leaves, so the record changes go there and the rest stays additive; startup refusal is the existing exit-75 contract extended, and it is what an agent can act on (`D091` at first use is discovered in production). Rejected: a JS interop layer (not portable, aliasable); one `Web` effect (hides authority); web stream locks and controllers (unneeded with values and one thread); shared-memory workers (§8.1); a `Crypto` effect (nothing to authorize; entropy is `Random`); SHA-1/MD5 (not offered); tightening `Url.is_valid` (breaks `url"…"` programs for no capability); adding operations to `Console`/`Clock`/`Task` after 0.2.0 (breaks user handlers inside the contract). Performance: pure modules in Sakura cost what the corpus already measures; hot codecs are externals in both runtimes, so Base64, UTF-16, hashing and DEFLATE run at host or Rust speed; `Bytes.concat` is linear; no combinator allocates without a bound; the §17.153 window policy applies to any number a phase wants to quote. Changed: RFC 0002 (new), `docs/plans/web-apis.md` (new), `research/15-web-apis.md` (landed), `research/README.md`; §6.2, §8.4, §8.6, §10.2–10.4, §16 items 13 and 22 receive their sentences as each phase lands (plan phase 12). Impact: Opus (phases 0–11, one session each, the order in the plan), Sol (vector tables, inventory rows, index and llms lines, gap sentences), Astra (the 0.2.0 migration list gains the `Payload` and `Method` items), owner (accept RFC 0002 after FCP; answer its two questions: workers off the 1.0 gate, tier-2 crypto on native not before 1.0; both recommended "yes").
263. **Phase 1 stays on `main` and ships in 0.1.0; while the tag is pending, additive phases land on `main` as they are ready and the breaking phases 4a/4b are held as PR branches until the tag; `Encoding.encode` keeps its `requires encodable(enc)`; phase 4a moves redirect following out of the host into `std/http`, so `host()` and `scoped()` share one loop and `scoped`'s list is checked per hop; one `encoding_decode` external with the `Decoder` state in Sakura is endorsed (round 35, 2026-10-20, after phases 0 and 1 `7dd9dd47`..`d0222605` landed).** Facts: RFC 0002 §Compatibility said only phase 0 may land before the `v0.1.0` tag; the phase 1 brief said additive std APIs were fine, and `d0222605` (`Bytes.slice/concat`, Base64, `std/encoding`) plus the bug fix `321b983e` are on `main` with no existing signature, ABI, JSON or diagnostic contract changed; phase 4b (effect additions, an ABI MINOR bump) is in progress in a worktree; `v0.1.0` is not tagged, the owner dropped the wall-clock quiet window on 2026-10-19 and the gate is now an instruction-count baseline (`7137b0a3`, `320c9980`) that the owner blesses, measured on the exit commit `dee11301` in a clean worktree (release.md §2: "the commit the gate signs, never `main`'s head"), with instructions per call taken as the difference between one call and 1 + k calls, so process startup, and with it the size of `sakura_runtime.js` and of std, is subtracted; the tag is cut from `main` after the preparation commit (release.md §3, §5); RFC 0001 starts within-minor compatibility at 0.2.0, so 0.1.0 carries no promise an added module could break; §17.257 already held one branch (the JSON kind split, PR #4) for the tag; `Encoding.encode(s, enc)` is declared `requires encodable(enc)` where `encodable` is false only for `Windows1252`, so the trap depends on the encoding argument alone, never on the string; the Encoding Standard's `TextEncoder` encodes UTF-8 only and its legacy encoders exist for form submission; `Http.scoped(hosts)` is a Sakura handler that checks a request's URL against its list and forwards to the inner handler, so the hops the JS host follows inside one `http_send` are checked against `net` (`7dd9dd47`) but not against the list, which the host cannot see; `Http.scripted` cannot script a redirect today, so phase 0's evidence is runtime tests; phase 1 built `Decoder.push/finish` in Sakura over one `encoding_decode` external, with `unfinished(b, enc)` holding back a UTF-8 lead byte short of its continuations, an odd UTF-16 byte and a trailing high surrogate, and nothing for Windows-1252, where the plan named `encoding_decoder_push` and `encoding_decoder_finish` externals. Decision: **(1) `d0222605` and `321b983e` stay and ship in 0.1.0.** RFC 0002's "only phase 0 before the tag" sentence is withdrawn; it protected a wall-clock baseline on a head-adjacent commit that no longer exists. **(2) The rule while the tag is pending.** An additive phase (2, 3, 7a, R; later 5, 6, 7b, 8, 9, 10 if the tag is still pending when they are ready, which it should not be) lands on `main` when its gates are green, with its `[Unreleased]` → Added line; the preparation commit's changelog puts whatever is on `main` into 0.1.0's section, and the inventory lists the new modules with the rest of std (the 0.2.0 contract covers them from 0.2.0, as it covers everything). A breaking phase (4a, 4b, and any ABI version bump) does not touch `main` before the tag: it is rebased daily and held as a PR branch, as PR #4 is, and merged in queue order right after the tag (4b first, its "after" being phase 0; 4a when phase 3 is on `main`). Agents are never idle on this account: 2, 3, 7a and R are open now. Nothing in RFC 0002 delays the tag; the tag's one remaining input is the owner's bless of the counted baseline, after which Opus makes the preparation commit from `main`'s head and the owner tags it (release.md §5; changed source bytes invalidate only the candidate approval, not the baseline, which names `dee11301`). **(3) `encode` keeps `requires encodable(enc)` (D020).** Confirmed: the precondition is a property of the program, not of its input, so the §7.4 classification makes it a caller defect; a `Result` would force every UTF-8 and UTF-16 caller to unwrap a failure that cannot happen, and the web offers no Windows-1252 encoder either. Windows-1252 is decode-only; `encodable` is `pub` so a caller with a runtime-chosen encoding tests it first; the doc comment says so (it does). **(4) Phase 4a moves redirect following into `std/http`.** Every `Http.host()` and `Http.scoped()` send reaches the host with `redirect: "manual"`; one Sakura function follows hops for both: at most 20, `Location` resolved against the request URL with phase 2's parser, the hop's `host:port` checked against `scoped`'s list when there is one (the host checks `net` on each send, since each hop is its own `http_send`), `authorization` and `secret_headers` dropped when scheme, host or port change, `Request.redirect = Manual` returning the 3xx and `Error` failing `HttpError`; `Http.stream` closes a 3xx body and reopens. The host's hop loop from `7dd9dd47` is deleted in the same commit: one implementation, not two policies. Consequences: the policy is identical on every backend and native inherits it when it gains `Http`; hops appear in the effect trace; `Http.scripted` can script a 3xx, so the phase-0 cases that were runtime tests become semantics fixtures (`http_redirect_follows.sak`, `http_redirect_drops_secrets_cross_origin.sak`, `http_redirect_scoped_rejects_hop.sak`, `http_redirect_21_hops.sak`); the `net` refusal per send keeps its runtime test; `Http.recording` records each hop as an exchange, and a 0.1.0 cassette (final exchange only) still replays, because the replayed request meets no 3xx. Phase 4a's acceptance gains these fixtures and the owner's review as security reviewer, since it relocates an approved security fix. Rejected: `scoped` alone following manually while the host keeps its loop (two loops, two places to forget the header drop); passing the scoped list to the host as a hidden request field (an ABI shape for one caller). **(5) One `encoding_decode` external, endorsed.** The `Decoder` is an immutable Sakura record and `unfinished` is correct for the three families (lead-byte lengths for UTF-8, odd byte and trailing high surrogate for UTF-16, nothing for Windows-1252); the plan's two stateful externals are struck. Why: a release gate that measures a fixed commit does not need a frozen `main`; holding additive work in worktrees costs agent time and rebases for no protection, while a breaking record change on `main` would put half of 0.2.0's migration into an alpha whose fixtures and corpus are being blessed; `requires` is for facts about the program, `Result` for facts about the data; one hop loop in Sakura is smaller, portable and testable, which is what §1 and §5 ask of every std behaviour. Performance: none measured; the std loop costs one `http_send` per hop, as the host loop did. Changed: RFC 0002 §2.1, §2.4 (`Follow`), §Compatibility, status lines, §Unresolved (owner's answers of 2026-10-20 recorded); `docs/plans/web-apis.md` §1, §2, phase 0, phase 1, phase 4a, §4. Impact: Opus (phases 2, 3, 7a, R proceed on `main`; 4a and 4b held as PR branches; 4a's scope grows by the std loop and the host loop's removal), owner (bless the counted baseline; review 4a as security reviewer), Sol (none new).

264. **The quiet window is dropped. A baseline is a blessed instruction-count run from the reference Mac, measured while other work runs; instructions retired per call are the primary metric and wall time is information (the owner's decision, stated directly by the owner, Aniruddh Dubge, on 2026-10-19; supersedes the quiet-window parts of §17.153, §17.228 (2), §17.238 (4), §17.250 (1) and §17.252, and `docs/release.md` §2; no round).** Facts: the window needed the owner's MacBook idle for about 4–4.5 hours (§17.252): agents paused, a one-minute load under 3.0 in every 15 s snapshot and no build, benchmark or agent executable at 10% CPU (`BUSY_EXECUTABLE`); the owner's attempts failed on load, and agents work on that machine most hours; macOS's `/usr/bin/time -l` prints the instructions retired, cycles and peak RSS of the one process it runs, all its threads (verified by the owner on the reference Mac, host `d88970189598`); rustc-perf (perf.rust-lang.org) reads instructions as its primary metric because they barely move with background load; on this Mac `node -e 1` retires 1.33 G instructions with a 0.8% range across six processes, and in the counting harness's first runs (`fib`, under agent load) a cell's five per-call values spread 0.3% or less on Node, Wasmtime and native, while one Bun cell in two was bimodal (one process in five 3% lower, the others within 0.01%); a Wasmtime `fib` cell's instruction ratio over hand JS and its wall-time ratio differed by half; the full counted run at `320c9980` (all four suites in about an hour with agents working; `bench/results/2026-10-19-320c9980-*`) spread a median 0.09–0.30% on Node, Wasmtime and native cells and 1.35% on Bun, and its envelope on counts reads `miss` on 241 of 264 gating cells (met 19, absent 4), the wall times of the same processes pointing the same way; the harness's `measure` warms up for a fixed time, so counting its process would count a load-dependent number of calls; the exit commit `dee11301` predates the counting harness (`7137b0a3`; Node under `--predictable` from `320c9980`), and `main` after it carries WS-P13b, row 31's dispatch fix, batched trace writes and the coverage-matrix index. Decision: (1) **The gate is a blessed instruction-count baseline from the reference Mac**: `bench/bench run --instructions` of the `js` and `wasm` suites, blessed by the owner, with `native --lane matched` and `compile --instructions` as evidence, all four at one commit in one clean worktree; no idle machine, no paused agents, no load gate. The reference machine stays (§17.252 (1)); a counted run elsewhere is direction only. (2) **The metric**: per cell, k calls beyond one, k a power of two calibrated on the counter until the extra calls retire 2^32 instructions (at most 65,536); five pairs of fresh processes, one call and 1 + k calls, in the shuffled order of a timed run; a pair's value is its many-call count less the median one-call count, over k, so start-up, loading and the first call's compilation cancel; Node runs under V8's `--predictable` (its GC and compiler threads otherwise retire a scheduling-dependent count: hand-JS `shapes` at 100,000 counted 0.46–1.16 G per call by default and 0.455–0.460 G single-threaded) and Bun under its defaults; the cell is the median with the spread (max − min) / median; wall time per call from the same processes stays beside it as information. `bless` takes a counted run whatever its `meta.host.quiet` and still refuses a failed oracle or a dirty `compiler/` or `bench/` tree. (3) **The commit**: a counted baseline measures the commit it was run at, which must contain the harness; the first is `320c9980`, so the M4 baseline includes the post-exit commits named above, and the gate signature still names `dee11301` as the exit commit. §17.263 reads the baseline as measured on `dee11301` from `docs/release.md` §2's old wording; it is measured at `320c9980`, which precedes phase 1 (`7dd9dd47`..`d0222605`), so that entry's point, that phase 1 is outside the baseline, holds. Whether this baseline closes item 11 for M4, or the owner wants a counted run of the exit commit (a commit of `dee11301` with the harness, which `main` does not have), is the owner's call. (4) **Reading**: `compare` and `envelope` read instructions when every file they read is counted, and are then never advisory; §17.109's ceilings keep their numbers and are read against instruction ratios, and the report says it read counts. A ceiling set on time and read on counts is a different measurement, so the design lead may re-derive the ceilings on counts before `v0.2.0`; until then a miss on counts is carried under a named decision as a miss on time was. (5) **What may be published**: instruction counts are deterministic counters (§17.251, §17.253) and may be quoted as instructions retired per call on the reference Mac at commit C, marked "pending owner bless" until the baseline file is on `main`; a wall time or time ratio from a counted run is not quoted as a claim. (6) Linux CI keeps timing (it has no such counter); its pull-request `compare` against a counted baseline reads that file's `median_ms` and is advisory when the base was loaded. Why: a gate the owner cannot run is no gate; the window tried to make wall time repeatable on one host, and instruction counts are repeatable on that host under load; the cost is that a count is not a time (cache misses, branch mispredictions and IPC are invisible to it), which is why wall time stays beside it and the ceilings are flagged. Rejected: a looser load threshold (still fragile and still noise); a cloud or VM host (§17.252 (1)); `proc_pid_rusage` through `ctypes` (the same counter with more code, and `time -l` is the one the owner verified); counting the timed `measure` process (its warm-up is clocked). Performance: none; this changes how speed is measured, not the compiler. Changed: `bench/harness/bench.py` and `bench/README.md` (`7137b0a3`, `320c9980`; their messages cite §17.262 and §17.263, numbers that went to rounds 34 and 35 meanwhile, and both mean this entry), `docs/release.md` §2, `docs/plans/m4-exit-checklist.md` item 11, the website's benchmarks page. Impact: the owner (bless the two counted runs; item 11's commit question), Astra (the gate report reads the counted files), the design lead (the ceilings on counts).
265. **The envelope is information for 0.1.0 and the tag's gate is the blessed baseline; §17.109's cross-engine ceilings keep their unit, time, and are read in a wall-time lane beside the count lane, while the same-engine targets (Sakura against hand JavaScript on the same engine) are read on counts and are the operative speed targets; `320c9980` is the baseline commit, ratified; Bun is advisory in a counted `compare`; the performance push after the bless is WS-P14–WS-P18 on the JS backend, then WS-W5–WS-W7 on WASM, in a lane beside the web-APIs phases (round 36, 2026-10-20, on Opus's report of the counted runs at `320c9980`).** Facts: `bench/results/2026-10-19-320c9980-envelope.md` reads `miss` on 241 of 264 gating cells, `met` 19, `absent` 4 (`json_validate` has no Wasmtime cell); by count, Sakura WASM on Node is a geometric mean 27× Rust matched, 25× Go, 11× OCaml and 12× Koka, Wasmtime 29× Rust, the worst `sieve` at 203–315× and `nbody` at 131–163× Rust, the best `tokenizer` on Node at its two largest sizes, 2.97× and 2.83× (`met`); the wall times of the same processes point the same way (`sieve` at n = 200,000: hand JS 1.13 ms, WASM on Node 36.5 ms, Wasmtime 59.1 ms), so the gap is real, but a count ratio is not a time ratio: §17.264 recorded a Wasmtime `fib` cell whose instruction ratio and time ratio differed by half, matched Rust keeps LLVM's autovectorisation and retires fewer instructions per unit of work, and a JIT, a bounds-checked sandbox or an RC runtime retires more at a different IPC; §17.109 set every ceiling on wall-time medians from research/10 and called them gates for *claiming* competitiveness, not promises; §17.152 (2) and §17.228 (2) carry a miss under a named decision; §17.225 made 1.0's evidence in-repo. Same-engine readings on counts at the largest size on Node (`2026-10-19-320c9980-js.md`), ceiling in brackets: `fib` 1.39 (1.5), `countdown` 1.57 (1.3), `sieve` 4.62 (1.5), `nbody` 11.90 (1.3), `spectral_norm` 4.49 (1.3), `binary_trees` 1.41 (1.5), `pipeline` 0.29 (2.0), `rbtree` 2.52 (1.5), `map_set` 3.28 (3.0), `shapes` 2.24 (1.5), `tokenizer` 0.30 (1.5), `json_validate` 1.39 (2.0), `deltablue` 6.06 (2.0), `handled` depth 1 0.88 (2.0) and depth 16 0.88 (3.0), `contracts` 2.69 (2.0), `contracts_plain` 2.99 (1.3): six of the fifteen meet their ceiling and the median of the fifteen is 2.24 against the performance round's 1.5 (§14.3); on Bun five meet and the median is 2.47 (`map_set` 3.85 under its provisional 5.0, §17.152); `map_set:int` is 6.20 on Node and 13.23 on Bun, `handled_fwd` 4.90 and 11.63, `handled_reentry` 0.70 and 7.21. WASM against hand JS on Node at the largest size (`-wasm.md`, Node then Wasmtime): `contracts` 68× and 90× where the JS backend is 2.7×, `deltablue` 106× and 124×, `handled_fwd` 81× and 98×, `sieve` 51× and 65×, `nbody` 48× and 59×, `spectral_norm` 33× and 43×, `handled` at every depth 22× and 28×, `json_validate` 24× (Node), `tokenizer` rising from 4.4× at n = 1,000 to 35× at n = 100,000 while the JS backend holds 0.28–0.30× at every size (a superlinear cost), `fib` 1.96× and 1.88×, `countdown` 1.94× and 1.89×. Spread (§17.264, `docs/release.md` §2): Node 0.14% median, the WASM lane 0.30%, Wasmtime 0.11%, native 0.09% (Go the noisiest), Bun 1.35% with 116 of 198 cells over 1% and 48 bimodal in their middle three pairs; `compare` flags a Sakura/hand-JS ratio that moves 5% and blocks at 10% (§17.110), a Bun row compounds four cells' spreads, and §17.136 already reads Bun's peak RSS as advisory. `compile`: `check_hello` p95 10.6 ms against §17.195 (1)'s 10 ms target, every research/10 §6 budget met. `main` after `320c9980`: `7dd9dd47`, `917f9ac3`, `321b983e`, `d0222605`, `75ee81f6` and the docs commits; the code adds `std/bytes` growth, `std/encoding`, Base64 and the per-hop `net` check (234 lines of `sakura_runtime.js`, `codec.rs` in the rt crate), four builtin ids and seven signatures; no benchmark program calls any of it, and a cell's count subtracts start-up, so the runtime's loaded size is not in it. WS-P13b (`2d808283`..`0530f328`) and row 31 (`9a37edbe`) are inside `320c9980`; `dee11301` has no harness, and a commit of `dee11301` with the harness grafted on would measure a tree no release ships. Decision: **(1) The envelope is information for 0.1.0; the tag's gate is the blessed baseline.** Item 11 closes when the owner blesses the counted `js` and `wasm` runs of one commit with every oracle green and the spreads reported; the envelope's `miss` is carried under this entry as the named decision (§17.152 (2), §17.228 (2)), and the 0.1.0 claim level follows §17.109's own words: the ceilings gate claiming competitiveness, so 0.1.0 claims none. `envelope` keeps exit 0 and `bless` does not read it. **(2) Two lanes, no re-derivation.** The cross-engine ceilings (numeric kernels, `tokenizer` and `json_validate` against Rust and Go; allocation kernels against OCaml and Koka; `handled` against Koka) are wall-time quantities and keep their unit: `envelope` reads them in a **wall-time lane** from the counted files' `median_ms` (direction only, the host being loaded, §17.153) and prints the **count lane** beside it, labelled a ratio of counts and not the ceiling's unit; the design lead derives no per-cell IPC correction to turn one into the other, since any such factor would be fitted to the result it judges. The ceilings are re-read, on counts or on time, when the native backend's first counted run exists (M5), the one backend that compiles to the comparators' ISA without a JIT, a sandbox's bounds checks or boxed scalars; until then the cross-engine envelope gates nothing and no WASM work is undertaken to meet it. The **same-engine targets are read on counts and are the operative speed targets**: §17.109's per-program Sakura/hand-JS ceilings on Node and on Bun, the performance round's acceptance (the median of the fifteen at most 1.5, no program over its ceiling without a named decision, §14.3) and, new, the WASM-on-Node lane against hand JS on Node, the same process and ISA. §17.264 (4)'s "read against §17.109's ceilings" is narrowed to those lanes; `compare` is unchanged by this. **(3) The website says**: the counts, pending the bless; the JS backend is within 1.5–3× of hand-written JavaScript on most of the suite and 4.5–12× behind on five named programs; the WASM backend is first-release code, 2–124× behind hand JS by count and far from native; there is no native backend yet; the cross-language envelope is not met and Sakura makes no cross-language speed claim at 0.1.0; where Sakura is ahead of hand JS on Node (`pipeline` 0.29×, `tokenizer` 0.30×, `handled` 0.88×) the page names the mechanism (fusion, ownership, direct handlers) and generalises nothing; no time or time ratio from a counted run is quoted (§17.264 (5)); the landing page carries no speed claim and gets none. **(4) `320c9980` is the baseline commit, ratified.** It is the first commit with the harness, it is on `main`, it ships in 0.1.0, and it holds WS-P13b and row 31, which 0.1.0 ships; item 12's gate signature keeps `dee11301` as the parity-and-verification exit and item 11 names `320c9980`. WS-P13b's delta is therefore not readable against this baseline; its in-repo evidence stays the WS-P13a and WS-P13c ablations and its series' note, and item 13's review is of the landed series. The bless stands for the preparation commit (§17.228 (2): the commits after `320c9980` touch no benchmark program's path); Opus confirms it with a counted run of `fib` and `shapes` on the `js` suite at the preparation commit and `compare` against the blessed file, Node reading `ok`, a few minutes, committed as evidence beside the results before the owner tags. No run of `dee11301` is made. **(5) Bun is advisory in a counted `compare`.** A Bun row never blocks; it is `flagged` when its ratio of ratios moves more than the block threshold (10%), not the flag threshold, and the row prints its four cells' `instruction_spread`; Node blocks as before. Processes stay five: Bun's bimodality is a tier-up at a different call, which more pairs shift and do not remove, and a doubled Bun lane costs a good part of the hour the suite takes; a flagged Bun row is confirmed, when it matters, by one rerun of that program with `--processes 9 --filter`. This mirrors §17.136's Bun RSS rule. Opus lands the rule and (2)'s two lanes in `bench/harness/bench.py` with `bench/README.md` after the bless and before WS-P14. **(6) The performance push.** The owner's standing goal, fast by default against other languages, has one honest route per backend: on JS and WASM-on-JS, competitive with hand-written JavaScript on the same engine, the one comparison a JS-hosted program admits without a unit problem; against Rust, Go, OCaml and Koka, the native backend (M5, experimental at 1.0, §17.246), where the envelope is re-read. So the push is two waves on the shipped backends, each row under WS-P13a's protocol: attribute first with a hand-edited emitted module, then land the mechanism whose arm moved the count; a fix that does not move its bucket is not landed (§17.218); every row lands with a counted before and after of its programs on the reference Mac and `compare` on counts against the blessed baseline, Node blocking and Bun advisory; a row's fix lands when its target cells drop at least 10% on Node counts and no other Node cell flags without a named reason. *Wave 1, the JS backend, in this order*: **WS-P14** flat scalars and Float records (`nbody` 11.90×, `spectral_norm` 4.49×, `sieve` 4.62× on Node; §17.152's representation round, now), arms (i) the body records updated in place through WS-P13b's field rule, (ii) `List<Float>`, `List<Bool>` and `List<Int>` over typed arrays in `sakura_runtime.js` (a JS number is already the double these hold and the backend's `Int` fits 2^53, §4), (iii) scalar replacement of a non-escaping record in a loop in `sakura_core/src/opt`; **WS-P15** `Map<Int, _>` (`map_set:int` 6.20× Node, 13.23× Bun), the Int-key path of the runtime map, dense ids staying `List` (§17.217); **WS-P16** `deltablue` after WS-P13b (6.06×), `--dump owned` and a profile of what remains, shared with `shapes` 2.24× and `rbtree` 2.52×; **WS-P17** forwarding handlers (`handled_fwd` 4.90× Node, 11.63× Bun, the one `handled` case over its ceiling): a wrapper clause that only re-performs is resolved when the handler is installed, so the operation reaches the inner handler in one dispatch; semantics-adjacent, a review packet beside WS-P2b's; **WS-P18** the ceiling sweep: `countdown` 1.57 against 1.3, `contracts` 2.69 against 2.0 and `contracts_plain` 2.99 against 1.3 on Node; `fib` 2.31, `binary_trees` 2.54, `json_validate` 3.01 and `handled_reentry` 7.21 on Bun, WS-P12's Bun-tax attribution moving from Astra to Opus. Exit: the performance round's acceptance read on counts at the 0.2.0 counted baseline, the median of the fifteen Node ratios at most 1.5 from 2.24, every remaining miss named. *Wave 2, the WASM backend, after WS-P14–WS-P16 land*, measured as WASM on Node against hand JS on Node: **WS-W5** contracts on WASM (68–90× against 2.7× on JS): what a passing `requires` costs in the emitter and the rt (a blame record built before the check fails, a frame, a string), fixed so it costs a compare and a branch as on JS; **WS-W6** `tokenizer`'s superlinear cost (4.4× to 35× from n = 1,000 to 100,000): a complexity bug in string or `Bytes` handling in linear memory, `compare`'s log-log slope check the test; **WS-W3** then **WS-W4** as written (the frame protocol; `handled` 22–28×, `handled_fwd` 81–98× and `deltablue` 106–124× are their instances, §17.230); **WS-W7** flat scalars in linear memory (`sieve` 51–65×, `nbody` 48–59×, `spectral_norm` 33–43×), WS-P14's representation carried to the WASM heap, designed once with M5's layout in view and ABI.md updated where it documents the layout. *Against the web-APIs phases (§17.263 (2))*: the perf lane is its own worktree; phases 2, 3, 7a and R, already open, finish as they are; the tag-queue merges (4b, PR #4, 4a) are not delayed; phases 5–11 (pre-rc) start after WS-P14–WS-P16 land, and wave 2 interleaves with them; both waves are in before `v1.0.0-rc.1`'s counted baseline (§17.225 (5)). Opus adds each row to `performance-r1.md` §4 as it opens. Why: a ceiling the measured backend cannot meet by any tuning is a finding, not a gate; keeping the ceilings' unit keeps them falsifiable; the same-engine ratios are the ones a count can judge and the ones users of the shipped backends feel; the baseline that ships is the one worth blessing; Bun's noise is Bun's and should not stop a Node-clean commit; and the order of the push follows the measured gaps on the shipped backend first. Rejected: re-deriving the cross-engine ceilings on counts now (no principled conversion; a fitted one would be unfalsifiable); removing the envelope from the harness (it is the record of the gap); a counted "`dee11301` plus harness" commit (it measures nothing shipped); dropping Bun from the baseline (a primary engine, §17.109, and a deploy target); more Bun processes by default (cost, and the bimodality survives them); holding the web-APIs phases for the perf lane or the reverse (agents are never idle on this account, §17.263 (2)); tuning WASM to meet the cross-language envelope (a structural gap of boxed scalars, RC, bounds checks and no autovectorisation; M5's job). Performance: none at runtime; this orders the work. Changed: `docs/release.md` §2 (the two lanes, the Bun rule, the baseline commit, the preparation-commit check), `docs/plans/m4-exit-checklist.md` items 11–13 and the closing paragraph, `website/content/docs/benchmarks.mdx` ("Against the targets" and (3)'s words), the §17 heading. Opus, after the bless and before WS-P14: `compare`'s Bun rule and `envelope`'s two lanes in `bench/harness/bench.py` and `bench/README.md`. Impact: the owner (the bless and item 12's signature are the two inputs left before the tag), Opus (the harness changes, the preparation-commit check, WS-P14–WS-P18, then WS-W5–WS-W7), Astra (the gate report reads the envelope as (2) says; WS-P12 moves to Opus), Sol (the benchmarks page's words are set here).
266. **`std/crypto` tier 1a stands as built on JS and native; its WASM step is a held PR stacked on phase 4b at ABI 1.6.0 and merged right after it; a key without the operation's usage is `D020`; `crypto.verify`; RFC 7914 §11 is the PBKDF2 vector; the accessors, the params types and the host-floor limits are RFC text; a derived output is at most 1 MiB with one typed error on every backend; an imported HKDF or PBKDF2 key is extractable when imported so; synchronous `node:crypto`; four RustCrypto crates behind `native`; `sign_webhook` waits for WASM (RFC 0002 §2.7, §6, §7; plan `web-apis.md` phase 7a; §17.263 (2), (3); round 37, 2026-10-20).** Facts: `3a027001` (the vector tables) and `3eab0003` (`std/crypto`) are on `main` with every gate green; `digest`, `hmac`, `verify`, `derive_bits` for `Hkdf` and `Pbkdf2`, `import_key`/`export_key` for `Raw` and `generate_key` for HMAC agree between `--target js` and `--target native` on NIST CAVP SHA-2 ShortMsg, RFC 4231, RFC 5869 A.1–A.3 and RFC 7914 §11; on WASM every primitive is `D090` ("builtin crypto_digest is not supported by the WASM backend yet"), seven fixtures are in `parity.rs`'s `KNOWN` under one reason string, and `INDEX.md`, the skill and the capabilities tour say so; the wasm32 `sakura_rt` object is built by bare `rustc` with no dependencies, so RustCrypto cannot be in the guest and the plan's route is `hosted` imports, an ABI MINOR revision, which §17.263 (2) holds until the tag; PR #5 (phase 4b) holds ABI 1.5.0 (`clock_monotonic_us`, the fiber rule); ABI §0 forbids a module recording a skipped number (N0b went 1.2.0 → 1.4.0 in one step) and 1.2.4/1.2.5 shipped as consecutive revisions in one release; JS calls `node:crypto`'s `createHash`, `createHmac`, `timingSafeEqual`, `hkdfSync` and `pbkdf2Sync`, not `crypto.subtle`, because a builtin is a direct call and `crypto.subtle` is asynchronous, so the plan's per-instance import cache has nothing to cache; `hmac` and `verify` are declared `requires is_hmac(key.algorithm) && permits(key, Sign | Verify)` and `derive_bits` `requires permits(key, DeriveBits) && fits(key.algorithm, params)`, with `allows(alg, usage)` and `permits(key, usage)` `@total` and `pub`; the RFC types `hmac -> Bytes` and `verify -> Bool`, so its "`Err(KeyUsage)`" line cannot be returned; `verify` is reserved (`V0007`) except after `.` or `fn` (§2.1), so the call is `crypto.verify(key, tag, data)` or `key.verify(tag, data)`, and `import std/crypto` binds `crypto`, so the RFC's `Crypto.digest` names nothing; RFC 6070 and RFC 5869 A.4–A.7 are SHA-1, which §2.7 does not offer; HKDF and PBKDF2 over SHA-384/512 have no official vectors; Node's `hkdfSync` bounds `info` at 1,024 bytes and `pbkdf2Sync` bounds iterations at 2^31 − 1, and both are `CryptoError`s on every backend; an absurd `derive_bits` length today is `D096` on native (the heap budget) and `D090` on JS (Node's `RangeError`), a backend-dependent defect; the plan's "export for HKDF, PBKDF2 keys" was read as extractable allowed, where Web Crypto imports those two algorithms non-extractable; `hmac`, `hkdf` and `pbkdf2` 0.13.0 enter `sakura_rt`'s `native` feature with `ctutils` and `cmov` (constant-time select with inline `unsafe` asm) as their transitive dependencies, exact-pinned, and the wasm32 object has none of them; `cookbook/sign_webhook.mdx` is generated from a `compiler/examples` project that `parity.rs` runs on WASM with no `KNOWN`. Decision: **(1) The WASM step is its own held PR at ABI 1.6.0, stacked on PR #5.** Opus builds it now: the `crypto_*` `hosted` imports in `sakura_wasm_host.js` and `validate.rs`, ABI.md §8.2 and the §0 line, `sakura_abi_version` `0x010600` on both hosts, the seven `KNOWN` rows and the three "waits" sentences deleted, `cookbook/sign_webhook.mdx` and its example project. The branch starts from `hold/webapis-4b`, rebases when it does, and merges right after it; the queue after the tag is PR #5 (1.5.0), the crypto step (1.6.0), PR #4 (no ABI), then 4a when phase 3 is on `main`. Not 1.5.0 shared: two PRs editing one version entry couple their rebases and their reviews (4b is Opus's work; crypto's is the owner's as security reviewer), and a MINOR number is free, as 1.2.4/1.2.5 showed. Phase 7a's acceptance ("every vector on three backends") is met when that PR merges; the queue row reads "JS and native `3eab0003`; WASM held" until then, and 0.1.0's notes state the `D090` as a known limitation of a module that precedes the contract. A non-JS embedder's refusal stays RFC §7's link-time one. **(2) A key without the operation's usage is `D020`, endorsed.** Which key a call passes is a fact about the program (§17.263 (3)); Web Crypto's `InvalidAccessError` is the same classification; `permits` and `allows` are the test a caller with a runtime-chosen key makes first, and each `requires` doc comment names them. RFC §Rejected uses changes its `Err(KeyUsage)` line; `KeyError`'s `NotAllowed(usage)` stays for `import_key` and `generate_key`, where the usages are data. **(3) `verify` stays reserved**; the RFC writes `crypto.verify(key, tag, data)` and `crypto.digest(alg, b)`. Unreserving one word for one module is not worth a lexer change and a §2.1 edit. **(4) RFC 7914 §11 is the PBKDF2 vector**, endorsed; the plan's fixture is `crypto_pbkdf2_rfc7914.sak`. **(5) JS = native parity is sufficient evidence for the SHA-384/512 KDFs.** Node's functions are OpenSSL's and native's are RustCrypto's: two independent implementations agreeing on literal inputs is what a published vector is; the inputs are literal in the fixture, so a third implementation can be run by hand. **(6) The accessors and the params types are endorsed** and enter RFC §2.7: `algorithm`, `usages`, `extractable`, `allows`, `permits`, `HkdfParams`, `Pbkdf2Params`, `DeriveParams`, `KeyReason`, `CryptoReason`, `derive_bits(key, params, bits)` with `bits` a positive multiple of 8. **(7) The limits are RFC §6 text, and the output length joins them.** HKDF `info` at most 1,024 bytes (`Info(n)`), PBKDF2 iterations `1..=2^31 − 1` (`Iterations(n)`), HKDF output at most 255 × hash length (`Length(bits)`), and now PBKDF2 output at most 2^20 bytes, 8,388,608 bits (`Length(bits)`), checked in Sakura before the external on every backend. The lowest host's bound is the contract, and a limit is typed, never a defect (RFC §6); the native-`D096`/JS-`D090` split goes with it. Opus adds the one comparison and the `_rejects_` case on `main` now (an additive module's fix before the tag). **(8) An imported HKDF or PBKDF2 key is extractable when imported so**, endorsed. The material is the caller's own import; `extractable` is the caller's choice for every `Raw` key, and the doc comment notes that Web Crypto differs. **(9) Synchronous `node:crypto`, endorsed**; the plan's `crypto.subtle` and its import cache are struck. Bun implements the five functions; Bun stays advisory (§17.265). **(10) The crate set is accepted behind `native`.** Four RustCrypto crates at exact pins, `cmov`'s asm reached only from the native object; the owner's 7a review as security reviewer covers the crate set and the licence list in the commit (plan acceptance); the MSRV job is the check that the pins build on the pinned toolchain. **(11) `sign_webhook` lands in the held PR**, endorsed; the tour's tested HMAC check serves until then. Why: §17.263's rule is additive on `main`, ABI bumps held, and one PR per ABI revision keeps the held series reviewable; `requires` is for facts about the program and `Result` for facts about the data; a limit that differs by backend in its defect code is a parity hole, and the fix is one comparison in Sakura. Performance: none measured; builtins are direct calls, and (7) adds one integer comparison per `derive_bits`. Changed: RFC 0002 §2.7, §Concrete examples ("Rejected uses"), §6, §Compatibility, metadata; `docs/plans/web-apis.md` §2, phase 7a, §4; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` (the 2026-10-20 7a entry answered). Impact: Opus (the WASM PR stacked on #5 at 1.6.0; the 1 MiB bound on `main`), owner (7a's security review: crate set, licences, the `D020` rule; the 0.1.0 notes' WASM line at the preparation commit), Sol (none).
267. **Phase 4b's dialogs are std functions over `print` and `read_line`, served by every `Console` handler, with `Console.scripted(lines)` for tests; the scope-outcome fix `ff66cded` leaves PR #5 and lands on `main` before the tag as its own commit, a behaviour change in both runtimes named here for the owner's review (RFC 0002 §2.8; plan `web-apis.md` phase 4b; §17.263 (2); round 37, 2026-10-20).** Facts: PR #5 (`hold/webapis-4b`) is two commits: `ff66cded`, a runtime fix, and `24e944a2`, phase 4b (`Clock.monotonic_micros`, `Task.cancel`/`cancelled`, `std/task.every`, the dialogs, `Json.render`, ABI 1.5.0); RFC §2.8 wrote `alert(msg) -> Unit !
