Why: a gate that blocks a faster head for being faster has stopped measuring memory; the one-call peak is the measurement the gate meant, it was in the files all along, and reading it changes no number anyone blessed; the fusion's trace shows the collector's phase, not retention, and §17.136's purpose (it caught `binary_trees`' dead ANF temporary, a live-heap rise) is served better by the statistic that cannot move with k. Rejected: reverting or carrying the fusion (−18.6% on its bucket, and the live heap fell); re-measuring the head at the baseline's `calls` (equal k still reads the collector's phase, 187 → 222 MB at k = 16, and costs a run per crossing where the one-call figure costs nothing); a wider margin or a GC-phase exemption judged by `--trace-gc` on each crossing (a rule that needs a reading each time is not a gate); waiting for the flag commit to re-read the many-call peaks (the 16 MB arm still crosses 23% on string, so the defect would stay under the new flags); a many-call minus one-call "retained per call" gate (the difference is the collector's phase at two different k, the noise this entry removes; a cross-call leak is the eval harness's and `bench_counters`' to catch). Performance: none in the compiler; `compare` reads a field it already has. Changed: `performance-r1.md` §4.1 (WS-P15 closed, the harness item, the WS-P18 arm); `bench/deltas.md` row WS-P15 (verdict pointer, by Opus with the re-read); `bench/README.md` `compare` row and peak-RSS section (Opus). Impact: Opus (one commit, before WS-P21's compare: (3) in `bench/harness/bench.py` with `test_bench.py` fixtures, a cell whose many-call peak crosses at doubled `calls` while its one-call peak does not reads `ok`, a cell whose one-call peak crosses reads a crossing and takes the confirmation group; `bench/README.md` (3) and (4); `compare` re-run over the existing WS-P15 files and the `deltas.md` row's verdict rewritten from it with the one-call figures; (5) inside WS-P20's row; (6) noted in the WS-P18 paragraph). Owner: nothing; no bless moves.

284. **Phase 5 (`std/stream`, `9139a178`) stands as built with one contract added and one bound closed: a view's row carries its operation's `Fail`, a CR is a terminator only before an LF, `to_list` gets `requires max_items >= 0`, the final unterminated line is checked against `max_line` as it is yielded, the private `Leg`/`Answered` rename stands; the reference evaluator's four `Bytes` skips and one `Fs.memory` skip and the two bare-corpus WASM `KNOWN` rows need no plan row; phase 8 is next when WS-P20 is on `main` (RFC 0002 §2.5 amended; plan `web-apis.md` §2, phase 5, §5; §17.280 (3), (5); §17.276; §17.279; round 41, 2026-10-20).** Facts: the REQUESTS entry of `9139a178` lists six readings; the escape check reached a view in four shapes (`stream_view_cannot_escape.sak` is `V6003`, and a combinator over a view, a hand-built `Source` capturing the body and a pulled `Step` are too), so the `design-question` §17.280 (5) anticipated was not needed; `http.sak` declares `body_source -> Source<Bytes, {Http, Fail<HttpError>}>`, `fs.sak` `file_source -> Source<Bytes, {Fs, Fail<FsError>}>` and `file_sink -> Sink<Bytes, {Fs, Fail<FsError>}>`, where RFC §2.5 wrote `{Http}` and `{Fs}`; `lines` splits on LF, `strip_cr` removes one CR at the end of each complete line, the pending tail is measured without its CR, and at `Done` the tail is yielded as it is, so a tail of `max_line` bytes plus a CR passes the pending check and is yielded at `max_line + 1`; `to_list` has no contract where `take` has `requires n >= 0`, `chunks` `requires size > 0`, `read_chunk` `requires max > 0` and `Blob.source`/`body_source`/`file_source` `requires chunk > 0`; the interpreter report (`corpus__interpreter_report.snap`, plan §3.5 L2) already carries 90 `unsupported (builtin …)` rows, 56 of them `string_to_bytes`/`bytes_from_list`, and the five phase-5 skips are the same two builtins and `fs_memory_root`; the bare-corpus `KNOWN` list already holds `host_fs_env` (`None`: type descriptors, no WASI Fs imports) and the Node-host-only rows; WS-P20 is not on `main` (§17.283 still files into its row). Decision: **(1) Reading (1) ratified**: a view's row is the operation's row as declared, `Fail` included, which is what §17.280 (3)'s "rows as the operations declare them" meant; RFC §2.5's view line now says so; `file_sink`'s `close` writes nothing, since `with_file` closes the file. **(2) Reading (2) ratified**, with the rule named: a CR is a terminator only as part of CRLF; a lone CR, trailing or not, is data (as `BufRead::lines` reads it, and unlike Go's `ScanLines`); an empty line is a line and a trailing LF adds none; RFC §2.5 says "a CR before the LF removed" instead of "a trailing CR removed". **(3) Reading (3) changed**: `to_list` declares `requires max_items >= 0`, so a negative bound is `D020` at the caller as every other bound in the module is; it still pulls exactly one item past the bound, which is the only way to know (ratified). **(4) The bound closes at `Done`.** `lines` checks the final unterminated line as it yields it (`String.len(pending) > max_line` fails `MaxLine` in the `Done` arm), so no yielded line exceeds `max_line`; the pending check during streaming keeps measuring without the CR, since an LF may still consume it. **(5) Readings (4), (5), (6) ratified**: `chunks` holds the carry and the item being cut; `decode_source` skips an empty decoded chunk and runs `finish` once; `encode_source` is `map`; `Leg<T> = Answered(T) | Hop(Request)` is private to `std/http` and no public name moved. **(6) No plan row for the evaluator's skips.** The interpreter is plan §3.5 L2's memory-accounting check and its `unsupported` rows are its own record, pre-existing for every `Bytes` fixture since phase 1 and for `Fs.memory` since `host_fs_env`; a `Bytes` builtin set for the interpreter lands when something needs its verdict on a `Bytes` program (an ownership audit of a `Bytes` path, or the first `Bytes`-shaped benchmark), and that is the row's trigger, not a date; until then the snapshot's count is the measure, and a phase whose fixtures are all `unsupported` says so in its REQUESTS entry, as this one did. **(7) The two `KNOWN` rows stand and need no row.** `stream_pipe_to_file_sink` (`None`) has `host_fs_env`'s cause and goes with it; `http_body_source_scripted` (`Wasi`) goes with a WASI `Http` import set, which no phase plans; `sakura build` parity runs both. **(8) Phase 8 is next**, when WS-P20 is on `main` (§17.279, plan §2: both edit `sakura_runtime.js`); 6 and 10 follow 8; until then the web lane's only items are (3) and (4). Why: a `requires` on a bound is the module's rule and a reader who sees `take`'s contract expects `to_list`'s; "no yielded line exceeds `max_line`" is the sentence the doc comment makes and one byte is still a breach of it; CR-as-data is the reading under which "split on LF" is the whole rule; a `KNOWN` row whose cause is another row's cause is tracked by that cause. Rejected: Go's rule (a lone trailing CR stripped at the end of input: a second terminator rule for one position); counting the pending tail's CR during streaming (a false `MaxLine` on a CRLF line of exactly `max_line` bytes); `max_items < 0` read as `0` (a silent bound where every sibling defects); a plan row for the interpreter's `Bytes` builtins (no consumer yet); a `.wasm.stdout` for either `KNOWN` fixture (§17.280 (5): none). Changed: RFC 0002 §2.5 (the view line, the `lines` phrase, `to_list`'s contract) and its metadata line (the SHA); `web-apis.md` §2 row 5 (the SHA), phase 5 (landed), §5. Impact: Opus (one small `fix(std)` commit, now, in the web lane: `to_list`'s `requires` with a fixture `stream_to_list_rejects_negative_bound.sak` (`expect-defect: D020`), the `Done`-arm check with one arm in `stream_lines_rejects_max_line.sak` (`["abc\r"]`, `max_line` 3, fails), both doc comments, the stdlib page and skill regenerated, a changelog line; then phase 8 when WS-P20 lands). Nothing for Sol.

286. **Phase 8 (`std/websocket`, `6b633a99`, ABI 1.8.0) stands as built: `Received = Data(Message) | Closed(CloseInfo)`, `connect` on a `String`, no `max_frame`, no secret headers, RFC 6455 in the runtime, a socket as an `Int` in the file table; one bound added (the receive queue holds at most `max_message` bytes beside its 64 messages, and a pong waits for a writable socket); an operation's `requires` is checked at the perform site from now on, `D020` blaming the performer, and the std handlers' private re-checks go; the twin-restart test's `live_objects` reading stands once the 4 KiB step is confirmed; `http_body_of` lands natively now, not as a `KNOWN` row; the owner's review list for the new `net` path; phase 8 on `main` releases phase 6 now, N1b's remainder, and MINOR 1.9.0 to the first of 7b-W or phase 10 (RFC 0002 §1, §3, §6, §7 amended; plan `web-apis.md` §2, phase 8, phase 6; `m5-native.md` §2; §7.2; §17.3, §17.115, §17.211 (2), §17.262 (2), §17.266 (1), §17.270 (1), §17.279, §17.285 (1), (2d), (3), (4); round 42, 2026-10-20).** Facts: the REQUESTS entry of `6b633a99` lists eleven readings. The module declares `Message = Text(String) | Binary(Bytes)`, `Received = Data(Message) | Closed(CloseInfo)`, `SocketReason = Connect(String) | MessageTooLarge | NotOpen | Failed(String)`, `Options { subprotocols, headers: List<(String, String)>, max_message }` and an opaque `Socket { id, protocol, max_message }`; a sum's constructors share the module's namespace (`V1001`, §17.3), so the plan's `Received = Text | Binary | Closed(CloseInfo)` cannot be declared beside `Message`. The `Url` refinement admits `http(s)://` and `/` (§17.262), so `url"wss://…"` does not type; `checked_url` runs `Url.parse`, refuses a scheme other than `ws`/`wss` and a fragment, and `ws_connect` runs the same `netRefusal(u)` as `Http.host()`, `hostname:port` with `ws` 80 and `wss` 443. The runtime's new section (`sakura_runtime.js` 4919–5216, about 300 lines, no dependency) speaks RFC 6455 over `node:http`/`node:https`'s `upgrade`: a 16-byte random key, `sec-websocket-accept` verified, a subprotocol accepted only when offered, any extension refused, every client frame masked with a fresh 4-byte mask, reserved bits, a masked server frame, an unknown opcode, a fragmented or long control frame and a misplaced continuation 1002, a data frame that would take its message past `max_message` 1009 before its payload is held (a 64-bit length above `max_message` reads as `Infinity`), text or a close reason that is not UTF-8 1007, a one-byte close payload 1002, a non-101 response drained and `Err` with no redirect followed, `Options.headers` refused for `host`/`upgrade`/`connection`/`content-length`/`transfer-encoding` and any `sec-websocket-*` name and otherwise passed to Node (whose header validation throws inside the `try`), 64 queued messages then `socket.pause()`, 5 s after a client close then `destroy` and 1006, 1001 from `file_close`'s step on every exit of the callback. The queue's bound is a count: 64 messages of up to `max_message` each is 1 GiB resident at the default before TCP holds the peer back; a ping is answered with `socket.write` whether or not the socket's write buffer needs draining. The global `WebSocket` cannot pause reading, bound a frame or send 1009 (§17.279 named it for the plan on the strength of Bun's page, not of its API). A socket is `nextFile++` in `files`, closed by `file_closing`/`file_close`, so ABI 1.8.0 adds three `async` imports (`ws_connect`, `ws_send`, `ws_receive`, request kind 4) and a Node-only `hosted` `ws_close`; handle kind 3 stays unused. Contracts: §7.2 says `requires` is checked on entry with `D020` at the call site, every build; `sakura_core/src/lower/expr.rs` emits that check at a def's entry (`contracts(&ret)`, line 156) and both backends consume Core's `Bind::Check`; the perform is lowered at `lower/mod.rs:1236` with no check, so an operation's clause is typed, printed by `sakura doc`, listed as an obligation by `specs.rs` and never run: `WebSocket.close(sock, 1001, "")` returns normally on JS and WASM against `requires closable(code, reason)`, and `Cli.exit` (`0..=255`), `Random.int` (`lo <= hi`), `Random.bytes` (`n >= 0`), `Fs.read_chunk` and `Http.read_chunk` (`max > 0`) and `WebSocket.connect` (`max_message > 0`) are the same; the JS host hand-checks `Random.int` in `random_int` and the phase-8 handlers call private `positive`/`close_args` defs, so `websocket_close_rejects_code.sak` is `D020` blamed inside std. The twin-restart test (`tests/wasm.rs`, §17.211 (2)) compared `live` bytes between direct style and `--no-direct`; with 1.8.0's three codes the direct run reads 9,152 against 5,056 with `live_objects` 8 on both, a difference of exactly 4,096; `heap.rs`'s classes end at 4,096 and a larger block is a page run, and under the host tests the data segment (the layout and code tables, `image.rs` `code_table_with`) stands in as heap blocks. `http_body_source_scripted` (phase 5) defects `D091` on native on `main` because `http_body_of` (a body without a connection, one chunk) is a host builtin the native host lacks, which fails `sakura_host_native`'s corpus test and `parity.rs`; `Http.scripted` handled inside `main` is not refused on native (§17.271 (9)). Phase 8 is on `main`, so §17.285's triggers "after phase 8" have fired; 7b is in flight and not on `main`; WS-P21 is not on `main`. Decision: **(1) `Received = Data(Message) | Closed(CloseInfo)`, ratified.** `send` takes a `Message`, `receive` returns a `Received`, and the arms read `Data(Text(s))`, `Data(Binary(b))`, `Closed(info)`; the RFC's example now says so. **(2) `connect(url: String, options, body)`, ratified.** The string is parsed before anything opens, `Connect(reason)` names the fault; `Url` stays the `http(s)` refinement and no `http(s)`→`ws(s)` mapping is done (a mapped scheme is a silent rewrite of what the program said). **(3) `SocketReason` and the 1006 reading, ratified.** The net refusal is `Connect("host:port is not in the manifest's net list")`, the RFC's `SocketError("…")` line is rewritten to it; a dropped connection is `Closed(1006, "", false)`, not an error, as the web's close event. **(4) No `max_frame`, ratified, and one bound added.** A frame is bounded by `max_message` before its payload is held, so a second knob would describe nothing. The receive queue is bounded in bytes as well as messages: the host pauses the socket when 64 messages wait or when the waiting messages total more than `max_message` bytes (the message being assembled not counted), and resumes below both; a pong is written only while the socket needs no drain (RFC 6455 §5.5.2 permits answering the most recent ping), so a ping flood cannot grow the write buffer. RFC §6's row reads "`max_message` (default 16 MiB) per message and per queue, 64 messages, then TCP backpressure". **(5) No secret headers, ratified; the owner's signature is the gate.** `Options.headers` are plain strings and no import is of kind `secret`; §15.11's sink rules apply, so a `Secret` cannot reach a header without a reveal. A `secret_headers` field shaped as `Request`'s, carried by a kind-`secret` import with §17.270 (1)'s zeroing, is a `REQUESTS.md` item for the owner's signature and lands as an additive 0.2.0 change when signed; nothing is built before. **(6) RFC 6455 in the runtime, ratified.** The three requirements the global cannot meet are the RFC's own (§6: backpressure, a frame bound, 1009); the cost is that the parser is ours, which is why (10) exists. Rejected: the `ws` package (the runtime has no dependency and gains none). **(7) An `Int` in the file table, ratified.** `file_closing` is the one release path the runtime already has, so scope exit, `fail`, defect and cancellation close the socket by the mechanism §8.4 names; the plan's handle kind and finalizer code are dropped from phase 8's file list; kind 3 stays reserved. The additions (`options()`, `protocol`, `closable` as `@total`, `messages` as a view, `ScriptStep`) are ratified; `scripted` failing `Failed(step)` on a mismatch instead of hanging is the deterministic-peer rule. **(8) An operation's `requires` is checked at the perform site.** The perform is the operation's entry: the compiler emits the def-entry check before every `Bind::Perform` of a contracted operation, in the performer's module, with the perform's own span as the blame (no `$site` parameter: the site is static), `D020` naming the operation and the clause as a call does; `ensures` on an operation (none in std today) is the same mechanism on the operation's normal return, `D021` naming the operation. A handler trusts the contract as a callee does and never re-checks; a handler arm that performs the operation again is a perform site and is checked again (§17.115: never hoisted, never deduplicated); the `D011` bracket and `W5005` apply as to a def. The private `positive`/`close_args` defs go with the fix; the JS host's own `requires` in `random_int` stays, since it guards the runtime's callers, not the program's. Lane: the web lane (phase 8's agent), one `fix(core)` commit now, before phase 6; files `sakura_core/src/lower/{mod,expr}.rs`, `std/websocket.sak`, fixtures, the regenerated LIR corpus, `bench_counters.txt` if a cell moves; disjoint from WS-P21 (`opt/owned.rs`, `emit.rs`) and WS-W5 (`lir/lower.rs`, `func.rs`, `exec.rs`); WS-P17, which will edit `lower/mod.rs`'s handler section, has not started, and if it starts first the perform hunk is kept beside it. Acceptance: `websocket_close_rejects_code.sak`'s `D020` moves to the caller's perform span (the fixture's expectation reviewed, not normalized); a negative fixture per contracted std operation that lacks one (`cli_exit_rejects_code.sak`, `random_int_rejects_reversed_range.sak`, `random_bytes_rejects_negative.sak`, `fs_read_chunk_rejects_zero.sak`, `http_read_chunk_rejects_zero.sak`, `websocket_connect_rejects_max_message.sak`), each `expect-defect: D020` with the perform's span, identical on three backends and in `--json`; one positive fixture in which a `scripted` handler records every argument it sees and no violating one arrives; the `D020` JSON record unchanged (no diagnostic-contract version moves); `sakura doc`'s printed contract unchanged; §7.2 gains the sentence "an operation's `requires` is checked at the perform site, blaming the performer". **(9) `live_objects` stands, once confirmed.** What §17.211 (2)'s test pins is a leaked partial list, which is objects; a block count is the measure that cannot move with the data segment. The cause is confirmed once, not assumed: Opus reads the code table's byte size on the two runs (a scratch print, not landed) and records both sizes and the run step in the test's comment; if the 4,096 is not that table crossing a run boundary, it is a leak and this entry's ratification does not apply. **(10) The owner's review of the new `net` path**, recorded as a dated line under the phase-8 REQUESTS entry, as 7b's crate set will be; the list: (a) `netRefusal` is the one policy: the same function as `Http.host()`, `ws` 80 / `wss` 443, the `hostname:port` string as `URL` yields it (an IPv6 host keeps its brackets, an IDN host is its punycode), and it runs before any socket opens; (b) no redirect: a non-101 response is drained, the request destroyed, `Err` returned, and no second host can be reached from the handshake; (c) TLS: `node:https` defaults, `rejectUnauthorized` untouched, no `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` read, no proxy environment honoured, so egress is direct and the grant is the whole policy; (d) headers: the `WS_OWN` set and `sec-websocket-*` refused, names and values passing through Node's validation inside the `try` (a CR or LF is `Err`, never on the wire), `authorization` and `cookie` allowed as plain strings per (5); (e) the handshake: a fresh 16-byte key, `sec-websocket-accept` verified, a subprotocol only when offered, every extension refused (no `permessage-deflate`, so no decompression surface), a fresh 4-byte mask per frame; (f) the parser: the 1002/1007/1009 cases above, `s.buf` bounded by one frame plus one TCP chunk, the 64-bit length read, fragment state reset on every message and on failure; (g) bounds: the 64-message and `max_message`-byte queue of (4), the pong rule, the 5 s close timer and `destroy`, `unref` after end, `file_closing` on every exit including cancellation (1001), `suspend`'s cancel destroying the handshake request; (h) the strings a program sees (`failureOf(e)`, the status line, the subprotocol and extension refusals) carry no header value or credential; (i) the scripted peer and `checked_url` touch no network; (j) `ws_peer.mjs` binds `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port; (k) no dependency added. **(11) `http_body_of` lands natively now.** A scripted body is not a declared platform difference, so a `KNOWN` row would record a missing builtin as a difference; the builtin (one chunk, cut at `max`, as the JS runtime's) goes into `sakura_host_native` as a `fix(native)` commit by the web lane before (8), since a red `parity.rs` on `main` is a gate (§17.285 (5)); if `cargo test --workspace --locked` on `main` is not red, it still lands first. **(12) Waits released and the order.** Phase 8 on `main` fires three triggers of §17.285: the scheduler is free, so **phase 6 starts now** in the web lane after (11), (8) and the (4) fix, with no ABI MINOR (its codec is `miniz_oxide` in `rt`, no host import) and its `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` hunk as the lane's last commit, rebased over whatever lock `main` has when it lands, adding only its crate (`cargo update -p <crate> --precise <pin>`, every other line unchanged, `--locked` green), so it no longer waits for 7b's lock (§17.285 (2d) is amended: the lock is shared append-only under (1)'s rule); **N1b's remainder** (Http, serve, Llm natively) may take the next free line, (11) being its first item; **MINOR 1.9.0 is free** and goes to the first of 7b-W (after 7b is on `main`) or phase 10 (after 6) to be ready, the other taking 1.10.0 after it lands (§17.266 (1)); 11 after 10; 7c after 7b-W, optional; 12 beside each. The (4) fix and (8) change no import, so ABI.md's WebSocket paragraph gains the queue sentence at 1.8.0 unchanged. Why: every reading keeps the RFC's rule where the RFC had one and the most conservative shape where it had none; the queue byte bound is the limit AGENTS.md asks for stated in the unit the attacker controls; a printed contract that never runs is the one thing §7.2 forbids, and the perform site is where a def's rule already puts the check, so the fix is the existing mechanism at one more site rather than a per-handler convention that every std author must remember; an object count is the invariant the twin test states, but a measurement that changed by exactly one run step is explained, not confirmed, until someone reads the table. Rejected: `ReceivedText`/`ReceivedBinary` constructors (two names for one message); widening `Url` to `ws(s)` (a refinement that admits two protocol families refines nothing, and `Request` would accept a `wss` URL); a `WsUrl` refinement (a second URL type for one function; additive later if a second use appears); checking operation contracts in every handler arm (the blame needs a threaded site, every handler author must repeat it, and the host's `scripted` would still be unchecked); leaving them unchecked as documentation until `sakura verify` (§7.2: every build); a `KNOWN` row for `http_body_of`; holding phase 6 for 7b's lock (a one-block lock conflict is mechanical, and the pure parts cost 7b nothing); assigning 1.9.0 now to 7b-W (7b is not on `main`, and a reserved MINOR is a MINOR in flight). Performance: a perform of a contracted operation pays its predicate and a branch (§17.115); no counted program performs one on a hot path; the queue bound is one counter per socket. Changed: RFC 0002 §1 (the example: `url: String`, the `Data(…)` arms), §3 and the first-use list (`Connect(…)`), §6 (the `WebSocket` row), §Security (frames bounded by `max_message`), §Metadata (phase 8); `web-apis.md` §2 (the order paragraph), phase 8 (ratified), phase 6 (starts now, the lock rule); `m5-native.md` §2 (N1b's trigger fired); §7.2's sentence lands with (8); the §17 heading's intro. Impact: Opus, the web lane, in this order: (11) `fix(native)`; (8) `fix(core)` with its fixtures; the (4) fix with `websocket.test.js` cases for the byte bound and the pong rule and ABI.md's sentence; (9)'s confirmation in the test comment; then phase 6. The owner: (10), one review, recorded under the REQUESTS entry; (5)'s signature when asked. Sol: phase 12 for `std/websocket` (the stdlib page's `Received` shape, the `net` sentence in `manifest.mdx`, the recipe's arms if the RFC example changed them). Nothing for Astra.
287. **WS-W5 is accepted as landed (`d2534e3e`) and closed: its exit is re-read as its mechanism's bucket, which is exhausted (`contracts` −10.2% and −10.1% at n ≥ 10^5, −9.5% and −9.8% below, the bracket having been 9.3% of the count; `contracts_plain` is the control cell, and its 0% is the evidence the change touched only the contract path); the three non-contract arms open as three rows: WS-W8, a `Unit` join parameter stays `Unit` (`lower.rs`, ABI errata L8, the bucket rule, not the 10% cell rule); WS-W9, the reference-count decrement in place (`func.rs`, the `drop` export, ABI §10's `drops` redefined as what compiled code asked for, `bench_counters.txt` byte-identical as the proof); and `cx::wasm::rt()`'s 1,376-byte frame as WS-W3's first fix, since it is the `wasm::rt` bucket §17.218 left unresolved, so WS-W3's fix opens now with `cx.rs` in its set; a perf row names its target cell and its control when it opens, and §17.265 (6)'s 10% reads the target (plan `performance-r1.md` §4.1; ABI.md §3.1, §7, §10, errata L8; §17.218, §17.265 (6), §17.285 (2b), (3), (5); round 42, 2026-10-20, on Opus's design-question).** Facts: `d2534e3e` emits no `contract_enter`/`contract_exit` bracket around a predicate that cannot raise; the counted compare against the blessed `3bf2343f` reads `contracts` 3.21 M → 2.90 M (−9.5%) at n = 1,000, −9.8% at 10^4, −10.2% at 10^5, −10.1% at 10^6, `contracts_plain` +0.2%, every other Sakura cell within ±0.8%, verdict `ok`, nothing flagged; every `expect-defect` fixture, the `--json` `defect` record, the LIR corpus (27 pairs elided in 19 snapshots, nothing else), the native corpus and `bench_counters.txt` are unchanged. The attribution by hand-edited WAT at n = 10^5: `increment`'s four bracket calls and four `rt_take_defect` tests were 28 M of 302.9 M (9.3%); `total`'s bracket wraps the call of `List.all`, which can raise, so it stays (1.2 M); the landed count is 272.0 M. What remains between `contracts` (2,713 M) and `contracts_plain` (1,663 M) is `List.all`'s closure loop in the predicate, about 1,000 instructions an element of `rt_dup`, `drop`, `list_at` and `rt_box_i64`, the costs `contracts_plain` itself is made of. `contracts_plain` has no contract; 85% of its count is `total`'s `fold`, and `run`'s loop alone is 25.6 M of 166.9 M. §17.285 (2b) wrote the exit as both cells down 10%: the designer named the plain twin as a target when it is the control. Three arms outside any contract, each measured by Opus on the emitted module: (a) every `while` loop's `Unit` join parameter is a generic word (ABI errata L8: `local_reprs` in `sakura_lir/src/lower.rs` widens every `Unit` join parameter to `Word` unconditionally), so each iteration boxes `()` and calls `drop` on it: an inline immediate test before the call read −4.5% on `contracts_plain` and −7.4% more on `contracts`; (b) an inline `rc > 1` decrement before calling `drop` read −13.5% on `contracts_plain` and −20% more on `contracts`, and changes what ABI §10's `drops` counts ("calls of the `drop` export, compiled code's and the host's"), the counter `reuse_and_borrow_counters_reconcile_by_hand` and the native corpus read; (c) `cx::wasm::rt()` (`runtime/rt/src/cx.rs`) is `slot.get_or_insert_with(|| Rt::new(…))`, so `Rt::new`'s construction is inlined into every runtime call's prologue and each call reserves a 1,376-byte frame; returning before it when the instance exists read −3.2%. §17.218 attributed 28.2% of all-frame `fib`'s samples to `wasm::rt` as a leaf with the mechanism unresolved and ordered WS-W3's fixes as one `rt()` per step, the frame resolved once per step, then the free list; WS-W3's fix waited for WS-W5 in `exec.rs` (§17.285 (3)). The LIR corpus and the native backend both consume `local_reprs`' output; the JS backend boxes nothing. Decision: **(1) WS-W5 is accepted and closed at `d2534e3e`.** A contract row's target cell is the contracted program and its control is the plain twin; the control's 0% is what shows the mechanism touched nothing else, and §17.285 (2b)'s "both cells" is corrected here, not met by a contract mechanism, because none exists for a program without a contract. On the target, the mechanism's bucket is exhausted: the bracket was 9.3% of the count and the landed change removed 9.5–10.2% of it (the extra is the elided `rt_take_defect` tests); the one bracket left wraps a call that can raise and is correct; so under §17.218's rule (a fix lands when it moves its bucket; a lane closes when its bucket is empty) the two small sizes' 0.2–0.5% shortfall against the 10% figure is recorded in the row as a shortfall, not rounded up and not chased with an unrelated mechanism. The row reads **closed, exit met on the bucket, 10% met at n ≥ 10^5**. `exec.rs` is free; `lower.rs` and `func.rs` pass to (2) and (3). What remains of `contracts` against hand JS (61× at n = 10^6 against 2.7× on the JS backend) is the cost of boxed scalars and reference counting in `List.all`'s loop, read at WS-W9 and WS-W7, not a contract cost. **(2) WS-W8 opens: a `Unit` join parameter stays `Unit`.** `local_reprs` keeps a `Unit` join parameter `Unit` unless some jump passes it a word: an optimistic fixpoint over the def's blocks (every `Unit` parameter starts `Unit`; a jump whose argument's representation is not `Unit` demotes the parameter to `Word`; a demoted parameter is itself an argument elsewhere, so iterate until nothing changes; a `Unit` local bound to a managed binding stays `Word` as now). A `Unit` parameter is then neither boxed at the jump nor dropped at the loop head. Files: `sakura_lir/src/lower.rs`; `sakura_codegen_wasm/src/func.rs` only if the emitter cannot carry a `Unit` join parameter as it carries a `Unit` local; the LIR print snapshots; `bench_counters.txt`; ABI.md errata L8 at the next PATCH ("a `Unit` join parameter that some jump feeds a word"); `bench/deltas.md`. Exit, under the bucket rule: `boxes` and `drops` in `bench_counters.txt` fall by one per loop iteration on every `while` program, the expected counts read by hand on `contracts_plain` n = 1,000 and recorded in the row; every LIR snapshot diff reviewed one by one and each a join parameter changing representation, nothing else; every `expect-defect` fixture, `--no-direct`, trace parity and the native corpus green; the counted compare against the blessed file `ok` with `contracts_plain` and `contracts` read (about −4.5% and −7.4% expected) and no Node cell flagged without a named reason. **§17.265 (6)'s 10% is not WS-W8's gate**: a representation erratum closing (a `Unit` that was a word) lands under §17.218's bucket rule when the box and the drop per iteration go to zero, as WS-W1 and WS-W2 landed on `frames`; the delta is counted and recorded. **(3) WS-W9 opens: the decrement in place.** Compiled code's `Drop` of a word tests inline what `object.rs`'s `counted` tests (`is_ptr`, the `STATIC` flag in the header's flag byte) and whether `rc > 1`, and when all three hold stores `rc − 1` at offset 4; otherwise it calls the `drop` export as now (the export keeps `dec` and `release`). ABI.md changes, all PATCH: §3.1 or §7 gains the sentence "compiled code may decrement a counted object's `rc` in place while it is above 1; the `drop` export performs the last decrement and the release"; **§10's `drops` is redefined** as "reference-count decrements compiled code asked for (`Drop` of a counted word, in place or through the `drop` export) and the host's calls of the export", the mirror of `dups`' wording, so the counter keeps its meaning and its value: for every fixed execution `stats()` returns the same `drops` as before. Opus chooses how the in-place decrements are counted (an exported mutable `i64` global the `stats` export adds in, one `global.get`/`add`/`global.set` per in-place drop, is the expected shape; a hunk in `heap.rs`'s `Stats` is one line and goes through §17.285 (1)'s rule, `heap.rs` being WS-W6's). Files: `sakura_codegen_wasm/src/func.rs`, `runtime/rt/src/exports.rs` and the `stats` export, ABI.md §3.1/§7/§10, `bench/deltas.md`; native unchanged (it calls `sakura_drop`; the in-place form reaches native with N3's reuse tokens, where the rc test already exists). Exit: `bench_counters.txt` byte-identical before and after (the proof that `drops` and `dups` kept their meaning; a changed cell is a bug, not a regeneration), `reuse_and_borrow_counters_reconcile_by_hand` and the §7.5 cycle and lifetime tests green, every `expect-defect` fixture, `--no-direct` and trace parity; the counted compare `ok` with `contracts_plain` down at least 10% on Node counts (−13.5% measured), `contracts` read, every other Node cell that moves listed in the row with its direction, none flagged worse without a named reason. Order: WS-W8 then WS-W9, the WS-W5 agent in its worktree, each its own commit and counted compare against the same blessed file (not summed, §17.285 (5)); WS-W8 is small and lands first so WS-W9's compare reads loops that no longer drop a `Unit`. **(4) `cx::wasm::rt()` is WS-W3's first fix, and WS-W3's fix opens now.** The 1,376-byte frame is the `wasm::rt` bucket's mechanism, attributed by Opus's measurement, so §17.218's wait for attribution of that bucket is over (the `arena_obj` bucket's attribution is still Astra's and still owed, and does not hold this); WS-W5 is out of `exec.rs`, so §17.285 (3)'s trigger has fired. `runtime/rt/src/cx.rs` joins WS-W3's file set. First commit: the initialisation moved behind a `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` path, so the fast path is a load and a test; then §17.218's order (one `rt()` per step, the frame resolved once per step, the free list). Exit as WS-W3's row: each commit with the `perf` bucket before and after on the twelve-call protocol and all-frame `fib` 2× faster as the row's acceptance, plus the counted compare for each commit (the −3.2% on `contracts_plain` is recorded, not a gate; a fix that does not move its bucket is not landed). It takes the first implementer line that frees, ahead of §17.285 (4)'s N2; WS-P17's `find` hunk in `exec.rs` and WS-W3's are different hunks, keep both. WS-W4 after WS-W3 and WS-W7 after WS-W6 and WS-P21 as before. **(5) A perf row names its target cell and its control when it opens**, and §17.265 (6)'s 10% reads the target; a control that moves is a finding. The open rows are re-read so: WS-W6's target is `tokenizer` n = 100,000 and its slope, its control the smaller sizes' ratio to hand JS; WS-W7's targets `sieve`, `nbody`, `spectral_norm`. Why: a plain twin is in the suite to show what a contract costs, so a change to contracts that leaves it at 0% did exactly what it should, and asking it to fall was the designer's error, not the lane's; a bucket measured at 9.3% and removed is a finished mechanism, and a 0.5% shortfall against a round number at two sizes is reported, not rounded; the three arms are three mechanisms in three file sets, so they are three rows, each with the exit its mechanism admits (a counter going to zero, a counter staying identical, a `perf` bucket moving), because one lane with three exits would land on whichever moved; `drops` must keep counting what compiled code asked for or N3's and N4's reconciliation reads a number whose meaning moved under it; and the `rt()` frame is a WS-W3 fact found by WS-W5, so it goes to the row that owns the bucket. Rejected: keeping WS-W5 open for arm (a) so `contracts` passes 10% at every size (a loop's `Unit` is not a contract, and the lane's attribution would be muddied by a second mechanism); reading `contracts_plain` out of WS-W5's row (it stays as the control, and its 0% is in the ledger); letting `drops` count only the calls that reach the export after WS-W9 (a counter whose meaning changes with an optimisation reconciles nothing); counting in-place drops nowhere (the counters are deterministic for a fixed execution and `bench_counters.txt` is the corpus that proves it); a `--counters` build (two builds, two truths); the inline immediate test before `drop` as arm (a)'s fix (it treats the symptom at every call; the representation is the cause); carrying the inline decrement to native now (M5's rows own the native rc path); a fourth row for `List.all`'s loop (WS-W9 and WS-W7 are its mechanisms). Performance: WS-W8 removes one box and one `drop` call per `while` iteration on WASM; WS-W9 makes every non-final `Drop` a load, a compare and a store; WS-W3's first fix takes the 1,376-byte prologue off every runtime call; none changes a program's result, a defect record or a counter's value. 288. **Phase 7b (`std/crypto` tier 1b, `d401d073` vectors, `2a12eee4`) stands as built on JS and native: ECDSA is P-256 with SHA-256 only, `r || s`; `sign` keeps `Random` in its row and the backends keep their nonces (RFC 6979 on native, OpenSSL's on JS), signatures compared through `verify` only; an AES-GCM nonce is 12 bytes; `kind: KeyKind` and the private material as scalar or seed followed by the public point; imports read only the DER forms `export_key` writes; the new variants are 0.2.0's, so tier 2's are too (7c before the 0.2.0 preparation commit or outside 1.0); `rt`'s key copies are zeroed in one `fix(rt)` commit before 7b-W, the heap's hygiene is an M5 row; the `import_key` reachability cost is accepted and measured once; THIRD_PARTY.md gains the nine crypto crates and a test that keeps it complete; 7b-W starts now at ABI 1.9.0 and phase 10 takes 1.10.0; §17.286 (9)'s 4 KiB step is confirmed as the data segment crossing a run, not a leak, and `live_objects` stands; an operation used as a function value blames its clause with no call-site span, as a contracted def used as a value does (RFC 0002 §2.7, §5, §6, §Compatibility amended; plan `web-apis.md` §2, phase 7b, 7b-W, 7c, §4; `m5-native.md` §2; `tests/wasm.rs`; §17.115, §17.263 (2), §17.266 (1), (7), (10), §17.270 (1), §17.285 (2d), §17.286 (8), (9), (12); round 42, 2026-10-21).** Facts: the REQUESTS entry of 2026-10-21 lists seven readings. `Algorithm` gains `AesGcm(Aes128 | Aes256)`, `Ecdsa(P256)`, `Ecdh(P256)`, `Ed25519`, `X25519`; `Usage` gains `Encrypt | Decrypt`; `KeyFormat` gains `Pkcs8 | Spki | Jwk`; `CryptoKey` gains `kind: KeyKind = SecretKey | PublicKey | PrivateKey` read by `crypto.kind(key)`; `KeyPair = { public, private }` from `generate_key_pair(alg, usages, extractable) ! {Random}`; `DeriveParams` gains `EcdhWith(CryptoKey)`; `KeyReason` gains `Format(KeyFormat) | Malformed`; `CryptoReason` gains `Nonce(Int) | Tag | ZeroSecret`; `encrypt`/`decrypt(key, nonce, aad, data)`; `sign(key, data) ! {Random}` for HMAC, ECDSA and Ed25519. `sign` draws from `Random` on neither backend: `crypto_sign` on native is `p256`'s RFC 6979 (the `rt` test matches RFC 6979 §A.2.5 byte for byte) and on JS `node:crypto`'s `sign` with `dsaEncoding: "ieee-p1363"`, whose nonce is OpenSSL's generator; Node offers neither RFC 6979 nor a caller-supplied nonce, so a deterministic JS signature means P-256 scalar arithmetic in Sakura or JS, a second ECDSA to review; key generation does draw from `Random` in std (`private_scalar`: `Random.bytes(32)`, retried on P-256 while not below the order), so a pair under `Random.seeded` is the same bytes on every backend, which `crypto_generate_under_seeded_random_is_deterministic` pins; RFC §2.7 and §5 already declare randomized signatures as one of the two determinism exceptions. `aes-gcm` 0.11.1 is 96-bit-nonce only; Web Crypto takes any nonce length. The material layout is read by `private_part` (the first 32 bytes) and never leaves the module: `CryptoKey` is opaque, has no `Show` or `Schema`, and `export_key` writes `Raw` as the scalar or the point, never the concatenation. SPKI and PKCS #8 are fixed DER prefixes compared by `strip` (`spki_prefix`, `p256_pkcs8_head`/`mid`/`bare`, `pkcs8_25519`), the forms Web Crypto writes; P-256 PKCS #8 is read with and without its public key; other valid encodings (compressed points, PKCS #8 v2 with the public key, other parameter forms) are `Malformed`; JWK is written in member order with `ext` and `key_ops` and read with `Json.parse`, checking `kty`, `crv`, `alg` (secret keys), `key_ops` (every usage asked for), `ext` (`false` refuses an extractable import), ignoring `use`. P-256 points are checked on the curve and scalars in `1..n` on both backends; Ed25519 and X25519 public keys are any 32 bytes as Web Crypto imports them; Ed25519 `verify` is dalek's cofactorless `verify`, OpenSSL's check; a small-order X25519 peer is `ZeroSecret` (`was_contributory`; Node refuses it). ECDH and X25519 `derive_bits` take at most 256 bits. A public key may only `Verify` (ECDH and X25519 public keys nothing), `NoUsages` applies to secret and private keys, and `generate_key_pair` with a usage the algorithm lacks is `D020` like `generate_key`. An exhaustive `match` over `Algorithm`, `Usage`, `KeyFormat`, `KeyReason` or `CryptoReason` written against v0.1.0 no longer compiles; RFC 0002 §Compatibility says 0.1.0 precedes RFC 0001's compatibility start, 0.2.0 is the one breaking window before 1.0, and after 0.2.0 "only additive modules and additive functions" land before the rc; tier 2 (phase 7c: `RsaOaep`, `RsaPss`, `RsassaPkcs1`, `P384`, `P521`, `AesCbc`, `AesCtr`, `AesKw`) adds variants to `Algorithm` and `Curve` and is "optional before the rc". On native, `rt::crypto`'s `take_bytes` copies each argument's bytes into a `Vec<u8>` (`data_bytes(b).to_vec()`) and drops the Sakura object; the `Vec` and every derived `Vec` (a shared secret, a scalar, a plaintext) are freed unzeroed, as in 7a; the Sakura heap `Bytes` that `reveal` and `Bytes.slice` make from a key's `Secret<Bytes>` are freed by `heap.rs` unzeroed on native and WASM, and a JS `Buffer` cannot be zeroed by the program; §17.270 (1) zeroed every copy a kind-`secret` import's encoder frees on WASM, and `zeroize` 1.9.1 is in `Cargo.lock` as the dalek crates' dependency; the 7a entry did not raise `take_bytes`, so §17.266 ruled nothing on it; REQUESTS 426's reading stands that memory hygiene is hygiene under the trust model and the contract is that a key reaches no text, log or cassette. Reachability is per def: `import_key`'s `match format` reaches `decode`'s four readers, so a program that imports a `Raw` HMAC key carries the DER prefixes and the JWK reader (the commit: "the larger reachable std code behind `import_key`"; no byte count recorded); the alternative is four import functions, a shape change. `sakura_host_native/THIRD_PARTY.md` (N0a) lists the native toolchain's seventeen direct crates with unmodified upstream notices under `third-party/`, says "this skeleton ships no release artifact", and lists none of 7a's four (`sha2`, `hmac`, `hkdf`, `pbkdf2`, MIT OR Apache-2.0) or 7b's four (`aes-gcm`, `p256` MIT OR Apache-2.0; `ed25519-dalek`, `x25519-dalek` BSD-3-Clause), nor `curve25519-dalek` 5.0.0, BSD-3-Clause and transitive through both; BSD-3-Clause requires its notice in binary distributions; §17.266 (10) made the licence list in the commit the owner's 7a review input, which is not the notices file; no `cargo deny`-style check exists in the workspace; `release.yml` ships no native binary (native is experimental and off the tag gates, §17.245 (2)). 7b is on `main` and phase 6 is not, so of §17.286 (12)'s two candidates for MINOR 1.9.0 only 7b-W is ready; ABI §0 forbids a skipped number; the eight tier-1b fixtures are `KNOWN` rows in `parity.rs` and the corpus test, and `INDEX.md`, the skill and the capabilities tour carry the "waits" sentences. Decision: **(1) ECDSA is P-256 with SHA-256, ratified.** The hash is fixed by the curve (JOSE `ES256`; Web Crypto's `hash` parameter is not offered), the signature is `r || s`, 64 bytes; a second curve, if 7c lands, fixes its own hash the same way (`P384` SHA-384, `P521` SHA-512), so `sign` never grows a parameter. **(2) `sign` keeps `Random`, and the backends keep their nonces, ratified.** The row says the one true thing about the operation: its output is not a function of its inputs. A signature's bytes are compared through `verify` on every backend and in every fixture, and nothing prints one (plan §4); the doc comment stays as written. JS is not made deterministic: Node has no RFC 6979 and takes no nonce, so determinism there is a second ECDSA implementation in Sakura or JS, which is more to review than a declared difference, and RFC §5 already declares it. Native's determinism is not a contract either: a hedged nonce (RFC 6979 §3.6's extra entropy from `Random.bytes(32)`) may replace it without a signature change, and is the first use the `Random` row is reserved for. Key generation under `Random.seeded` is the same bytes on every backend and stays so. **(3) A 12-byte nonce, ratified.** `Nonce(n)` for any other length, checked in Sakura before the primitive on every backend; `aes-gcm`'s bound is the lowest host's, and §17.266 (7)'s rule makes it the contract; RFC §6 gains the row. A longer nonce (GHASH-derived) is a different construction with a worse bound, not a feature withheld. **(4) `kind` and the material layout, ratified.** `KeyKind` is Web Crypto's `type` and `crypto.kind(key)` reads it; the private material as scalar-or-seed followed by the public point is a std-private layout under an opaque type, so it is not a contract and the RFC does not state it; `export_key` writes `Raw` as the scalar or the point as now, and that is the contract. **(5) Imports read only the DER forms `export_key` writes, ratified.** One accepted encoding per form is the smallest parser; the forms are the ones Web Crypto and OpenSSL's defaults write, so interoperation holds, and `Malformed` names everything else. Reading a further encoding later is additive (nothing that imported before stops importing), so it waits for a program that needs it, named in a REQUESTS entry with the producer. (4)'s validation rules, the 256-bit ECDH bound, the usages by half and the JWK rules are ratified as read. **(6) The new variants are 0.2.0's, confirmed, and tier 2's are too.** 0.1.0 precedes the compatibility start and 0.2.0 is the one breaking window, so the five sums grow now without a migration note beyond the changelog's. The consequence: after 0.2.0 a variant added to a `pub` std sum is not an "additive function" under RFC §Compatibility, since an exhaustive `match` stops compiling; so **7c is no longer "optional before the rc": it lands before the 0.2.0 preparation commit or its variants are not in 1.0** (a tier 2 after 1.0 is a new module name or the next breaking window). Phase 7c's row and heading read so. **(7) `rt`'s key copies are zeroed, one `fix(rt)` commit, now.** Every `Vec<u8>` `take_bytes` makes and every derived `Vec` in `rt::crypto` (a scalar, a point's private input, a shared secret, a plaintext, a digest state's input) is zeroed before it is freed: `zeroize` (already in the lock through the dalek crates, no new entry, `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`) or a ten-line `Drop` guard, Opus's choice; a `rt` test that a freed copy's bytes read zero is not possible safely, so the test is that `take_bytes` returns the wrapper type and the review reads each `Vec`; the commit cites this entry and goes in the web lane before 7b-W, in `crypto.rs` only. The heap's hygiene is larger than 7b: a Sakura `Bytes` holding revealed material is freed unzeroed on native and WASM, and JS cannot zero at all; it opens as row **N-S** in `m5-native.md` §2 (zero-on-free for a `Bytes` made from a `Secret`'s reveal, or a `Secret<Bytes>` that never materialises a plain `Bytes`: `reveal` in `std/crypto` is the one site), read at the 1.0 security review with the owner, not dated, not a 7b or 7b-W gate: the contract (RFC §2.7: no text, log or cassette carries a key) is met, and what remains is hygiene under the trust model. **(8) `import_key`'s reachability cost is accepted; measured once.** A key format is an argument, so the four readers are reachable from one function, and the price is std Sakura code (a few DER prefixes and a JWK reader) paid once by a program that imports keys at all; four import functions would change the RFC's shape for a number no one has read. Opus records the number once, in the REQUESTS entry's answer line: the emitted WASM module's bytes and the JS bundle's bytes for `crypto_hmac_rfc4231` at `2a12eee4` against its parent. No row: if a constant-argument specialisation (a `match` on a literal argument pruned at the call site) is ever worth building, it is a perf-lane item over every std function, not a crypto one, and the number is its first evidence. **(9) THIRD_PARTY.md: the Opus fix.** One `docs(native)` commit, now, in the web lane: nine rows, `sha2` 0.11.1, `hmac` 0.13.0, `hkdf` 0.13.0, `pbkdf2` 0.13.0, `aes-gcm` 0.11.1, `p256` 0.14.0, `ed25519-dalek` 3.0.0, `x25519-dalek` 3.0.0 and `curve25519-dalek` 5.0.0 (the notice obligation follows the licence, not the direct pin, so the transitive BSD-3-Clause crate has a row), each with its upstream licence file unmodified under `third-party/<crate>/` (the BSD files carry the copyright line, which is the notice); the header's "this skeleton ships no release artifact" rewritten to the fact (the native runtime is experimental, off the tag gates, and `release.yml` ships no native binary; the file is what a binary distribution ships beside it); and **a test is the gate**: a `sakura_host_native` test reads `THIRD_PARTY.md` and asserts a row for every optional dependency of `runtime/rt`'s `native` feature and every dependency of `sakura_host_native` (the two `Cargo.toml` files parsed by hand, no new crate), so a third miss is red. The owner's 7b review as security reviewer covers the crate set (§17.266 (10)'s form) and is recorded as a dated line under the REQUESTS entry, as phase 8's was. **(10) 7b-W starts now at ABI 1.9.0; phase 10 takes 1.10.0 after 7b-W lands.** §17.286 (12) named the first ready of the two, and 7b-W is the one on `main`'s side; the step is 7a-W's shape: the seven new `crypto_*` builtins as `hosted` imports in `sakura_lir::image::WASM_HOSTED`, `sakura_wasm_host.js` and `validate.rs`, ABI.md §0 and §8.2's `crypto_*` line extended at 1.9.0, `sakura_abi_version` `0x010900` on both hosts and `test_bench.py`'s assertion (§17.270 (2)), the guest's argument tuple wiped as the 7a imports' is, the eight `KNOWN` rows in `parity.rs` and the corpus test emptied (the WASI cell keeps its `Host::Wasi`-only rows as 7a-W did) and the three "waits" sentences deleted; one commit, the ABI bump inside it, green on its own base; (7) lands before it in the same lane. Phase 10 follows phase 6 at 1.10.0 (§17.266 (1)). **(11) §17.286 (9) is confirmed: the data segment, not a leak; `live_objects` stands.** Facts, from Opus's reading of `a_twin_that_runs_out_of_gauge_restarts_once_per_entry` (`32419806` and `ddeba41f` are the lane's fix commits so far; Windows CI green): the code table is not the cause, it is 3,208 bytes in both runs; the whole data segment of the `applied` program is 4,192 bytes in direct style against 3,888 under `--no-direct`, so direct style crosses one more 4 KiB run, and the growth is the twin table plus the twin statics; `live` net of the runs is 960 bytes in both (9,152 − 8,192 = 5,056 − 4,096) and `live_objects` is 8 in both; on `mapped` the segment stays under 4 KiB both ways and `live` matches at 1,056,960. The mechanism §17.286 (9) described (a static segment held as heap blocks crossing a run boundary) is the one found; the component it named, the code table, was wrong, and the data segment is the right name. The ratification applies: an object count is the invariant, and the 960-byte equality above the runs is the second proof. The test's doc comment is updated to this text, verbatim: "objects, not bytes: under the host tests the data segment (the layout and code tables, the twin table and the twin statics) is held as heap blocks rounded up to 4 KiB runs, and twins make it larger. Confirmed (design §17.286 (9), §17.288 (11)): on `applied` the code table is 3,208 bytes in both runs and the whole segment is 4,192 bytes in direct style against 3,888 under `--no-direct`, so direct style crosses one more run; `live` reads 9,152 against 5,056, the bytes above the runs are 960 in both (9,152 − 8,192 = 5,056 − 4,096) and `live_objects` is 8 in both; on `mapped` the segment stays under 4 KiB both ways and `live` matches at 1,056,960." No assertion is added on the segment's size (the test would then pin a layout). **(12) An operation used as a function value blames its clause only, acceptable, not a follow-up.** §17.115 already rules that a call through a function value carries `$site = −1`, so a contracted def called as a value reports `D020` with the clause span and no call-site span; `32419806` gives an operation as a value (`let f = Random.int`) the same reading inside its wrapper. One rule for defs and operations is the right shape; a site through a value would need the site threaded into every closure call, which §17.115 rejected for defs. The fixture that pins it, if the lane has none, is one `expect-defect: D020` program calling an operation through a `let`-bound value, identical on three backends and in `--json`; a doc sentence in §7.2's paragraph: "through a function value, the clause span only, as for a def". Why: every reading keeps the RFC's rule where it had one (the determinism exception, the lowest host's bound, the opaque key) and the smallest surface where it had none (one DER form per key, `Random` as a declared fact rather than a drawn one); the variant rule is RFC 0002's own compatibility text read to its consequence for 7c, said now so the window is not found closed later; a zeroed `Vec` is ten lines in one file and the kind of fix §17.267 (2) lands without waiting, while the heap's hygiene is a design across three backends that the security review should read whole; a notices file that a test keeps complete costs less than the third omission. Rejected: deterministic ECDSA on JS by a Sakura or JS implementation of P-256 (a second signing implementation to review for a byte equality no caller may rely on); dropping `Random` from `sign`'s row (the hedged nonce would then be a row change, which §17.286's rule makes a 0.2.0 item or never); a `nonce_len` parameter or Web Crypto's any-length GCM nonce (a weaker bound for interoperation no one asked for); stating the material layout in the RFC (an opaque type's inside is not a contract); a lenient DER reader (every accepted encoding is parser surface, and `Malformed` is a clear answer); declaring tier 2's variants in 0.2.0 ahead of 7c with `Unsupported` (variants that do nothing on every backend); a `#[non_exhaustive]`-like attribute for std sums (a language feature for one module's schedule); zero-on-free in `heap.rs` for every block (a cost on every free for a hygiene property the trust model does not promise; N-S reads the narrow form first); `zeroize` as a new direct pin for the guard alone (it is already in the lock; if Opus writes the guard by hand, no manifest line moves); four `import_*` functions (a shape change for an unmeasured size); a size budget for std reachability (no row without a number); listing only direct pins in THIRD_PARTY.md (the obligation is the licence's); a `cargo deny` dependency for the check (a workspace tool for one table). Performance: (3) and (5) are comparisons already made; (7) one `fill` per freed copy in a crypto call, the copies being key-sized; (8) is measured, not changed; nothing else runs. Changed: RFC 0002 §2.7 (tier 1b's shapes, `kind`, `KeyPair`, `generate_key_pair`, ECDSA as ES256, the DER and JWK rule, the `Random` sentence), §6 (the nonce and ECDH rows), §Compatibility (the variants in 0.2.0; 7c's deadline), §Metadata (phase 7b); `web-apis.md` §2 (7b landed, 7b-W now at 1.9.0, phase 10 at 1.10.0, 7c's row), phase 7b (landed paragraph), phase 7b-W and 7c; `m5-native.md` §2 (row N-S); `compiler/REQUESTS.md` (the 2026-10-21 entry answered); §7.2 (the function-value sentence); the §17 heading's intro. Impact: Opus, the web lane, in order: the `tests/wasm.rs` doc comment of (11) and (12)'s fixture if missing, in the lane's next small commit; (7) `fix(rt)`; (9) `docs(native)` with its test; 7b-W at 1.9.0 with (8)'s two numbers in the REQUESTS answer line; then 7c's deadline is in its row. The owner: the 7b crate-set review, one dated line under the REQUESTS entry; N-S at the 1.0 security review. Sol: phase 12 for tier 1b (the stdlib page's `kind`, `KeyPair` and the nonce sentence).
