296. **Phase 10 (`std/channel`, `Stream.buffer`/`tee`, `784532f0`, ABI 1.12.0) stands as built: `with_channel` is the name (RFC 0002 §2.9 corrected), the nine readings are ratified, the JS scheduler's synchronous fiber end and its `D090` on a drained event loop pass named-maintainer review, a view handed to a `buffer`/`tee`/`decompress_source` body that escapes it is documented as `Done` and is not a beta gate, and the two `D090` test exemptions stand with one beta.N item that removes them (RFC 0002 §2.9 and its §6 rows; §6.3; §8.4; §8.6; §17.280 (2), (4); §17.284 (1); §17.289 (11); §17.291; §17.292; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` the phase-10 entry; round 48, 2026-10-21; owner's delegation while asleep).** Facts, from reading `784532f0`, not its list. *Name:* `with` is `WITH_KW` (`syntax_kind.rs` 253), the handler form `with H { … }`, so `Channel.with` is `V0001` after `fn` or `.`; `Fs.with_file` (`fs.sak` 40) is the module's precedent for a scoped callback named `with_<noun>`; the site (`tour/concurrency.mdx` 131–138), the stdlib page, the skill and the changelog already teach `channel.with_channel`; RFC §2.9 and a row of its §6 table still write `Channel.with`. *Rows:* `channel.sak` 31–58 as the entry lists them; `send`'s `Full` case is dead by construction (JS `channel_send` only calls `channel_try_send` when `closed || items.length < cap`; rt `channel_send` waits otherwise), so `send` answers `Ok` or `Err(Closed)` only. *Scheduler, JS* (`sakura_runtime.js` 370–380, 428–450, 4059–4100, 4146–4198): `t.done` is called from exactly one place per fiber — `startFiber` when `runTask` returns an outcome, else the `resumeLater` whose `drive` returned an outcome rather than another promise (a re-suspension resolves the outer promise with the inner one and calls nothing); inside `t.done` the order is outcome stored, `parent.kids` pruned, the group's `onDone`, then the waiters resolved in push order, each a microtask, which is `finish_task`'s enqueue-at-the-back in wait order; `onDone` may cancel siblings synchronously, whose `wake` runs a nested `drive` with `T.t` saved and restored and whose own `t.done` re-enters `onDone`, guarded by `s.failed !== null` (`scope`) and `winner !== null` (`race`/`all`); `cancel` now always resumes one hop later, even when `cancelTask` ended the fiber synchronously, which is one hop more than before and what rt does for the canceller; `joinAll` counts down, `race`'s `decided` resolves on the first end with `winner` already set. *`D090` on JS:* `beforeExit` fires only when the loop holds no handle; every host wait in the runtime holds one (timers, sockets, stdin, the `setImmediate` of `virtualTick` and `yield`), a channel wait holds none, so the record fires only when every task waits on a channel or on a fiber that does; `once` plus the `settled` flag make it fire at most once; the pending `o.then` never runs; the message is the hosts' "every task is waiting", exit 70; no finalizer runs, as on WASM and native, where the hosts end the run with the tasks blocked. *Channel, both runtimes:* a woken sender re-tests under the same condition it waited on, so it never answers `Full`; a woken receiver that finds the queue taken waits again at the back; a cancelled waiter leaves its list (JS: `suspend`'s cancel callback; rt: the epoch test in `wake_waiter`); `channel_with`'s finalizer empties then closes, so a body's cancellation wakes every waiter; rt's `T_BLOCKED` is counted up in `wait_here` and down in `wake_waiter`, state `BLOCKED` tested first. *The `V6003` gap:* §17.284 (1) found the escape check reaches a view in four shapes, every one a closure that visibly captured a value of a `@resource` type; `buffer`'s body receives `received(rx)` already built, typed `Source<T, {Task | e}>`, which holds no resource type, so the check has nothing to see, exactly phase 6's item 2 (`decompress_source`, `compress_source`); an escaped `received` view pulls `recv` on a channel that the finalizer closed and emptied and gets `None`, so `Done`, on every backend; a stricter check later would refuse programs beta.1 accepts. *Exemptions:* `corpus.rs` 130–136 ignores the object and counter delta only when the outcome is `Defect 90` with the exact message, and still requires the second run to end the same way; `native/mod.rs` `task_free` returns early on an unfinished root task, so the blocked tasks of a `D090` run stay in the arena until the instance drops. Decision: **(1) `with_channel` stays.** The name follows `with_file`, the site and the skill already teach it, and the stutter in `channel.with_channel` is the cost of a keyword the handler form owns; admitting `with` after `.` or `fn` (a contextual keyword) is rejected inside the last window, and `Channel.open` is rejected (`open` promises a handle to close; this is a scope). RFC 0002 §2.9 and its §6 `MessageChannel` row now name `channel.with_channel`, with one sentence on why. No code change. **(2) The nine readings are ratified as built**, each a contract of beta.1: (2) `with_channel<T, R, e>(capacity, body) -> R ! {Task | e}` `requires capacity > 0` (no rendezvous; relaxing a `requires` is additive, so a capacity-0 handoff can arrive in 1.x if a program needs one); `send -> Result<Unit, SendError> ! {Task}`, `Err(Closed)` before or while waiting and never `Full` (the shared `SendError` is kept: one type for both sends, the dead case documented, as it is); `try_send` and `close` carry `Task` (a pure call may be dropped or reordered by Core, and both change shared state); `close` on the `Sender` only, a second close a no-op; no byte bound (items are not serialized; `chunks` bounds bytes before `buffer`, §17.280 (4)). (3) The callback's end closes and empties; an end an outer fiber still holds reads `Err(Closed)`/`None`. (4) `buffer`/`tee` under `Task.all`, a failure on either side the result, the producer stopping at its next send, a pull in progress finishing first, `body` under `{Task | e}` only, `tee` sending to the first channel then the second. (6) `D090` on all three backends. (8) wake-all with retry, in wait order. (9) ABI 1.12.0 under §17.289 (11). **(3) The escaped-view gap is documented, not gated.** The observable is `Done` and nothing else: no resource outlives its callback (the channel is closed and emptied by the finalizer; a codec state is released by RC or GC), no backend differs, nothing is unsafe. §17.280 (2)'s `V6003` sentence is read as what the checker proves: a view whose closure captured a value of a `@resource` type cannot leave the callback that introduced the resource; a view a std callback hands its body (`buffer`, `tee`, `decompress_source`, `compress_source`) is scoped by contract and is `Done` once the callback returns, which `stream.sak`'s `buffer` doc already says; the stdlib page and the tour say the same in one sentence each, in Sol's next docs commit. A checker rule that refuses the escape would be a stricter check on programs beta.1 accepts, so it is not a beta.N item; if dogfood shows programs doing it, a *warning* (`W6xxx`, additive) on a body that returns or stores its scoped parameter is the 1.x shape, and it needs a marker the type can carry, which is an RFC. **(4) The JS scheduler change is approved** (named-maintainer review, delegated): the single-delivery property, the `onDone` re-entrancy guards, the one-hop rule for every waiter and the `beforeExit` record hold as read above; the parity fixtures (`stream_buffer_propagates_failure` now one trace on three backends, every existing `task_*` fixture unchanged) are the evidence that the hop count matches rt's run queue. Two facts recorded, not changed: a host handle that is `unref`'d before its operation can complete would let `beforeExit` report `D090` on a run that was not stuck, and none of the runtime's waits does so today (`wsEnd` unrefs after `end`, when `ws_receive` already answers `Closed`); `cancel`'s extra hop is observable only through interleaving, which the fixtures cover. **(5) The two exemptions stand for beta.1; one beta.N item removes them.** The corpus exemption is keyed to the exact `D090` message and still demands the same ending twice, so a leak in any other outcome fails as before; one fixture takes it. Beta.N, `native/mod.rs` and `exec.rs`, not a tag gate: `Instance::task_free` on an unfinished root task cancels it first (`cancel_all`'s unwind: its finalizers run, its blocked waiters leave their lists by epoch) and then frees it, so a `D090` run leaves nothing in the arena and `corpus.rs` drops the `stuck` clause; acceptance is `channel_recv_every_task_waiting` passing the unchanged leak check on native, every other corpus row unchanged. The JS side needs nothing (the process exits). Why: the name question is cosmetic and the precedent decides it; the readings are the conservative ones and each was checked against the code, not the list; the gap is a promise the docs already stopped making, and a check that cannot see a type has no business guessing; the scheduler change removes a cross-target difference by making JS do what rt does, and the review found its invariants explicit in the code; the exemptions are narrow and the fix that removes them is small and belongs in the embedding API. Rejected: a grammar change for `with`; `Channel.open`; a `send` that returns `Bool` or `Result<Unit, Closed>` (the RFC's type, one `SendError`); unwinding every task's finalizers on `D090` (a run with no runnable task has no task to blame; the three backends agree today, and changing it is a semantic change inside the window for no reported need); making the view escape a `V6003` before the tag (no marker exists, and a stricter check after beta.1 is breaking); a `Full` answer from `send` after a lost race (neither runtime can produce it). Performance: none of this changes code. Changed: this entry; RFC 0002 §2.9 (the name, one sentence) and its §6 `MessageChannel` row; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` (the answer under the phase-10 entry); the §17 heading. Impact: nobody before the tag. Opus, beta.N: (5)'s `task_free`. Sol: (3)'s one sentence on the stdlib page and the tour with the next docs commit. The owner: nothing waits; an objection to any verdict before the tag is one revert.
297. **Lane B's five `v1.0.0-beta.1` riders (`0cd14c67` WP-6, `7d789964` RQ-3, `ad2e8612` WP-5, `b8f416f8` RQ-5, `4020b9b1` RQ-6) reviewed against §17.294 at the owner's delegation: four stand as built with their flagged deviations ratified (`Http.scoped`'s refusal names `host:port`, `error` lexes as an identifier after `.` and before `:`, an invalid character at a line's end ends its statement, `ok_json` keeps its own body); a diagnostic for a binder named `error` and a one-record recovery for an anonymous record literal are beta.N (§17.294 RQ-3, RQ-5, RQ-6, SS-15, WP-5, WP-6; `compiler/REQUESTS.md`'s lane-B entry; round 49, 2026-10-21).** Facts, read at the diffs: `allowed` (`http.sak` lines 246–250) refuses with `host_port(req.url)`, the shape the manifest refusal uses; `error_field_names` (`lexer.rs`) retags `ERROR_KW` to `IDENT` after a `DOT` or before a `COLON`, so `fn f(error: String)`, a lambda parameter and `let error: T = …` now parse while a use of `error` in a body is still the keyword; `hole_error` emits one `ERROR_TOKEN` for the literal and `ERROR_TOKEN` joined `ends_statement`, and the three records the design-15.7 snapshot lost were `V0002 unterminated string literal`, `V0001 expected `}`` and `V0001 expected `]``, the cascade of the one byte; `report_unused_imports` marks a name used when a lookup resolves to its import binding and a bare module import used when any lookup reaches an item of that module by any route, the prelude and builtins included; `check_modules` (`sakura_types/tests/common`) drops `W1003`; `offline.py`'s `ORACLE_SHARED = {'W1003'}` exempts the code from both the starter's initial check and the candidate check, because task 07's oracles use `Status`, which only the starter imports; `ok_json`'s body is unchanged beside `status_json`; `error_field_name` and `response_status_json` join the bare-WASM corpus's `KNOWN` with `json_codec`'s reason. Decisions: **(1) SS-15 amended: the scope refusal is `"<host:port> is outside Http.scoped"`.** `<url>` was this log's slip, and the built text is the better one: a URL carries a path, a query and, before `Url.parse` strips them (`url_credentials_are_secret`), credentials, none of which belongs in a reason a log or an LLM transcript carries; `host:port` is what `scoped` checks, so the three refusal reasons share one shape, what was checked rather than what was asked. `http.sak` line 114 already says so; the capabilities page lists the text as built (lane D). **(2) RQ-3 ratified as built, the lexer mechanism included; the widening is accepted for beta.1 and gets a diagnostic in beta.N.** §17.294 said the token stays `ERROR_KW` and the parser admits it where a field name stands; the retag is a fifteen-line position rule with the same observable grammar, item position still dispatches to `error_decl`, and `fmt` prints as written, so no program changes meaning. The widening — `(` and `,` precede a parameter as they precede an error tag's field, so the lexer cannot tell them apart — leaves a binder named `error` parsing with no way to use it: `fn f(error: String) -> Int { 1 }` compiles with a dead parameter and `fn f(error: String) -> String { error }` fails at the use, where 0.1.0 failed at the binder. That is no worse than before and no dogfood wrote one, so it is not a gate. Beta.N: the parser reports `V0016 keyword_binder` (PARSE family, next free after `V0015`), "`error` is a keyword: it names a field, not a binding; choose another name", at a `PARAM`, a lambda parameter, a `let` pattern or a pattern binding whose `IDENT` reads `error`, one `ui` case; the spec's sentence becomes "the keyword `error` is a valid field name and not a binding name". Rejected: retagging only after `{`, `,`, `..` and `(` (a parameter list opens with `(` too); a raw-identifier syntax (§17.294's reason stands). **(3) WP-5 ratified as built: one record is the right count, and `ERROR_TOKEN` ending its statement is what `lib.rs`'s sentence promised.** The 15.7 snapshot's change is the fix, not a loss: the three records that went were cascades of the same byte. One edge is known and unmeasured, beta.N: a line ending in an invalid character whose next line starts with a token that neither continues a statement (`continues_statement`) nor begins one could now report a second record where the `ERROR` node swallowed it; the first shape that shows two records becomes a `ui` case asserting one. **(4) RQ-5: (a) the "used" rule is ratified for beta.1 as the conservative reading.** An imported name is used when a lookup resolves to its import binding, in a value, a type, a pattern or a `@contract_test` attribute (§17.294's list, the fixture's five cases); a bare module import is used when any lookup reaches an item of that module by any route. The strict reading — a module import is used only when a lookup resolves through its own binding — would warn on `import std/env` in a program that reaches `Env` through the prelude; the warning would be true and its fix safe, but it is an additive tightening the beta can take if a dogfood asks, and the one shape `W1003` must never have is a false warning carrying a `MachineApplicable` fix, which the conservative side cannot produce. **(b) `check_modules` dropping `W1003` is ratified**: test scaffolding with shared preambles; the warning is held by `tests/ui/W1003_unused_import` and the three hir snapshots. **(c) The harness exemption is refused as a standing rule and accepted only as the state of `main` until the gate lands.** It loosens the candidate check for every task (a candidate may now leave any import unused, its own additions included), and it does not fix the defect it was for: 07's oracles depend on an import the candidate may legitimately drop, `sakura fix` is in `SAKURA_SUBCOMMANDS`, and `W1003`'s fix is `MachineApplicable`, so an agent that runs `sakura fix` on task 07 removes `Status`, both oracles then fail to compile, and `oracle()`'s `require` turns a correct repair into a harness error rather than a verdict. The fix is the one task 10's `valid.sak` already uses: an oracle imports every name it uses. A same-meaning re-import is silent (`bind_import_name` returns on `prev == b` without a diagnostic) and `import` is an item at any position, so an oracle appended after the candidate's items may import what it needs. **Gate, beta.1, before the preparation commit, for whoever runs the harness next**: (i) `tasks/07-health-route/oracle/{dispatch,health}.sak` open with `import std/request.{Get, Request, Text}`, `import std/response.{Status}`, `import std/router.{Router}` and `import std/url.{Url}`; (ii) task 10's `failure.sak`, `invalid.sak` and `valid.sak` import `Http` and `Response` the same way (the audit of the twelve tasks: 07's and 10's are the only oracles naming a starter import); (iii) 07's `starter`, `gold` and `hollow` `src/main.sak` drop `Status` from `import std/response.{Response, Status}`, and `task.json`'s `starter_files` and `starter_sha256` are re-recorded (`expected_diagnostics` stays `[]`); (iv) `offline.py` drops `ORACLE_SHARED` and both filters, restoring `not any(row.get('code') for row in rows)` and the plain `codes` set, and the README's sentence becomes "an oracle imports every name it uses; a same-meaning re-import is silent"; (v) the offline harness runs end to end (gold 25/25, hollow 0/25) and the 03 fixture is re-recorded by replay if its verdict line changes (its `W1003` tool output is the compiler's true answer and stays). Rejected: narrowing the exemption to the starter's names (masks the `sakura fix` path all the same); the harness merging imports (code for what one line per oracle does). **(5) RQ-6 ratified as built.** `ok_json` keeping its own body beside `status_json` is fine: the comment carries the contract ("the short form of `status_json(200, value)`"), the two bodies are equal by inspection, and a call would route through a `requires` that is always true. The two `KNOWN` rows are ratified with `json_codec`'s reason: a bare corpus module has no type descriptors. **(6) WP-6 ratified as built**, with two readings: the message says `Type { request: …, … }` where §17.294 wrote `Circuit { request: 0, … }`, because the checker does not know the type the author meant and the design's example was the dogfood's; and the fixture's five `V0009` after each `name:` are the parser's cascade for a shape it does not model, seven records for a two-field literal — beta.N, ranked below (2)'s diagnostic: a parser recovery that takes `name: …` up to the next `,` or `}` as one statement, so a k-field anonymous literal is k `V1002` and nothing else. Changes: this entry; the §17 heading; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` (the answer under the lane-B entry). `Gen.flat_map` is `Gen { sample: fn(size) { f(g.sample(size)).sample(size) } }` with a `for_all` test and a seeded fixture that prints the same samples twice. `Fs.read_up_to` (`fs.sak`) is `with_file` over `read_chunk` with `requires limit >= 0`: the first read asks `Int.min(65_535, limit) + 1`, every later one `Int.min(65_535, limit - n) + 1`, so the total read is at most `limit + 1` bytes in chunks of at most 65,536, `read_chunk`'s own `requires max > 0` is never violated (at `n == limit` it asks one byte, and a byte there is the failure), the reason is `"larger than <limit> bytes"` with the path as `with_file` reports it, and `limit = 0` admits the empty file; the fixture crosses a 65,536 boundary (70,000 bytes) on both sides and includes the missing-file `FsError`; `fs_read_up_to` joins the bare-WASM `KNOWN` list with `with_file`'s existing reason, `fs_read_up_to_rejects_limit` the WASI one with `Fs.memory`'s. `Http.sequence` (`http.sak`) keeps `var left` on the `Http` handler and, because a closure cannot assign handler state (`V2041`) and `follow` takes a closure, resolves one request's hops under a private `effect Sequence` whose handler `consuming(script)` removes the first matching entry per `take` and reports `left()`; `sequence_follow` returns `(response, left)` and `send`/`stream` write `left` back; a failure anywhere inside `follow` (a miss on hop 2, the 20-hop limit, a bad `location`) escapes `sequence_follow` before `left` is written, so every entry the hops took is back in place: the fixture's `hops` script answers request 2 with entry 3's redirect, misses `/missing`, and request 3 is answered by entry 3 *again* — the same entry answers twice. `stream` resolves hops through `follow` (the `send` path, no body opened per hop) and opens one body for the final answer, where `scripted` uses `follow_stream`; for in-memory responses the two are indistinguishable. Decision, one per reading. **(1) One `Port<S, R>` for both sides: ratified.** Without overloading, `send`/`recv` on a handle and on an inbox need one type, and the aliases say which way each port faces; `send` on an `Inbox` needs a `Never`, which only a diverging expression supplies; `recv` on an `Outbox` typechecks, since `Never` holds every constraint (`check/body.rs` 724), and answers `Finished` under both handlers — harmless, noted. The worker's `recv` returning `Received<I>` rather than the RFC fragment's `Option` is the one shape per port; RFC 0002 §2.9's fragment is corrected to `Message(b) => …, _ => break` in 11b's doc pass. **(2) `spawn -> Result<R, WorkerError>`: ratified.** §2.9 wrote `-> R` and in the next sentence two `Err` results; the `Result` is what the sentences meant. RFC §2.9 corrected in 11b. **(3) The entry's row is `spawn`'s: ratified.** Under `inline()` the entry runs on the performer's handlers, which is sound only if the parent handles what the entry performs; live, the worker's roots come from its grants and the parent's row is merely wider than what it performs. The cost is the static mirror of the grant rule: a parent that spawns an `Http` worker declares `Http`, so under `sakura run` it needs a `net` entry — which its worker's grants must be a subset of anyway. Rejected: two row variables with a union (no row union in a signature). **(4) Grants: ratified, and the enforcement is sound.** A subset entry by entry, exact strings, no path normalisation (`"./data"` is not `"data"`): fail closed. The "effect without its permission" half is `startup_denial` applied at spawn, one rule in two places (`manifest.rs` 139–152 and `workerDenied`): **an effect that joins one joins the other** (`Llm` is in neither, as its handler is `Handler<Llm, {Budget, Http}>`, so a worker using it declares `Http`). An unset parent table admitting any grant is §6.2's "unset means no host limits" read for the parent; the worker still gets exactly the grant as its table. The chain holds because `granted()` is per isolate from `process.env.SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`, every host reads it, the thread's variable is the grant and nothing in the thread can widen it: a worker's own spawns are checked against the worker's grants (`workers.rs`, `nested`). One item for 11b, not of the grant model: the thread's `process.env` is the parent's whole environment, which `Env.host()` filters but an `@external(js)` in the worker could read (an external is outside the permission model today, §6.2); 11b passes `env` as the `SAKURA_*` variables the runtime reads plus the names in the `env` grant, one filter in `worker_start`. **(5) `inline()`'s parent table is the empty one: ratified.** It is §17.159 (3)'s table — `sakura test` sets empty grants — so `none()` is the only subset, and grants attenuate nothing inline because the worker runs on the performer's handlers, which are the test's fakes; that is what inline is for. Inline cannot apply the "effect without permission" half (no reflection on the row), so `spawn(http_worker, Grants.none(), …)` runs inline and is refused live: the one inline/live divergence, stated in the module header and tested on the live side. A defect inline is the program's and a failure reaches `spawn`'s caller — one instance. **Beta.N:** the inline `live` counter is not restored when `body` fails (the `ponytail` comment), so a program that recovers from sixteen failed spawns meets `Limit` inline alone; one finalizer. Rejected: `inline_with(table)` (nothing asks for it). **(6) 64 per direction, no `close`: ratified for 11a; `Worker.close(w)` is 11b's additive item**, after which the worker's inbox reads `Finished` and the RFC's loop ends by itself; until then an entry loops until its parent's callback returns and cancels it. RFC §2.9/§6's "capacity per spawn" is amended to 64 per direction, fixed (WebSocket's one queue bound; a per-spawn capacity would make each worker's memory a program choice, rejected). **(7) Topics as JS runtime builtins until 11b: ratified**, for the reason given — a waiting subscription needs a resource the publisher can reach, which handler state cannot hold (`V6003`) — and 11b brings `topic_subscribe`/`topic_publish` to `rt` under its MINOR. `publish` counting this instance's full queues while cross-thread delivery is asynchronous and uncounted is `BroadcastChannel`'s own semantics and what §2.9 claims (cross-thread is delivered, uncounted; no cross-process delivery is claimed). Inline determinism holds: one `BroadcastChannel` per name per thread, never delivered to its sender, so a one-instance program (every inline test) sees exactly its synchronous local `channel_try_send`s in subscription order, under `Task.deterministic`'s schedule over `with_channel` and `Task.scope`, the mechanism §17.296 ratified. **(8) Dispatch by the function's identity in a list: ratified as 11a's mechanism.** `Worker.start` is a public operation, so `Worker.start(f, [g], …)` runs `f` inline and `g` live — a misuse the operation's doc names; 11b, which needs a name for WASM and native anyway, decides whether the key the compiler already knows (`WorkerEntry.key`) replaces the list. `V1010` at a `spawn` of anything but a non-generic `@worker` function is ratified (`Tool.of`'s rule, no new code). **Beta.N:** `@worker` on a function of another shape, or on a non-function, is accepted and never spawnable (its `$worker$` entry is dead code); a `V1010`-family check at the attribute's span that it sits on a top-level non-generic `fn(Inbox<I>, Outbox<O>) -> Unit ! {Worker | e}`. **(9) The refusal off JS: ratified** — `sakura run --target wasm` refuses the root row (the module carries no root-effect descriptor; a module run outside `sakura run` meets `D090` at its first worker operation, as native does for a handler `main` installs) and native's `UNAVAILABLE`; `expect-stderr@<backend>` for every backend is ratified. **(10) `Codec` without the decode text: ratified.** The text is `Json.decode`'s message, which is not a contract and may differ by backend, and a `Failed` must compare equal on three backends; the operations `start`/`post`/`take`/`publish_text`/`subscribe_text` being visible as `Worker.<op>` is the price of std code over the codec, ratified. **(11) The `worker_topic_fanout` rows: kept, justified under §17.170 (2), expiring with 11b.** The rows carry their reason and the harness's `passes now; drop it` guard; moving the fixture out of `tests/semantics` to bring it back in 11b is churn, and it is the parity evidence 11b must produce. 11b's acceptance includes all four tables empty of it (`parity.rs`'s `KNOWN` and `KNOWN_NATIVE`, `sakura_codegen_wasm/tests/corpus.rs`'s topic row, `sakura_host_native/tests/corpus.rs`); the two bare-WASM rows for `Json.encode`/`decode` are `json_codec`'s existing class and stand. **(12) ABI numbers: MT-3 takes 1.14.0; 11b reserves 1.15.0.** 11a used no MINOR, so §17.298 (c)'s first-ready rule applies as written — "should 11a not be committed when MT-3 is ready, the first-ready rule gives MT-3 the lower number and 11a the next" — and 11a's number is 11b's: the worker entry export, the message imports and the topic queues in `rt`. MT-3's `ABI_VERSION` is `0x010e00`; §17.298 (c)'s "1.15.0" reads 1.14.0 from here. **(13) The heap bound, for 11b.** The thread runs with Node's default `resourceLimits`; `sakura run` sets no heap flag for the parent either (`sakura test` alone passes `--max-old-space-size=1024`), so the worker is as bounded as its parent and `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` is `D096`; 11b sets `resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb` from the parent's bound when one exists, so RFC §6's "heap per worker" holds by construction. Why: (1)–(3) and (5) are the conservative readings whose alternatives need language features (overloading, row unions, reflection); (4) was read at its lines against the one question — can a worker hold more than its grants — and the answer is no on every route the runtime offers; (6), (7) and (11) defer to 11b what 11b must build anyway; (12) is §17.298's own rule applied to the fact that 11a took no number. Rejected: a per-spawn capacity; an inline table parameter; the fixture split; 11b ahead of MT-3 at 1.14.0 (first ready, one at a time, §17.289 (11)); a decode message in `Codec`. Performance: none on the paths 1.0 promises; a `Worker.spawn` is two channels and a scope inline, a thread live. 300. **MT-3 as built (`a05bf302`, ABI 1.14.0) reviewed at the owner's delegation: the lowering, the runtime merge on three backends, the ABI number and the `apiSchema` stripping stand; two amendments to the lowering, both in `schema_keywords` alone — `minLength` becomes ⌈n/4⌉ (option (b)), and a length bound below zero states nothing — and the `<`/`>` ±1 form and `pattern` stay unlowered (§17.293 MT-3, §17.298 (c), §17.299 (12); round 52, 2026-10-21).** Facts: `sakura_core::lower::Lower::schema_keywords` walks the `where`'s top-level `&&` conjuncts (`conjunct_exprs`, the spine peeled as many times as the syntax counted), takes `<=`/`>=` with a literal (negated allowed, `Int` or finite `Float`) on the right, and names `minimum`/`maximum` when the left is `it` over an `Int`/`Float` base (refinement chains unwrapped to the primitive), `minLength`/`maxLength` when it is `std::string::len(it)` over `String` with an `Int` literal, `minItems`/`maxItems` when it is `std::list::len(it)` over a `List`; a keyword stated twice keeps the tighter value; the text is one JSON object carried in the Core `Refinement`, the snapshot, the JS `$rt.refined`'s fifth argument and the native `["w", …]` row's fifth element, both absent when empty. `jsonSchemaJs` spreads the keywords over the base's schema; `sakura_rt::json::schema` merges them in the same order (a key the base has keeps its place, its value replaced); the WASM host delegates to the JS one. `apiSchema` drops `minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength` and `maxLength` beside the four it already dropped. Fixture `json_schema_refinement_keywords.sak` prints one text on JS, WASM-on-Node and native; `runtime.test.js` pins the runtime merge and the four-argument form of a module built before 1.14.0; the `rt/tests/json.rs` case §17.298 (c) asked for was not added. **(1) Ratified as built:** the conjunct split (no parentheses in HIR, so `n` from the syntax is the only safe count; a chain that is not `n` deep states nothing); the tighter-of-two rule; the decode check unchanged; the fifth-argument/fifth-element layout with the older-host behaviour §17.298 (c) named; the number `0x010e00` by §17.299 (12); the WASM corpus skip (a bare module has no descriptors, as `json_codec`); the native pin being the fixture's `.stdout` rather than an `rt` unit case — the same text on three backends is the stronger check, and a unit case would pin the merge a second time; a refinement of a refinement spreading the outer keywords over the inner's (`Small = Percent where it <= 10` gives `0..10`; an outer bound looser than the inner's wins the key, which is looser than the rule and so still sound — tightening across a chain is not now). **(2) `minLength`: option (b).** `String.len` counts UTF-8 bytes; JSON Schema's `maxLength`/`minLength` count characters (Unicode scalar values, draft 2020-12 §6.3). A string of at most n bytes has at most n scalars, so `maxLength: n` admits everything the `where` admits — looser, sound, kept. A string of at least n bytes has at least ⌈n/4⌉ scalars, so `minLength: ⌈n/4⌉` is the tightest bound that admits everything the `where` admits; as built, `minLength: n` rejects `"é"` under `String.len(it) >= 2` at any client that validates before sending (an MCP client, a `Tool` consumer), which is a wrong promise in the one place MT-3 exists to make a true one. (b) keeps the common case exact — `String.len(it) >= 1` (non-empty) is still `minLength: 1` — where (a) would drop it, and (c) keeps a bound the decoder can contradict. The rule the docs state: **the schema states only what every value the `where` admits satisfies; a bound it cannot state that way is omitted or widened; decode is the rule.** The exact change, `schema_keywords` only (the keyword text is in the module, so no runtime, host or ABI change): in the `("std::string", Ty::String)` arm, when `!upper`, the value and text become `(value / 4.0).ceil()` and its integer text (`i.div_ceil(4)` on the literal, after the sign is applied); the tighter-of-two comparison then runs on the widened values, which is what a client sees. Its comment and the ABI.md, CHANGELOG and `mcp.mdx` sentences say "`maxLength` is the byte bound, `minLength` ⌈n/4⌉; both admit every string the `where` admits". Fixture: `Name` is unchanged (⌈1/4⌉ = 1); one field `handle: String where String.len(it) >= 8 && String.len(it) <= 32` is added to `Form`, expected `"minLength":2,"maxLength":32`, the `.stdout` regenerated on the three backends and the corpus snapshot with it. A program that wants an exact character bound writes `List.len(String.chars(it)) >= n`, which states nothing today; lowering that shape to an exact `minLength`/`maxLength` is additive and not now. **(3) A length bound below zero states nothing.** `String.len(it) >= -1` (vacuous) or `<= -1` (unsatisfiable) would emit `minLength: -1`/`maxLength: -1`, which draft 2020-12 forbids (a non-negative integer), and a strict validator refuses the whole tool schema at compile time, not the one value. One guard in the two `len` arms: `if value < 0.0 { continue; }` (the `minimum`/`maximum` arms take any number). With (2), `minLength: 0` after widening is omitted too (it states nothing). No fixture for a degenerate `where`; the guard is read. **(4) `<`/`>` on `Int` as the ±1 bound: stays omitted.** §17.298 (c) listed it; the implementation and the fixture (`it < 10` states nothing) leave it out. Omission is always sound, the `Float` case has no ±1, and the `exclusiveMaximum`/`exclusiveMinimum` keywords would need a fifth pair in `apiSchema`; additive later if a program needs it, not a gate. **(5) `pattern` is not lowered: confirmed.** std has no `String.matches` (the CHANGELOG line is right); when it exists, a lowered `pattern` must be the same dialect JSON Schema names (ECMA-262, draft 2020-12 §6.4), so the std regex's dialect is decided first, and the API would drop it anyway ((6)). `mcp.mdx`'s "`minimum`, `maxLength`, …" names only emitted keywords; `pattern` is not in its list. **(6) `apiSchema` stripping: confirmed.** The one structured-outputs target is the Anthropic Messages API (`output_config.format`), whose documented JSON Schema support excludes numerical constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`) and string constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`); `pattern` is outside its supported list too (formats only), and its own SDKs strip the same keywords and re-check client-side, which is what `Llm` does through decode. `API_DROPS` is right as a list; a provider added later gets its own list, not a shared minimum. Rejected: (a), losing `minLength: 1`, the most common refinement; (c), a schema the decoder contradicts; emitting both `minLength: n` and a `description` naming bytes (a validator reads keywords, not prose); changing `String.len` to count scalars (§17.293's `String` is bytes, and `chars`/`graphemes` exist for the other counts); an `rt` unit case for the native merge. Performance: none (the lowering runs once per refined type at compile time; the runtime merge is unchanged). Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and its intro sentence (300 added). The owner: nothing waits on a decision; an objection to (2) is one revert to `minLength: n` with its caveat.

Decision. **(1) Library entries stay in 1.0.** §17.225 (2) chose "a WASM library consumed from the Node host across the pull boundary" as the sixth domain, and a library nobody can call is half a domain: the beta's backends page says so today in G02's words. The cost is about 16 agent-hours on the chain, additive, and `v1.0.0` is no earlier than three weeks out on the floors of §17.291 (4), so the slot exists; the owner left the cut to this entry and the reasons to keep it are the ones §17.293 gave. **The implementation spec**, one Opus lane, follows; an implementer who finds a sentence here contradicted by the code posts the reading in `REQUESTS.md` and takes the conservative side, as every lane does. **(1a) What an entry is.** An entry is a `pub fn` of the package's root module (the module `src/main.sak` or `src/lib.sak` names, the one `main` would be in) other than `main` and other than a `@worker` function, that is non-generic, whose parameter types and result type each have a runtime schema (`PrimOp::Schema` renders it without `null`: no function, no unsolved parameter, no `Secret`, no `@resource` type), whose row holds only `Fail<…>` and std effects with a parameterless `host()` (exactly `root_handlers`'s rule for `main`; `Task` included), and whose error union, if any, is of `error` types with schemas. A `pub fn` failing any clause is not an entry and nothing says so in beta.3 (the rule is on the page; a `W` code naming the failing clause is additive, 1.x, if an author asks); a package with `main` may also have entries (nothing forbids a program that is also a library). Entries exist on every target: Core lowers them once; the JS and WASM backends expose them; native compiles them and exposes nothing ((1e)). **(1b) Core** (`sakura_core`: `ir.rs`, `lower/mod.rs`; the snapshot crate): `Module::entries: Vec<Entry { name: String, def: DefId, fun: DefId, params: Vec<(String, Ty)>, result: Ty, errors: Vec<String> }>`, built by `entries(package)` beside `workers(package)`, in the root module's declaration order, `name` the function's source name, `errors` the qualified names of the union's members (`[]` for a pure row). `def` is `$entry$<name>`, one parameter of type `Ty::Tuple(params' types)` (a 0-tuple when there are none), whose body installs `root_handlers(fun)` as `$entry` does, projects each tuple element and calls `fun` with them, and returns its value; the literal-refinement inits are prefixed as for `$worker$`. The snapshot carries `entries` as it carries `tests` (`sakura_core_snapshot` gains the field; `back` restores it, unlike `workers`). The schema of each param and of `result` is the text `PrimOp::Schema(ty)` renders on that backend. **(1c) WASM** (`sakura_codegen_wasm/src/lib.rs`, `validate.rs`; `rt/src/exports.rs`, `wasm.rs`, `abi.rs`; `rt/ABI.md`): three exports, all required of a 1.16 module, listed in `validate.rs`'s closed list and ABI §9. `entries() -> (ptr, len)`: `u32 n`, then per entry `u32 code` (the index `start` takes, as `tests`' `code`), name, module (each `u32 len`, UTF-8), `u32 nparams`, per param name and schema text, the result's schema text, `u32 nerrors`, per error the qualified type name — `entries_table` beside `tests_table`, the schema texts from `sakura_lir::schema`. `start_entry(code, payload) -> task`: `payload` is a `Bytes` from `alloc_bytes` holding the `sakura-vt1` tuple of the arguments, consumed; refused (0) unless `host_bytes(payload)`, as `invoke` refuses; decoded by `vt_decode` into one tuple value; the task is started under `code` with the tuple as the root frame's slot 0 and `$entry$<name>` receives it as its parameter (the frame convention `rt_code_serve_request` uses for `handle(request)`); 0 when the heap is exhausted or `code` is not an entry's (the codes are a `u32` list in the image beside the table, so the check is a membership test). `entry_value(task) -> ptr`: for a finished task whose outcome is `ok` or `fail`, a `Bytes` (the host drops it) holding the `sakura-vt1` 1-tuple of the value — the result for `ok`, the error value for `fail` — through `vt_encode_tuple(&[value])` with `vt_secrets` false (an entry's types carry no `Secret`, (1a)); 0 for any other outcome or an unfinished task. `outcome(task)` is unchanged: `main`'s and a test's payloads keep their layout, and a host that never calls `entry_value` sees nothing new. `ABI_VERSION` is `0x011000` (1.16.0): §0's MINOR rule read for a new layout (`entries`' table and `entry_value`'s payload) a host must read; the three exports are required, so a 1.15 host refuses a 1.16 module by the MINOR rule, as every MINOR on the chain has; §0's history and §9 state the three; `rt/tests/fixtures/abi/1.16.0/` is captured as §17.232 (c) says; `sakura_abi_version`'s fixtures and the host's `ABI_VERSION` move together. **(1d) The Node host** (`sakura_wasm_host.js`; `runtime.test.js`): `Host.prototype.entries()` reads the table once into `{ name: { code, module, params: [[name, schema]…], result, errors } }` (schemas `JSON.parse`d, as `json_schema`'s is), a `HostFault` when the module exports no `entries` (a module built before 1.16.0: "this module has no entries; build it with sakura 1.0.0-beta.3 or later"). `export async function callEntry(host, name, args)`: `host` an instantiated `Host` (`await loadTypes(); await host.instantiate(bytes)` as `runMain` does, so `__types__.js` beside the module is loaded); `name` an entry's name, else a `HostFault` listing the entries; `args` an array whose length is the entry's parameter count, each encoded with its schema through `encode` (a value the schema refuses is `encode`'s existing `HostFault`), the tuple written by one `Writer` and placed with `copyOut`; then the pending-completion loop of `runTask` runs, factored so that `runTask(entry)` and `callEntry` share it (`runTask` becomes `start` plus a `runStarted(task)`; nothing observable changes for `main` or tests); on `ok` and `fail` the host reads `entry_value(task)` and decodes the 1-tuple with the result's schema or, for `fail`, with `"X"` (the dynamic reading, which yields the error type's class from `__types__.js` by its variant id); then `task_free`. The answer is `{ kind: "ok", value }`, `{ kind: "fail", error, shown }` (`shown` the outcome's text, as today), `{ kind: "defect", code, message, spans }`, `{ kind: "exit", code }` or `{ kind: "cancelled" }`: the outcome's own shape plus the value; `callEntry` never throws for a guest outcome, only for a host misuse (`HostFault`) or an ABI mismatch. Permissions: `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` is read exactly as `runMain` reads it — the process's variable, parsed once into `granted()` — so a consumer sets it before its first call, to the JSON of the manifest's `[permissions]` table it wants enforced, and the root handlers `$entry$<name>` installs are bounded by it as `main`'s are; an entry whose row declares an effect the table grants nothing for fails at its first operation with the effect's own error (the exit-75 shape check is `sakura run`'s and does not run here, which the page says). One `Host` serves many calls in sequence; two `callEntry`s on one host at once are a `HostFault` (the guest runs one root task per `run` loop; a consumer that wants concurrency instantiates two hosts). **(1e) The JS backend** (`sakura_codegen_js/src/lib.rs`; `sakura_runtime.js`): the build writes `__entries__.js` beside `__main__.js` when the package has entries: it imports each `$entry$<name>` and exports `entries` (the same table as an object, schemas as literals) and `export function callEntry(name, args)`, which calls the runtime's `runTask` on `$entry$<name>` applied to the args as one tuple, under `registerOps`, and returns a `Promise` of the same `{ kind, … }` shape; values are the runtime's own JS values (records as their classes, `Int` as the runtime holds it; the page states the mapping once), no encoding; `main`'s `runMain` is untouched. The same consumer source runs against both builds with one import line changed, which is the parity the fixture checks. **Native**: Core's entries are in the image (the table is a static the driver ignores; `$entry$<name>` is dead code), `sakura build --target native` succeeds for a library, and no C API exists in 1.0 — native is experimental and off every gate (§17.245 (2)); a native `callEntry` is M5b's. **(1f) Fixtures and evidence**: `compiler/tests/entries/quotes_like/`, a small library with three `pub fn`s — an entry with a record parameter and a `Fail` union that answers `Ok` for one input and fails for another, a pure entry over a `List`, and a `pub fn` that is not an entry by (1a) (a `Secret` parameter) — plus a `main`, so the module is also a program; `crates/sakura_cli/tests/entries.rs` builds it with `--target js` and `--target wasm` and runs `consumer.mjs` (Node: `callEntry` on each entry with a good argument, a failing one, a wrong-arity call, an unknown name, a value the schema refuses) asserting one JSON transcript byte for byte on both backends, and that a module built without entries (the `abi/1.15.0` fixture) is the `HostFault`; `runtime.test.js` pins the table's decoding and `entry_value`'s 1-tuple; an `rt/tests` case starts an entry with a non-host `Bytes` and gets 0; the LIR corpus snapshots regenerate if a def index moves. **Dogfood**: `dogfood/parcel-quotes/consumer/` — the Node storefront of the brief (its "Additional Node consumption acceptance"), written by Claude Opus 5.5 in a fresh session from the page alone against the installed beta.3, calling `quote` with `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` set to the manifest's table, asserting a quote, an `Err` and a refused host; its friction goes to `FRICTION.md` as before. **Docs**: one page, "Embedding a library in Node" (`website/content/docs/tour/embedding.mdx`; Astra drafts, Sol lands) with the parcel-quotes consumer as its example, the entry rule of (1a), the permissions paragraph, the value mapping on JS, and the ABI line; the backends page's G02 sentence flips to "since 1.0.0-beta.3"; `std/INDEX.md` unchanged; CHANGELOG `Added` with the ABI line; `cli.txt` unchanged (no new flag); phase 12's pass for it. Size: about 16 agent-hours: Core 3, WASM and `rt` 5, the Node host 3, JS 1, fixtures 2, the consumer 1, docs 1. **(2) The beta.N queue after beta.2**, ordered, in four lanes whose file sets are disjoint; every row is one commit with its fixture and CHANGELOG line unless marked; "ABI" says whether the row takes a MINOR on §17.289 (11)'s chain (one in flight at a time); size S ≤ 2 h, M ≤ 6 h, L > 6 h.
