Lane W is serial by the chain: 1 (with 2) then 3 then phase 12's pass; its agent is the chain's one implementer. Lanes C and R each take their rows in the order given and never touch a W file (`std/worker.sak`, `rt/src/exports.rs`, `rt/src/wasm.rs`, `sakura_wasm_host.js` are W's until 3 lands; `rt/src/json.rs` and the crypto and cli sections of `sakura_runtime.js` are R's; `sakura_core/src/lower/mod.rs` is shared by 3 and 5 — 5 edits `schema_keywords` alone and rebases under 3). Lane D is prose, workflows and `dogfood/`, where Opus's only code is the upgrades, `judge`, `dogfood.yml` and the `spec_docs.py` check. **Held behind the lanes**, not in the table: the perf rows (WS-P16 → P17 → P18 on the JS line; WS-W8 → W9 → W3's fix → W4 → W7 on the WASM line; the `import_key` row; the `arena_obj` attribution), by the owner's 2026-10-21 word ("no new perf lanes") and §17.291 (3)'s "counts, not gates": a perf row starts only when a lane empties and its files are free, one at a time, and lands as a beta.N read at 1.0.0's envelope; a row not on `main` by beta.3's preparation commit is 1.x ((3b)). Native's remainder (N1b's `Http`, `Llm`, secrets, log, runner codes, `V8004`; N2's three controls; N2f) waits for row 1 (both touch `sakura_host_native`) and then takes the lowest-priority slot, off every gate. `Http.is_refused` stays conditional on a second program asking (§17.294 SS-15). **The betas**: `v1.0.0-beta.2` is rows 1–2 with the batches already on `main` (its preparation commit follows row 1's push; nothing waits for 3); `v1.0.0-beta.3` is rows 3–13 and 18–19 and whatever of 14–17 and 20 is ready, and is the last feature beta; a later beta.N exists only for a defect fix or a contract change, and each restarts the seven days ((3b)). **(3) The path to `v1.0.0`**: the evidence still missing, who produces it, and what this entry changes. **(3a) The nightly streak and the campaign** (§17.291 (4) (i), (iii); §17.225 (4)). Missing: all seven nights (none has counted: the scheduled runs since the fixes are absent, 2026-10-21's, or red, before them) and all 24 CPU-hours per target (no ledger entry). Producer: `fuzz.yml`'s schedule, read each morning by Sol, who records the run id and colour in a dated table in `compiler/fuzz/README.md` (the ledger the campaign section names and never got), files a red night as a `soundness` issue the same day and hands it to lane C or R by file, and dispatches the campaign input (`max_total_time`) on GitHub-hosted runners in runs that add up to the hours, logged in the same table; a scheduled run that does not appear is itself a finding (GitHub's cron is late, not absent; two missing mornings in a row is a workflow defect for Sol). The streak counts scheduled runs only, consecutive, ending at the tag; a finding restarts it and never the beta. Unchanged from §17.291 (4). **(3b) The seven days** (§17.291 (4) (ii)). Missing: the clock has not started (it starts at the last beta's tag). Decision: beta.3 is the last feature beta ((2)); the seven days run from beta.3's tag; a perf row, a native lane or any additive change that misses beta.3's preparation commit is 1.x, not a beta.4, unless it is a defect fix or a contract change, which is a beta.4 and a new seven days. This changes nothing the owner decided: §17.291 (4) is the owner's floor, and naming the last beta is the lead's scheduling under it. `v1.0.0`'s date is then the first day with seven clean nights ending at it, seven days since beta.3, the campaign hours in the ledger, and (3c)–(3e) in the notes. **(3c) Agent-DX** (§17.225 (3), road-to-1.0 stage 6 (b)). Missing: the per-family numbers in the skill condition (10/12, 8/12). The paired paid run of §17.182 (4) needs a fresh owner key and the owner's written approval of $5.04 against the $5.80 left under the $10 cap; the report says the key is not available and no rerun is authorized; the owner's standing rule is the cap and nothing else paid, and the owner's "route every decision to Fable" delegates design, not the spending of the owner's money. **Decision: the paid paired run is dropped as a 1.0 gate.** It is not dropped as a run: if the owner hands a key with that written approval before `v1.0.0`, Sol dispatches `agent-eval.yml` for seed 1 inside the cap and the notes carry its numbers; nothing waits for it. What replaces the bar is evidence the agents produce for free, each already in the plan or one small build away: (i) the pilot's 48 episodes as the recorded measurement, stated with its Wilson intervals, its date, the skill it measured (not today's) and that no second paid run happened; (ii) the offline harness green in CI at the tag (gold 25/25, hollow 0/25, the `W1003` gate landed), the proof the tasks and oracles are sound; (iii) the subscription episodes §17.225 (3) named and never built: Opus adds `runner.py judge` (a submission directory produced outside the runner, verdicted with `offline.py`'s rules; family, condition and whether the skill was loaded, read from the client's transcript), and Sol runs the twelve tasks through the owner's Claude Code seat as delegated agents under the harness's sandbox rules and tool allowlist, in the skill condition, one seed, free of the cap; the per-task verdicts are the numbers the notes state, labelled "subscription episodes, Claude family, judged offline"; a Codex seat run is the second family's if the owner's seat is usable (§17.255 (4)), else the notes say the second family is untested, as §17.255 (4) already provides; (iv) the six dogfood programs as the writing evidence at program scale: six fresh Opus sessions without the source, each program's first-try `check` and test counts as its `FRICTION.md` records them (dispatch-packlist: clean on the first try, 23 of 24 tests on the first run; the others as recorded), and the per-beta upgrades of (3d). The bar for 1.0 becomes: (ii) green, (iii) run with its verdicts in the notes and no task failing in both (iii) and (i), every failing task's cause a message or docs item fixed before the tag or a task defect fixed in the task (§17.225 (3)'s own clause), and (iv) complete. Permitted by: §17.225 (3)'s own text, which already made the subscription episodes the free half and the paid run conditional on the owner's approval; road-to-1.0 stage 6 (b)'s "owner to confirm the eval reading", which the owner delegated; and the cap, which this entry does not touch. **(3d) The dogfood upgrades** (§17.291 (1b), §17.255 (3)). The `v0.1.0` → beta.1 round is done as the facts record it, and it passed the test the round exists for: no hunk any program needed was missing from the notes. Two readings: the lists were written by Opus, not Astra — accepted for this round, since the prediction was written before the code was touched and the file says so, which is the whole of the cross-family test's mechanism that a single family can keep; from beta.2 on, Astra writes the list (§17.255 (3) as written), and where Astra is unavailable Opus may, in a separate commit that precedes the upgrade commit, so the order is in the history and not only in the file. Repair-queue's two wording gaps were notes defects and are fixed (`60eb3c2f`, items 1 and 3). Missing: the per-beta rounds — for beta.2 and beta.3 each, the list from that beta's section alone, then the upgrade, same acceptance — and the CI run: no workflow runs the corpus on an installed binary. Opus adds `dogfood.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` with `version`, and on each tag): `npm install --global sakuralang@<version> --ignore-scripts` on `ubuntu-24.04`, then `sakura test` on `js` and `wasm` for the six, cassettes committed, no `net` — the §17.225 (2) "run in CI against the installed binary, never the source build" that was never wired. Acceptance at 1.0: six green on the last beta's installed binary with every hunk explained; the parcel-quotes consumer ((1f)) joins the run at beta.3. **(3e) The spec's semantics** (§17.225 (9), §17.291 (3e)). Missing, after the six chapters that landed as this entry was written: `gaps.md`'s 167 lines each resolved to a fixture or marked informative with its reason, `modules.md`'s entries paragraph once (1a) lands, and the reviews — the six chapters are read here against the code as the grammar was, in two entries of three, each sentence checked at its fixture, before `v1.0.0`'s preparation commit. Producer: Astra for the gaps and amendments (`spec_docs.py --check` already reads the labels, so no tooling is owed); Fable for the reviews. Complete at 1.0.0, not before beta.3; size M. **(3f) Already produced**: the envelope at beta.1 (blessed under the owner's delegation; read again at beta.2, beta.3 and 1.0.0 on the same Node pin, a miss carried under a named decision); signed and notarized Darwin archives (`v1.0.0-beta.1` ships them); `verify-published.yml` green on every row for beta.1; zero open `soundness` issues; RFC 0001 accepted at beta.1. **(4) The three findings of the beta.1 upgrade round**, each a decision. **(i) Bug (hint), beta.N, row 18.** `std_import_fix` learns the constructors of std `pub` sum types: an unresolved call or pattern `Name(…)` that is a constructor of exactly one std type offers `import std/<m>.{Type}` as a `MachineApplicable` fix and says "`Text` is a constructor of `Payload` (`std/request`): write `Payload.Text(…)`" (the rewrite stays `suggested`, since it changes the call); `V1007` on `Bytes(b)` takes the same path when the name is both a type and a constructor; the `Test` suggestion was the two-edit fallback §17.187 withdrew for members, now withdrawn for bare names when a constructor matches. One `ui` case with `Text("s")` and `Bytes(b)`. **(ii) By design; nothing changes.** §17.292 (2) promised the value's text, `malformed JSON`, in `parse`'s doc comment and pinned it; a program that prints `"malformed JSON: {e.message}"` wrote its own prefix over the value's, and the fix is the program's (print `e.message` or `show(e)`); std does not second-guess a caller's prefix, and a message that varied by caller would be the backend-dependent text the fix removed. Recorded in parcel-quotes's `FRICTION.md` as the author's. **(iii) Two decisions.** First, `verify`'s obligation set is not a contract: STABILITY.md names `verify` a preview over a restricted fragment, `verify_summary`'s `kind` and `schema_version` did not move, and a proof that becomes decidable (WP-8) or an obligation that becomes visible (the perform-site `requires`) is the preview improving; but a change a program's author can see in `--json` with no source change belongs in the notes, so the CHANGELOG gains one `Changed` line under `Unreleased` naming the two (row 20, Astra), and from beta.3 on every lane E-shaped commit carries its own. Second, the new `unsupported` is a defect of the perform-site check, not of the program: `Cli.exit`'s `requires code >= 0 && code <= 255` at a call with a literal argument is decidable by evaluation, and an `unsupported` on it is noise in the one summary the brief's verify gate reads; row 19: a perform-site `requires` whose arguments are literals (or `@total` expressions over literals) is evaluated and reported `proved` or `disproved`, and the encoder's `unsupported` is kept for the rest; fixture: workshop-power's shape (a `main` calling `Cli.exit(0)`) under `compiler/tests/verify/`, `verify --json` with no `unsupported` row. **The owner's steps** at `v1.0.0`, unchanged: bless at each beta.N and at 1.0.0 (delegated), the tag, the channel approvals, the `verify-published.yml` dispatch; and, if they choose, a key for (3c)'s optional run. Why: (1) because the owner chose the sixth domain and a beta that calls itself feature-complete for 1.0 should not ship a library nobody can call when the mechanism (`invoke`, `vt_decode`, `encode`, `runTask`) is three exports and one function away; the spec reuses every piece the served-request path built rather than a second one; `entry_value` beside an unchanged `outcome` keeps `main` and tests byte-identical for every host; `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` as the consumer's table is §17.293's reading and the brief's requirement at zero new surface. (2) because the lanes are bounded by files (§17.285 (1)) and the one serial line is the chain; naming the last feature beta is what turns the seven-day floor into a date. (3c) because the paid run's precondition is a spend decision only the owner makes, and the plan already contained its free replacement; a bar that waits on money the owner has not offered is a bar nobody can meet, and the evidence the agents can produce — the pilot, the oracles, the seat episodes, six programs and their upgrades — is more than twelve tasks measured once. (3d) because the first round passed its own test while this entry was written and the role deviation is recorded rather than redone (a re-write by Astra after the fact would predict nothing); (3e) because Astra has written five of six chapters in the right form and what is left is one chapter and the gaps list. Rejected: cutting entries from 1.0 (the sixth domain was the owner's choice and the cost is sixteen hours on a path that is three weeks long anyway); a `kind = "lib"` manifest key to gate entries (a fact the root module already states); a `W` diagnostic now for a `pub fn` that is not an entry (additive, unasked); encoding the result in `outcome`'s `ok` payload (a shipped layout, so MAJOR by §0's letter); a `callEntry` option that passes a permissions table (the variable is the one mechanism every host reads; a second one is a 1.x RFC); concurrent `callEntry`s on one host (one root `run` loop per instance); a native `callEntry` (M5b); authorising the paid run from this chair (the owner's money); dropping agent-DX from 1.0 outright (the free evidence exists and the notes must say what was measured); a beta.4 for perf rows (every beta restarts the seven days; perf rows are counts). Performance: none; `entry_value` runs once per call. Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and its intro sentence (301 added); plan `road-to-1.0.md` (the out-of-beta paragraph's library-entries sentence and stage 6 (b) now cite this entry). Impact: Opus (lanes W, C, R; `judge`, `dogfood.yml`, the upgrades), Astra (the later migration lists, the gaps list, row 20's line, `embedding.mdx`'s draft), Sol (the fuzz ledger and campaign dispatches, the seat episodes, the Windows row, the pages); the owner: nothing waits; a key for (3c) is optional; an objection to any verdict is one revert.

302. **Phase 11b (`std/worker` live on WASM and native, topics in `rt`, `Worker.close`, `35be3ac3`, ABI 1.15.0) stands as built for `v1.0.0-beta.2`: grant enforcement read at its lines on the three hosts holds (a worker's table is exactly its grants, a subset of its spawner's own table entry by entry, its thread's environment the `SAKURA_*` variables and its `env` grant's names, its own spawns checked against its grants), the `topic_deliver` slice order is right, descriptor layout 5 is within the native rule, the inline path is deterministic, the six readings are ratified, the bare-WASM `worker_topic_fanout` row stands in `json_codec`'s class, and nothing gates beta.2 — three riders, none on a 1.16.0 file (§6.2, §17.245 (2), §17.289 (11), §17.299 (4)–(8), (11), (13), §17.301 (1c), rows 1–4; RFC 0002 §2.9, §6, §7; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` 2026-10-21 phase 11b; round 54, 2026-10-21; owner's delegation).** Facts, from the diff (80 files) and the files it touches. *Grant enforcement, per route.* JS (`sakura_runtime.js`): `worker_start` finds the function by identity, `workerAdmit(effects, …)` builds the table and refuses it unless `grantsWithin(table, granted())` — each list `includes`d in this isolate's `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`, a missing key read as `[]`, any table when the own one is `null` — and not `workerDenied` (`Fs` with an empty `fs.read`, `Http`/`Serve`/`Sql`/`WebSocket` with an empty `net`, `startup_denial`'s lists); `workerSpawn` starts the thread with `env: workerEnv(table)` (the `SAKURA_*` variables but `SAKURA_TRACE`, the variables the `env` grant names, `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` the grants) and `resourceLimits: workerHeap()` (the parent's own `maxOldGenerationSizeMb`, else `--max-old-space-size` among its options, else none). WASM (`sakura_wasm_host.js`): `Host.workerStart(code, ptr, len)` finds the entry by the code in `workers()` (−3 when none), decodes the grants tuple and runs the same `rt.workerAdmit`, then `rt.workerSpawn` with `{ sakuraWasm: { module, entry, key, argv } }`; the thread's `runWorker` builds a fresh `Host` whose `fs_root`, `env_get` and `netRefusal` are the JS runtime's over the thread's own `granted()`, which is the grant. Native (`sakura_host_native/src/worker.rs`): `start_worker` finds the function by code in the descriptor's table (`parse_table`, trailing bytes refused), checks each list with `within` against `self.config.permissions` (exact strings; `None` is no limit), then `denied`, and builds the worker's `Config` with `permissions: Some(grants)`, `trace: None` and the parent's `cwd`; the driver's `run_worker` gives it the parent's `Limits`; the worker's `NativeHost::env_get` and `fs_root` read its own `config.permissions`, and its `start_worker` checks a nested spawn against the same — its grants. Evidence: `a_live_worker_reads_only_what_its_grants_name_on_every_backend` (a sibling directory the parent may read, a variable the parent sees, a wider nested spawn: refused on each of JS, WASM, native), `grants_attenuate_a_live_worker_and_none_cannot_fetch` (JS, WASM), the `worker.rs` unit case. One divergence found: `Permissions::parse` natively gives `env: None` for a table without an `env` key (`env_get` then reads any variable), and `within(&g.env, None)` admits any `env` grant, where JS's `grantsWithin` reads the missing key as `[]`. `sakura run` serialises every field of `Manifest::Permissions` (`serde`, `env: []` when unset) and a worker's own table always has the key, so the case needs a hand-set `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS`; the invariant holds on it (the parent reads every variable, so the worker holds no more), but the subset check differs by backend: rider (a). The native host reads `std::env` elsewhere only in `Config::from_env` (the `SAKURA_*` variables, once, by the driver), and native has no `@external`, so no route lets a worker read a variable its grant does not name. *Topics.* `Rt::data` is `(len, at)`; `topic_deliver(name: (u32, u32), text: (u32, u32))` destructures `((nl, na), (tl, ta))`, and both callers (`rt_topic_deliver` on wasm32, `Instance::topic_deliver` natively) pass `rt.data(..)` — right. Delivery is between runs on both hosts (`topicInbox` drained before a run on WASM, `Wake::Topic` natively), never to the sender, dropped where a subscription is full; `a_topic_reaches_subscriptions_in_other_workers` crosses two threads on three backends. *Descriptor.* `sakura_native_main_v5`, 112 bytes, the worker table at +96/+104; `UNAVAILABLE` loses `Worker`; a worker's thread applies the same list at its start. *Inline.* `inline()` keeps 11a's mechanism (two `with_channel(64)`, one `Task.scope`, `Task.cancel` when `body` returns); `close` is `close_local` (the local `Sender`'s `close`); `topic_publish` fans out synchronously to this instance's subscriptions in registration order, then posts to the host, which never delivers to its sender. Parity's `KNOWN` and `KNOWN_NATIVE` are empty; `worker_close_finishes_inbox` holds on three backends. Decision. **(1) A stopped native worker in a pure loop keeps its thread: ratified for beta.2.** Observable: natively `worker_join` waits for the thread, so a parent whose worker computes without waiting returns from `spawn` when the computation does, and an unbounded pure loop keeps the parent in `spawn` where JS's `terminate` returns; from the stop the worker's output is dropped (`is_stopped`), and its `Fs` writes, within its grants, continue until its next wait. Native is experimental and off every gate (§17.245 (2)). Rejected: a time limit in `join` (it would make `spawn`'s return a race); `join` not waiting (a worker still running after `spawn` returned is worse than a parent that waits). The fix is a safepoint poll in compiled code, M5b's with preemption; the `ponytail:` stands; one sentence on the stdlib page (rider (b)). **(2) Native worker env scoping: ratified**, by the facts above (`Env.host()` sees the grant's names; nothing else in the host reads the process environment after startup). Rider (a) closes the missing-key divergence so the three subset checks are one. **(3) Grant paths as exact strings: ratified, fail closed.** `"./data"` beside a manifest's `"data"` is a refusal, never an admission; identical strings name one directory under one working directory, which the thread shares. A lexical normalisation (`Path::components`, no filesystem access) would admit more and is a security-relevant change: additive, 1.x, only if a program asks; the docs say the grant is the manifest's string (rider (b)). **(4) Native refusing an `Http` worker with exit 75, read as `Failed(WorkerError(Defect("exit 75")))`: ratified.** −1 at `start_worker` would report `GrantExceeded` for a grant that is not exceeded; a `WorkerReason` for one experimental backend's missing service is rejected; the shape is the one a JS thread's `Exit` already reports, and the row disappears when native gains `Http` (N1b). **(5) The inline `live` counter: §17.301's row 2 is withdrawn** (the row stays for the numbering, nothing is left). Sakura code has no finalizer, and a builtin for one counter in the test handler is more mechanism than its ceiling costs: sixteen *failed* spawns in one deterministic test before `Limit`. The `ponytail:` in `std/worker.sak` stands as the recorded ceiling; reopened as a `Task`-level finalizer only if a std module needs one for itself. **(6) A live-test timeout hanging the test binary: harness only, rider (c).** `sakura_env` kills `sakura`, and the `node` or `main` it started keeps the pipes open, so `t_out.join()` blocks; the child goes in its own process group (`CommandExt::process_group(0)`, Unix), the group is killed at the limit, and the pipe readers are joined through a channel's `recv_timeout`, so an orphan holding a pipe fails the test instead of holding it; Windows takes `taskkill /T /F` on the Windows row. **(7) The bare-WASM `worker_topic_fanout` row: the deviation is ratified.** §17.299 (11) asked the *topic* rows gone, and they are: parity's two tables and the native corpus are empty, so topics run on WASM and native under `sakura run`. The bare corpus module carries no JS type descriptors, so `Worker.recv`'s `Json.decode` stops it — `json_codec`'s class, which (11) already accepted for two rows; `worker_close_finishes_inbox` joins it for the same reason, both rows carrying that reason and the harness's `passes now; drop it` guard. **(8) Descriptor layout 5 under the ABI policy: acceptable.** ABI §0's MINOR rule governs the WASM module and its host. The native descriptor's rule since layout 1 is the one §1b states — a layout change renames the entry, so an object of another layout fails to link rather than misread — and the driver's staticlib and the object come from one compiler build (`SAKURA_NATIVE_LIB_DIR`); native is experimental with no compatibility row (STABILITY `—`), and the `sakura.native` record's `abi` word is checked at startup by the MINOR rule as well. A native program linking only with its release's driver is the documented rule, not a promise broken. When native leaves experimental, the descriptor gets a versioned header the driver reads at startup instead of a renamed symbol (M5b, not now). Fact, no work: `rt/tests/fixtures/abi/` holds 1.4.0 alone; §17.232 (c)'s capture per MINOR has not been kept since, 1.14.0 included, so §17.301 (1c)'s `abi/1.16.0/` capture is that row's and no 1.15.0 capture is owed. **Riders, none a gate:** (a) `sakura_host_native/src/worker.rs` `start_worker`: `own.env.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])`, the missing key read as `[]` as JS reads it, one assertion in `grants_beyond_the_parents_table_or_an_unpermitted_effect_are_refused`; lane W's file, S; (b) phase 12's row 4 pass carries three sentences — the stopped native thread (1), the grant as the manifest's exact string (3), the native exit-75 end (4) — on the stdlib page, `std/INDEX.md` and the skill's `stdlib.md`; docs, S; (c) `sakura_cli/tests/common/mod.rs` as (6); lane R, S. None of (a)–(c) touches `rt/src/exports.rs`, `rt/src/wasm.rs`, `rt/src/abi.rs`, `sakura_core`, `sakura_codegen_wasm` or `sakura_wasm_host.js`, so library entries (§17.301 row 3, ABI 1.16.0) start on those files now without a collision. Why: the one question of §17.299 (4) — can a worker hold more than its grants — was asked again of each new route (the WASM host's thread, the native instance, the nested spawn, the environment, the topics) and the answer is no on every one; (1), (3), (4) and (8) are the conservative readings whose alternatives either race, admit more or add a mechanism for one backend; (5) spends nothing on a ceiling no test reaches; (7) keeps the acceptance's intent where the implementer kept its letter's reason. Rejected: a timeout in `join`; path normalisation; a new `WorkerReason`; a finalizer builtin for the counter; moving the corpus fixture. Performance: none on the paths 1.0 promises (a live spawn is a thread; inline is unchanged). Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and its intro sentence (302 added); §17.301's row 2 withdrawn by (5). Impact — verdict: **acceptable for `v1.0.0-beta.2` as landed; the beta.2 gate list from 11b is empty.** The implementer adds the dated review line to `REQUESTS.md` with the next push, as §17.299 had it. The owner: nothing waits on a decision; an objection to any verdict is one revert.

303. **The `MIN % -1` fix (`ee71ec7a`) ships in `v1.0.0-beta.2` as a Fixed entry, not a Breaking one, with runtime ABI erratum 1.15.1 for §2's `Int` row and `sakura_abi_version` unchanged; the fixture commits `0c5a6770`, `cd6aaa0e` and `854dddf4` stand, the corpus generator's `.wasm.stdout` preference and its failed-`main` skip included; the six semantics chapters (`73f34ea5`..`94f362e6`) are reviewed rule by rule against the design and their fixtures and stand, TY22 rewritten for `17a77175`; `gaps.md`'s `minLength` entry is resolved and the seven entries left are the ones no `.sak` fixture can pin, each assigned (§4.1, §17.260 (G05), §17.300 (2)–(3), §17.301 row 16; ABI §0, §2; `docs/spec/*.md`; CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`; round 55, 2026-10-21; owner's delegation of named-maintainer review).** Facts, read at `854dddf4`. *The fix.* §4.1 and §17.260 (G05) have said since round 31 that `-2^63 % -1` is `0` and only `MIN / -1` is `D001`; §17.260 assigned the lowering to Opus, the ABI row "(1.4.2)" to Astra and "G05's confirmation" to the owner, and none of the three landed before the `v1.0.0-beta.1` tag, so beta.1's WASM and native gave `D001` for the remainder (the `gaps.md` entry the chapters recorded). `ee71ec7a` moves the `MIN`/`-1` test under `IntDiv` alone in `sakura_codegen_wasm` (`i64.rem_s`) and `sakura_codegen_native` (Cranelift `srem`), and makes the five other evaluators agree: the LIR and Core reference evaluators (`sakura_eval`, `wrapping_rem`), the native test evaluator, the checker's constant folder (`consteval.rs`) and the range analysis (`ranges.rs`, where `x % -1` is defined for every `x`). No other remainder exists: `rt` has no interpreter, and the JS runtime's `rem` is unchanged because `MIN` is `D003` there before any operator. The ABI §2 row was edited in place with no §0 line and no version, where §0's own rule is that a change lands with its design decision and the two precedents for a behaviour-only change (1.8.1, 1.8.2) are errata lines with the global unchanged; `rt/ABI.md`'s 1.14.0 bullet does not carry `17a77175`'s ⌈n/4⌉ sentence either (it lives in `runtime/js/ABI.md` and the CHANGELOG, where the keyword text is produced), which is right. *The fixtures.* `defect_D001_int_min_div.sak` (`expect-defect: D001`, `@js: D003`, "before" printed) and `int_min_rem.sak` (four `0`s on WASM, nothing on JS, `.wasm.stdout` as the twin) are the two files §17.260 named; the corpus entries carry the WASM endings (`D001` with "before"; `ok` with four `0`s), so `regen_core` reading `<name>.wasm.stdout` before `<name>.stdout` is the parity harness's rule (§17.80) applied to the corpus, as it already applied `expect-defect@wasm`. `cd6aaa0e` leaves `main_failure_exits_1` out of the corpus because its `.expected` grammar has `Exit(n)` for `Cli.exit`'s silent exit only; the skip keys on `Exit(` with an `expect-stderr` directive, which is every failed-`main` fixture today and no `Cli.exit` fixture (none asserts stderr). `854dddf4` repairs the two links 11b's rename broke. *The chapters, each labelled rule read against its design section and its fixture's directives and expected output.* Evaluation: EV01–EV25 as drafted; EV26 states (G05) and its fixtures' directives exactly, the informative sentence after it records beta.1 correctly; EV27 lists six observations, all in `float_nan_negative_zero.stdout` (`false true false false`, `false false`, `true false -Infinity Infinity`, `NaN -0.0 -0.0 0.0`), consistent with §4.1 and §17.259 (G04); EV28's three orders and strictness are `eval_order_left_to_right.stdout`'s lines (`a1 a2 a3 callee`, `left right mul`, `y x`), §5.7 and §8.7; EV29 is `short_circuit_and_or.stdout`'s six lines. Types: TY23 is `V2001_type_mismatch_same_predicate_refinements.jsonl` (`expected B, found A`, §4.6); TY24 is `refined_field_construction_d010.sak`'s `D010` with `` refinement `Ticket.title` violated `` on stderr (§7.2); TY22 was stale — it still described the compiler before `17a77175` and said "the amendment is not built", while the fixture's `handle` (`>= 8 && <= 32` → `"minLength":2,"maxLength":32`) and `loose` (`>= -1 && >= 0` → no keyword) now pin §17.300 (2)–(3); rewritten here to state `minLength` ⌈n/4⌉ (omitted at `0`), the byte-bound `maxLength`, and that a bound below zero states nothing, with the byte-versus-character reason informative. Effects: EF21 is `handler_reinstall_fresh_state.stdout` `21 1 1` — the nested `with h, h` case is the one §5.5 (§17.259 (G07)) did not spell out, and the fixture's answer (the inner installation starts fresh too) is the only one consistent with "a fresh copy per `with`"; ratified as the rule's reading. Errors: ER20 is `main_failure_exits_1.sak` (`expect-exit: 1`, `expect-stderr: main failed with Rejected`); "followed by the failure's value" is what the three hosts print (`show(o.error)`, `o.shown`, `{shown}`), the fixture pins the tag prefix, enough; ER21 is the two `try` fixtures (`D030`, exit 70, nothing after). Concurrency: CC18 is `channel_rejects_negative_capacity.sak` (`D020` for `-1`, RFC 0002 §2.9); CC19 is the two `D090` fixtures (`queued one` then `D090`; `both wait` then `D090`), §8.6 and §17.280 (4). Modules: MO17 is `std_modules_are_exempt_from_w1003` (three modules each with an unused `import std/list`; `W1003` from the `app` file alone), §17.294 RQ-5; MO16 keeps its two CLI tests after the worker fixture's rename. Nothing in the thirteen contradicts the design body; no rule's sentence claims more than its fixture shows. *`gaps.md` after this entry.* Resolved: `minLength`. Left, each with its reason and owner: order-dependent tails (§5.2 rule 9; a `sakura_types` unit test when someone has a program that exhibits it — Astra, not a beta gate); source-level finalizer order (unobservable from source today, as `0c5a6770` found; closes when a std resource's finalizer has a source-visible effect, none planned); contract spans through a function value (§17.115; a `.jsonl` fixture over the defect record's `spans` in lane C, S, after row 19); pure loops (unpinnable by construction — a fixture would not terminate; stays informative for good); same seed, two runs in one process (a `rt` unit test, lane W after row 3, S); referenced-names-only cycles (a `tests/ui` fixture with an unused import closing a cycle and no `V1030`, lane C, S); the prelude's contents (a `tests/ui` fixture using one non-prelude std name without an import — `V1002` — lane C, S); `minItems` (a `List.len(it) >= n` field added to `json_schema_refinement_keywords.sak`, lane C, S, rebased under row 3's `lower/mod.rs`). The four S rows are additive fixtures, none a beta.2 gate; §17.301 row 16's "gaps.md resolved" is read as "every entry either pinned or stated as unpinnable with its reason", which it now is. Decision. **(1) Beta.2 ships `MIN % -1` as Fixed.** STABILITY's beta rule lists breaking changes "with a migration"; a breaking change is one that changes what a program that worked does (CHANGELOG, 0.1.0's note). Under beta.1 the expression stopped the program with exit 70 on WASM and native and `D003` on JS, so no program that completed computes a different value now, there is nothing to migrate, and the behaviour was the documented one since round 31. The CHANGELOG line gains the ABI erratum and the sentence why it is not breaking; no Breaking entry, no migration line. **(2) ABI erratum 1.15.1, landed here.** The in-place row edit was incomplete under §0: the line is added (the "1.4.2" §17.260 named, under today's number), the header reads 1.15.1, and `sakura_abi_version` stays `0x010f00` as 1.8.1 and 1.8.2 did, since no byte, import, export, outcome code or counter changes. The confirmation §17.260 left with the owner is given here under the delegation. **(3) The three fixture commits stand**, the `.wasm.stdout` preference and the failed-`main` skip included; the skip's key (`Exit(` with `expect-stderr`) is a heuristic with a known ceiling — a `Cli.exit` fixture that also asserts stderr would be left out of the corpus — recorded, not fixed, until such a fixture exists. **(4) The six chapters stand as reviewed**, with TY22 rewritten; EF21's nested reading ratified. **(5) `gaps.md` as above**: one entry resolved, seven left with owners, none gating beta.2. Why: the fix is the design's own sentence, late by three rounds, and the only cost of calling it Breaking would be a migration line that tells no one to do anything; the erratum line costs one bullet and keeps §0 true; the chapter rules were checked against outputs, not prose, and the one stale rule was the one whose fixture changed under it the same hour it was drafted. 304. **Security review of two findings from the Node consumer of the in-flight library entries (ABI 1.16.0, §17.301 row 3, not on `main`): (A) a set `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` table that leaves a key out is read as "no ceiling" for `net` and `env` on the JS and WASM hosts and for `env` on native, while `fs` and worker admission read the same absence as empty — a fail-open in published `v1.0.0-beta.1`, severity Low (no path through `sakura run` or `sakura test` reaches it: both drivers write every key; only an embedder writing the internal-tier variable by hand does), fixed in `v1.0.0-beta.2` as its one gate: absent means deny on every host, a malformed table is `D091`, a Security entry with a migration sentence for embedders and a note appended to beta.1's release notes, not a Breaking entry; (B) an entry parameter of type `Untrusted<T>` renders the schema `["X", "Untrusted"]`, which the WASM host encodes by JS shape with no validation of `T`, so a wrong value crosses and is misread in the guest — confirmed, fixed inside row 3 before 1.16.0 lands: the boundary carries `T`'s schema and the guest wraps, §17.301 (1a)–(1f) amended; every other boundary (`Json.decode`, `Tool.of`, `std/worker` messages, `tests()`, the compiler's MCP tools, the hosts' own `Untrusted` results) is read and has no such gap (§6.2, §6.4, §17.59, §17.159 (3), §17.209 (1), §17.299 (4), §17.301 (1), §17.302, §17.303; `runtime/js/ABI.md` §7; `rt/ABI.md` §8.3; STABILITY.md's environment rows; CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`; round 56, 2026-10-21; owner's delegation of security review).** Facts, read at `e340de43`. *(A) What an absent key means today, reader by reader.* JS (`sakura_runtime.js`): `granted()` (3643) parses the variable once, `null` when unset; `fs_root` (3653) builds `{ read: abs(p.fs?.read), write: abs(p.fs?.write) }` with `(dirs ?? [])`, so a missing `fs` is two empty lists and every host path is refused — deny; `env_get` (3594) reads `allowed = granted()?.env` and limits only when `allowed !== undefined`, so `{}` and `{"net": []}` let every variable through — no ceiling; `netRefusal` (4705) returns no refusal when `net === undefined`, `fetchArgs` (4739) runs it only when `granted()?.net !== undefined`, `serveHttp` (5694) refuses only when `net !== undefined`, and `ws_connect` shares `netRefusal` (§17.286 (10) (a)) — `Http`, `Serve` and `WebSocket` have no ceiling under `{}` or `{"env": []}`, which is the consumer's observation; `grantsWithin` (4479), the worker admission §17.302 ratified, reads a missing key of the own table as `[]` (`(ys ?? []).includes(x)`), so the same table that lets `main` reach any host refuses a worker that names one. The JS runtime is inconsistent with itself: three readers, two readings. A non-array list is worse than an absent one: `{"net": "api.example.com:443"}` reaches `net.includes(host)` on a string, a substring test that admits `example.com:443` — fail-open on a malformed table. WASM (`sakura_wasm_host.js` 377, 389, 780, 808 and the `ws_*` services): `env_get`, `fs_root`, `http_send`, `serveHttp` and the sockets are the JS runtime's functions over the same `granted()`, so the WASM host has exactly the JS readings — for `main`, for a test under `sakura test --target wasm`, and for `runMain` (1721), which reads nothing of its own. Native (`sakura_host_native/src/lib.rs`): `Permissions::parse` (43–70) builds `fs: Some(Grants { read, write })` from whatever is present (absent → empty — deny), `net: Some(strings(v.get("net")))` (absent → empty — deny; used by `worker.rs` 296–310 only, since `Http`, serve and `Llm` have no native host service yet, §17.301's queue), and `env: v.get("env").map(…)` (absent → `None`), which `env_get` (626–637) reads as no limit; the unit test `env_is_limited_by_the_manifest` (898–902) asserts `p.env == None` for `{"fs": {"read": ["a"]}}`, pinning the hole, and the doc comment (32) says "`None` lists are no limit", honestly. A table that is not JSON is `from_env`'s error and the driver does not start (fail closed); a non-array list is silently empty (deny). *How the drivers build the table.* `sakura run` (`sakura_cli/src/main.rs` 905–933) serializes `sakura_analysis::manifest::Permissions`, whose fields are plain `Vec`s with `#[serde(default)]` and no `skip`, so the JSON always carries `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `net`, `env` and `process`, every list empty when there is no `sakura.toml`; `sakura test` (`testing.rs` 149–151) writes `{"fs": {"read": [], "write": []}, "net": …, "env": …}` by hand, every key, on every target (`run_node_tests` is the one runner, `main.rs` 1028); a worker's thread gets `workerEnv`'s full table (4524) on JS and a full `Permissions` on native (`worker.rs` 334–341). So no program run or tested by the CLI, on any backend, can reach the hole; what reaches it is the process that sets the variable itself: an embedder of the JS build or of `runMain`, §17.301 (1d)'s consumer, or a test file like `redirect.test.js` (which writes `{ net: […] }` alone and so runs today with `fs` denied and `env` open — the fix changes nothing it observes). *What the documents promise.* §6.2 and `runtime/js/ABI.md` §7 say an unset table is no limit and give the table's shape with every key; neither says what a set table with a key missing means. `sakura new`'s manifest comment, `manifest.rs` 38 and `manifest.mdx` say "everything absent is denied" of the TOML table, which the driver honours by writing every key. `tour/capabilities.mdx` says running emitted JS without the variable does not establish the ceiling and is silent on a partial one. STABILITY.md lists `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` as internal (driver-to-host) and the native host's reading of it as experimental; §17.301 (1d) makes the variable the consumer's contract at beta.3 ("a consumer sets it … to the JSON of the manifest's `[permissions]` table it wants enforced"), the first supported path that hands the hosts a hand-written table. *(B) What crosses at an entry.* `sakura_core` lowers `Untrusted<T>` to `Ty::Opaque("Untrusted")` (`lower/mod.rs` 770), losing `T`; both schema renderers (`sakura_codegen_js/src/emit.rs` 371, `sakura_lir/src/schema.rs` 133) print an opaque as `["X", name]`; so an entry whose parameter is `Untrusted<ParcelInput>` (parcel-quotes's `quote`, the dogfood case §17.301 names) carries `["X", "Untrusted"]` in its table, which §17.301 (1a) admits because it is not `null`. The WASM host's `encode` (`sakura_wasm_host.js` 1197) sends `"X"` to `encodeDynamic`, which writes the value by its JS shape: an `rt.Untrusted` as `T.untrusted` plus its inner value by shape, a plain object by whatever shape it has, a number as `Int` when integral; nothing is checked against `ParcelInput`'s fields, and the guest's `vt_decode` (`rt/src/vt.rs` 398) accepts any inner word under `t::UNTRUSTED` by construction (the codec is typed by the sender). A field read then lands on a word of the wrong kind — the consumer's `grams: 28542640608928104` is a pointer or a float's bits read as an `Int`. `encode`'s `HostFault` on refusal, which (1d) relies on, exists for every schema form but `"X"`. The JS build ((1e)) encodes nothing, so a JS consumer must build `new Untrusted(…)` itself and gets no check either. *The other boundaries, each read.* `Json.decode` and `Json.encode`: `Untrusted<T>` holds only `Show` and `Eq` (`sakura_types/src/check/body.rs` 743–746), never `Schema`, so a program cannot decode into it or encode it — refused at compile time with the constraint's `V` code; and were a schema with `"X"` to reach the codecs, `fromJs` and `toJs` throw `internal` (3338, 3434) and `rt/src/json.rs` returns `OPAQUE` (`D090`, 823, 1558): fail closed, never a misread. `Tool.of`: `with_schema` requires `A: Schema` and decodes through `Json.decode` (`std/tool.sak` 37, 52) — the same refusal. `std/worker`: `spawn`, `send`, `recv` and `topic` require `Schema` (`worker.sak` 110–137) and copy through the JSON codec — the same. `tests()`: codes, names and modules only (`sakura_codegen_wasm/src/lib.rs` 581–592); no value crosses. The compiler's MCP tools (§12.6): JSON into the analysis library over serde, no Sakura value. The hosts' own `Untrusted` results (`fs_read_text`, `Response.text`, `Llm.generate_text`, `http_body_of`'s `["X", "std::http::Body"]`) are built by the host, encoded by `encodeDynamic` and decoded by `vt_decode` under `host_bytes`: the dynamic path is the host writing to itself, never a consumer's value; its integral-number rule (its own `ponytail:` note) is that path's one standing ceiling and stays host-only. Decision. **(A1) A key absent from a set table is an empty list: denied.** On every host, for every key, for `main`, tests, `runMain`, entries and workers. The unset table stays "no limits" (§6.2, ABI §7: a plain `node` run of emitted JS, the native host's `Config::test`); nothing changes there — the ceiling is still established by setting the variable, and now a set variable is the whole ceiling. **(A2) The fix is one normalization per host, at the one place each reads the variable**, not a guard in each reader: `granted()` returns `null` or a table with `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `net` and `env` all present as arrays of strings, missing ones filled with `[]`; the readers are unchanged (their `?.` and `!== undefined` tests still serve the `null` table). `Permissions::parse` builds `env: Some(strings(v.get("env")))` as it builds `net`, and the doc line reads "an absent list is empty". **(A3) A malformed table is the defect `D091` at the first read**, as a byte-count variable is (§17.209 (1)): not JSON, not an object, `fs` not an object, a list not an array, an element not a string — the record names the variable and the accepted shape, never the value (it may hold paths); on native `from_env`'s error already stops the start, and a non-array list joins it. Unknown keys (`process`, a future one) are ignored. Neither host ever reads a partial or ill-shaped table as open again; the substring hole closes with the shape check. **(A4) Is beta.1 vulnerable?** Yes, plainly: the JS and WASM hosts of `v1.0.0-beta.1` read a set table with no `net` key as unlimited network and no `env` key as the whole environment, the native host a missing `env` the same way, and a table with a string where a list belongs admits a substring match. Severity Low: `sakura run`, `sakura test` and every worker always write every key, so no Sakura program and no manifest reaches it; the exposed party is an operator or embedder who writes `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` by hand and leaves a key out expecting denial, over an internal-tier variable whose documented shape has every key. No advisory and no CVE: the condition is operator-constructed, nothing in the published channels exercises it, and the release is a beta "not for production". The release action: the fix ships in `v1.0.0-beta.2`, which is not tagged without it (the one beta.2 gate, where §17.302 and §17.303 had none), under CHANGELOG `### Security`; and beta.1's published release notes gain a "Known issue" paragraph (text below), appended by Sol under the owner's release delegation, the owner's veto standing. **(A5) Not a Breaking entry.** STABILITY's beta rule lists breaking changes with a migration; this is a security fix to an internal-tier variable, and the two drivers' behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. An embedder who passed a partial table and relied on the open keys loses them, which is the hole closing; the entry says so in one migration sentence inside the Security item, not in the migration list (which is for programs). The CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` `### Security` entry, to be added by the implementer: "A set `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` table that leaves a key out now denies that key on every host (design §17.304): `{}` grants nothing, as the manifest's comment has always said. In `1.0.0-beta.1` the JS and WASM hosts read a missing `net` as every host and a missing `env` as every variable, and the native host a missing `env` the same way, while a missing `fs` was already denied; a list that was not an array matched as a substring on JS. No program run by `sakura run` or `sakura test` was affected — both write every key — only a process that sets the variable itself. A table that is not an object of string lists is now the defect `D091` naming the variable and the accepted shape. Migration for embedders: pass the full table, `{"fs": {"read": [], "write": []}, "net": [], "env": []}` with your lists filled in; a key you leave out is denied. An unset variable still means no host limits." The beta.1 release-notes paragraph: "Known issue (fixed in 1.0.0-beta.2): a `SAKURA_PERMISSIONS` table set by hand that leaves out `net` or `env` is read as no limit for that key on the JS and WASM hosts (`env` on native). `sakura run` and `sakura test` always write every key and are not affected. If you set the variable yourself, write every key." **(A6) The fix list (lane R, row 0, before row 9; S; one commit; the beta.2 gate):** `compiler/runtime/js/sakura_runtime.js` — `granted()` (the permissions section, 3638–3648) normalizes and checks the shape, `D091` on failure; no reader changes; `grantsWithin`'s `?? []` may stay. `compiler/runtime/js/test/permissions.test.js` (new; the variable is read once per process, so a file of its own as `redirect.test.js` is) — `{}`: `env_get("PATH")` is `None`, `fs_root`'s grants are two empty lists, `netRefusal` refuses `127.0.0.1:1`, `serveHttp` returns `{ err }`; `{"net": "x"}` and `{"net": [1]}` are `D091`; the record's message carries no value. `compiler/runtime/js/test/wasm_host.test.js` — one case through `Host` under the same `{}`: `env_get` answers `None` (the WASM parity of the same function). `compiler/crates/sakura_host_native/src/lib.rs` — `Permissions::parse`'s `env` line and the doc comment at 32; `env_is_limited_by_the_manifest` asserts `p.env == Some(vec![])` and adds `{}` → `env_get("PATH") == Ok(None)`; a non-array list is `parse`'s `Err`. `compiler/crates/sakura_analysis/src/manifest.rs` — one unit test: `serde_json::to_string(&Permissions::default())` is the five-key JSON, pinning that `sakura run` writes every key (the sentence the CHANGELOG entry relies on). `compiler/runtime/js/ABI.md` §7 "Permissions" — after "Unset means no limits": "A set table with a key missing has that key empty (denied, since 1.0.0-beta.2; erratum 2026-10-21, design §17.304: until then the JS host read a missing `net` or `env` as no limit); a table that is not an object of string lists is `D091`." `compiler/runtime/rt/ABI.md` §8.3 — the same sentence after "exactly as for JS", as erratum 1.15.2 in §0 with `sakura_abi_version` unchanged (§17.303 (2)'s rule: no byte moves). `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` — `### Security` (new heading, above `### Fixed`) with the entry above. Lane D, with row 4: `website/content/docs/tour/capabilities.mdx` after the sentence on running without the variable — "A table that is set but leaves a key out denies that key (since 1.0.0-beta.2; the beta.1 JS and WASM hosts read a missing `net` or `env` as no limit, native a missing `env`)."; `manifest.mdx` is already right; `embedding.mdx` ((1f)'s page) states the full-table shape and "a key you leave out is denied" in its permissions paragraph. STABILITY.md: no row moves; whether the variable leaves the internal tier when `embedding.mdx` documents it is §17.301 row 4's question, not this entry's. **(B1) Confirmed: the fix is to validate `T`'s schema at the boundary**, and the way to do it with no new schema form is for the boundary to carry `T` and the guest to wrap. §17.301 (1a) is tightened: an entry's parameter types and result type hold `Schema` (the checker's `Constraint::Schema`, `body.rs` `holds`), with one exception — a parameter, or the result, may be `Untrusted<T>` at the top with `T: Schema`; so an entry's schemas never contain `"X"` or `null`, and a record with an `Untrusted` field disqualifies a `pub fn` as a `Secret` does. (1b): `Entry.params: Vec<(String, Ty, bool)>` and `result: (Ty, bool)`, the flag "untrusted", the `Ty` being `T`; `$entry$<name>` projects each tuple element and applies `std/untrusted`'s `of` (the `untrusted_of` builtin both backends have) to a flagged one before calling `fun`, and applies `untrusted_value` to a flagged result before returning it, so the value that crosses in either direction is a plain `T`. (1c): the table carries per parameter name, `u8 untrusted`, schema text, and the result as `u8 untrusted`, schema text — a byte added to a layout not yet published, so 1.16.0 absorbs it with no erratum. (1d): `entries()` exposes `params: [[name, schema, untrusted]…]` and `result: { schema, untrusted }`; `callEntry` encodes each argument with `T`'s schema, so a value the schema refuses is `encode`'s `HostFault` for the wrapped case as for every other, and decodes the result with `T`'s schema; a consumer never constructs an `Untrusted` and never sees one; `entries()` raises a `HostFault` ("an entry's schema cannot contain X or null") if a table ever carries one — a belt for (1a). (1e): `__entries__.js` carries the flag; the consumer passes the plain `T`; `$entry$<name>` is the same Core def, so the wrap is identical on both backends and no JS consumer builds a runtime class. (1f): `quotes_like` gains an entry with an `Untrusted<Rec>` parameter and one with an `Untrusted<String>` result, and a `pub fn` whose record parameter has an `Untrusted` field as a non-entry; `consumer.mjs` calls the first with a good value and with `grams: "x"` and pins the `HostFault` on WASM and the transcript on both; `embedding.mdx` says "pass the plain value; the entry receives it as `Untrusted<T>`, which is the type that tells the library it came from outside". Why: the only alternative that keeps `Untrusted` on the wire is a new schema form `["N", s]` understood by both renderers, `fromJs`/`toJs`/`bindVars`/`jsonSchemaJs`, the host's `encode`/`bind` and `json.rs`'s parser — seven readers for one wrapper that the consumer gains nothing by building, and `Untrusted` would still not be `Schema` inside the language. The flag costs one byte and one field. **(B2) The other boundaries stand**: none accepts a value under an `"X"` schema from outside; the two that could see one (`Json.decode`, the worker codec) defect rather than misread, and the type checker stops the program before that. `Untrusted<T>` stays outside `Schema` (§6.4's boundary is explicit by design; rejected: making it `Schema` so the codecs could carry it, which would let a decoded value arrive already "untrusted" with nothing in the source saying so). Gate: (B) lands inside row 3 before 1.16.0's ABI fixture is captured — a beta.3 gate, not beta.2's; (A) is beta.2's gate and precedes row 3 on `main`, so (1d)'s consumer never meets the hole. Performance: (A) one normalization per process; (B) one `untrusted_of` per flagged argument. Rejected: fixing only the readers the consumer hit (`netRefusal`, `env_get`) and leaving `serveHttp` and native — the same hole in three places; treating an absent key as "no ceiling" by rule and documenting it — the manifest's comment, the driver and `grantsWithin` already say deny, and a ceiling that opens by omission is the one shape a permissions table must not have; calling it Breaking — no program changes behaviour; an advisory — no supported path, no production release. Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and intro (304); §6.2's sentence on the unset table gains "a set table with a key missing denies that key"; the rest by the lists above. Impact — small, two lanes: lane R lands (A6) as the beta.2 gate; lane W applies (B1) inside row 3; lane D's sentences with row 4; Sol appends the beta.1 note. The owner: no decision waits; the beta.1 note is appended unless the owner says otherwise within the day.
305. **Lanes C and R reviewed at `f9667e20`: rows 6–13 and 18–19 stand as built, with the readings their `REQUESTS.md` entries record ratified; `v1.0.0-beta.2` is what is on `main` at its preparation commit, so those rows ship in beta.2 and §17.301's "rows 3–13 and 18–19" for beta.3 reads "row 3, 14–17, 20 and 21"; one gate precedes the preparation commit — the anonymous record literal's parser record takes its own code, `V0017 field_outside_record`, in place of `V1002`; row 10's third clause (a refined flag's message names the failing conjunct) is dropped from §17.292 (3); `MemoryEntry = Contents(Bytes) | Directory` is frozen; the parser's stack margin becomes row 21 (§17.292 (3), (7); §17.295 F5, F6; §17.297 (6); §17.299 (8); §17.301 (2), (4), rows 6–13, 18–19; §17.304; `compiler/REQUESTS.md`'s lane C and lane R entries of 2026-10-21; `sakura_syntax/src/lib.rs` `MAX_DEPTH`; owner's delegation, 2026-10-21: "route every decision to Fable"; round 57, 2026-10-21).** Facts, read at `f9667e20`. Lane C landed `1baa5d88` (row 6), `5a9ef5e4` (row 7), `9efa601e` (row 8, `V1013`), `218ea818` (row 18), `f9667e20` (row 19); lane R landed `80a40ec5` (row 9), `fea8f484` (row 10), `e340de43` (row 11), `dbbcde1d` (row 12), `17d50a86` (row 13); each carries its fixture and CHANGELOG line, and §17.304's gate (`6e0e87d7`) is on `main`. All ten are on `main` before beta.2's preparation commit, which §17.301 placed after row 1's push with "nothing waits for 3". *Row 7:* the record is `V1002` with `phase: "parse"`, built by the parser (`sakura_syntax::codes::FIELD_OUTSIDE_RECORD`, the one parser code outside `V0xxx`), because `editors/tree-sitter-sakura/tests/repo.rs` requires a compiler *parse* error for every file tree-sitter rejects; the resolver says nothing about the head, so `let cap = 1` then `{ cap: cap }` is reported too; the ui case carries `// fmt: exempt` because gate 8 (`fmt_clean.rs`) skips only `V00xx` parse codes; `V0016` is the last `V00xx` in `codes.txt`. The recovery was moved out of `block`'s frame (`#[inline(never)]`) because `long_chains_are_not_nesting` (10,000 `.f()`) overflowed the test thread's 2 MiB stack with it inlined: `MAX_DEPTH` is 128 and the parser's margin at that depth is a frame-size accident, measured nowhere; `sakura`'s pipeline runs on the process's main thread (no `stack_size` in `sakura_cli`; the native driver and three corpus harnesses use `1 << 28`), which is 8 MiB on macOS and Linux and 1 MiB on Windows. *Row 8:* `Worker.spawn` accepts an entry whose row lacks `Worker` (a pure `@worker fn(Inbox<Int>, Outbox<Int>) -> Unit {}` checks clean), so the check is non-generic, two parameters `Inbox`/`Outbox` (or `Port`) in that order, result `Unit`, any row; the message reads "`fn(Inbox<I>, Outbox<O>) -> Unit ! {Worker}`". *Row 18:* `Text` is a constructor of five std types (`form.Part`, `prompt.PromptPart`, `request.Payload`, `sql.SqlValue`, `websocket.Message`), so (4) (i)'s "exactly one std type" never fires for the round's own case; landed: one owner, else the one owner in a module the file imports, else the list with no fix. *Row 19:* workshop-power's `requires Cli.exit` depends on `run_cli()`'s result and stays `unsupported` by the row's own clause; the change is a literal call in a function the encoder gives up on as a whole; a literal is a Core local bound once to a literal (Core is join points and jumps, so a `var` after a loop is a join parameter, never that local); a false literal after a loop stays `unsupported`; `@total` expressions over literals are not included. *Row 10:* the first failing conjunct's text exists only in Core's `validate` lowering; a runtime holds the whole predicate as one `check` (JS `$rt.refined`, the descriptor's `check` index on WASM and native), so the clause in `cli_parse`'s message needs a per-conjunct list from Core and both codegens and a descriptor layout change on WASM. *Row 11:* `std/fs` already has the record `Entry = { name, is_dir }`, the type `File` and the type `Dir`, so the ruled `Entry = File(Bytes) | Dir` is `V1001`; landed `pub type MemoryEntry = Contents(Bytes) | Directory` and `Fs.memory_tree(entries: List<(Path, MemoryEntry)>)`, `Fs.memory` unchanged; the private `fs_memory_root` import now takes `(Path, Option<Bytes>)` pairs on all three hosts, no `ABI_VERSION` move. Decision. **(1) Beta.2 is `main` at its preparation commit.** The lanes were faster than the chain and §17.301 (2) said rows after 2 were beta.3's only because they were expected to land after it; nothing in a row depends on row 3, each has its fixture, and holding ten landed commits out of a tag is a revert nobody asked for. Beta.3 is row 3 (entries, 1.16.0), rows 14–17 and 20 as ready, row 21 (below), and stays the last feature beta; (3b)'s seven days are unchanged. **(2) Row 6: endorsed**, the `V9001` span chosen in `sakura_analysis` (`lower_core`, the first invalid def's `pos`) rather than `validate.rs`, which knows no files — a file outside the row's list is the right file, and the row's list is a start, not a fence. **(3) Row 7: a parser record carries a parser code — `V0017 field_outside_record`, the beta.2 gate.** `V1002` is `unresolved_name`, a resolve-phase code on every page, and the shape is not an unresolved name: `{ cap: cap }` with `cap` bound is reported, rightly, because `name: …` is not a statement. A code's family is part of its contract (an agent reads `V00xx` as "the file did not parse", gate 8 and `fmt` read it the same way, and the ui case needed an exemption to say otherwise), and a code assigned in beta.2 and moved in beta.3 is the churn a versioned contract exists to avoid, so it moves before the tag. Scope, lane C, S, one commit before the preparation commit: `sakura_diagnostics/src/codes.rs` (`V0017`), `compiler/diagnostics/codes.txt` (`V0017 active field_outside_record`), `sakura_syntax/src/codes.rs` (`FIELD_OUTSIDE_RECORD = codes::V0017`, the "one parser record outside `V0xxx`" comment deleted), `docs/spec/diagnostic-codes.md`'s row, the ui case renamed `V0017_anonymous_record_literal` with its `// fmt: exempt` line dropped and `V1002`'s spec-table link moved to `V1002_std_constructor_hint.sak`, `agent_docs` regenerated (the `V0017` error page, the index, the skill's table and zip), and the CHANGELOG line of `5a9ef5e4` reworded to name `V0017`; the message, the one-ERROR-node recovery, the parse phase and the tree-sitter gate are unchanged. The pass beside `check_main_rows` in `lower.rs` (defs, not bodies) is the right place, and `Port` in either position stands. **(5) Row 18: endorsed**, and (4) (i) reads from here: "a constructor of one std `pub` sum type, or of one such type in a module the file imports, names that type with its `import` (`MachineApplicable`) and the `Type.Name(…)` rewrite (`Suggested`); several owners are listed with no fix". The import rule is the right tie-break because the dogfood case imports `std/request` and a hint that lists five types for a file that imports one of them is not a hint. **(6) Row 19: endorsed**, and (4) (iii)'s "`proved` or `disproved`" and "`@total` expressions over literals" are withdrawn in favour of the lane's reading: a closed goal that evaluates true is `proved` wherever the call is (its path conditions dropped; the claim is about the call, not its reachability), a closed goal that evaluates false stays `unsupported` when the function is, because `disproved` claims a path the loop makes unreadable, and a computed value is never a literal. But a margin nobody measures is not an explicit limit (AGENTS.md), and the CLI's main thread on Windows is an eighth of the one the tests run on. Row 21, S: (a) `sakura_cli`'s `main` runs the pipeline on a thread built with `stack_size(1 << 28)`, the number the native driver and the corpus harnesses already use (one named constant, read by all of them), so the parser's margin no longer depends on the host's main-thread default; (b) `sakura_syntax/tests/robustness.rs` runs `deep_nesting_is_reported`'s cases and `long_chains_are_not_nesting` on a thread with a 1 MiB stack — the smallest main thread the binary meets — so the margin at `MAX_DEPTH` is a test, and a frame that grows past it fails in CI rather than in a user's shell; (c) `MAX_DEPTH` stays 128. No contract changes. **(8) Row 9: endorsed** as F5 specified (the four CRT identities, `Malformed` on JS and WASM, `Unavailable` on native). **(9) Row 10: the third clause is dropped from §17.292 (3).** The lane's two clauses landed (any-case constructor with exact spelling first; `<Low|High>` in the usage for payload-free variants, inside `Option` and `List`), on all three hosts. The third costs a per-conjunct check list through Core, both codegens and a WASM descriptor layout change — three lanes and an ABI MINOR for one usage line — when the message already names the type (`"0" does not satisfy the where clause of Port`) and `sakura doc Port` prints the clause; `Json.decode`'s refinement message is the same shape, so if a program ever asks, one 1.x row gives both the clause at once. The `fs_memory_root` layout change takes no ABI number because it ships in the same beta as 1.15.0 and only std calls it; `ABI.md`'s hosted-import row says so. **(11) Rows 12 and 13: endorsed.** Rejected: a `V1002` from the parser kept for the fixture's sake — the fixture is the thing that moves; a `Worker` requirement in `V1013` — it would refuse a program `spawn` accepts; the clause for `Cli.parse` as a lane-C row — the cost is three lanes for one line; `Option<Bytes>` as `memory_tree`'s public shape — a `None` that means "directory" is the implicit API the type exists to avoid; the stack margin as a beta.2 gate — no reproduction on a supported path, and the tag is the owner's date.
