306. **The seven consecutive clean scheduled fuzz nights and the seven calendar days after the last beta leave `v1.0.0`'s gate; the soundness campaign of §17.225 (4a) runs at full speed on the owner's Windows machine (WSL2 Ubuntu) instead of on GitHub-hosted runners, and `v1.0.0` is gated on that campaign's ≥ 24 CPU-hours per target completing with zero `soundness` findings, recorded in the ledger `compiler/fuzz/README.md` names and never got; everything else in the gate stays — no P1 defect, zero open `soundness` issues at the tag, `verify-published.yml` green on every row for the last beta and for `v1.0.0`, and 1.0.0 cut from a commit whose only difference from the last beta is its preparation commit — and the remaining code is the library entries in beta.3 (§17.301 row 3), row 21 (§17.305 (7)), the §17.303 gap fixtures and the eval transcript determinism fix; every other compute-heavy job that is not tied to the reference Mac moves to the same machine under `docs/plans/windows-compute.md`, the blessed instruction-count baselines excepted (§17.225 (4), (5); §17.245; §17.264; §17.291 (3g), (4); §17.301 (2), (3a)–(3b); §17.303 (5); §17.305 (7); `compiler/fuzz/README.md`; `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`; `docs/release.md` §2, §5; plan `road-to-1.0.md` stage 6 and its timeline; owner's decision, 2026-10-21: "can we leave the 7 day quiet period and 7 clean fuzz nights, i will run a new thread on my windows we can use all my windows compute for that" and "all the compute stuff ill do from windows"; round 58, 2026-10-21).** Facts, read at `e86a411a` (beta.2's preparation commit `611dae4f` and its blessed baselines). §17.291 (4) set `v1.0.0`'s floors as (i) seven consecutive clean scheduled nights ending at the tag, (ii) seven days after the last beta's tag with no P1 defect, no open `soundness` issue and no contract change, (iii) the campaign's 24 CPU-hours per target, (iv) the rest of §17.225's evidence; §17.301 (3a)–(3b) gave (i) and (iii) to Sol's morning readings and dispatches of `fuzz.yml`'s campaign input on hosted runners (six hours per dispatch, so at least four dispatches per target), and (ii) ran from beta.3's tag. None of (i) has counted: no scheduled night since the §17.285 (2a) fixes has been both present and green, and the ledger has no entry. The seven targets, their inputs and their assertions are `compiler/fuzz/README.md`'s table; `exec` is the differential (§17.225 (4b)) and needs Node and `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. The reference Mac (host id `d88970189598`) is the one machine whose instruction counts are the baselines (§17.264, release.md §2), about an hour per release. **Decision.** **(1) What leaves the gate.** (i) and (ii) are withdrawn: `v1.0.0` waits for no number of scheduled nights and for no number of days after the last beta. The owner's reason is the one §17.291 recorded for the beta — calendar floors buy nothing the evidence does not — and the evidence they stood in for, hours of fuzzing on the released code, is produced faster by one machine running the targets in parallel than by a cron running them 600 seconds a night. `fuzz.yml`'s schedule keeps running as a regression check (a red night is still a `soundness` issue the same day), but its colour is information, not a floor. **(2) What replaces them: the campaign on the owner's machine, with the ledger as its evidence.** §17.225 (4a)'s "at least 24 CPU-hours per target" stands and becomes the gate: each of the seven targets accumulates ≥ 24 CPU-hours (worker-hours; libFuzzer `-jobs`/`-workers` matched to the core count, so 24 CPU-hours is 1.5 wall-hours on sixteen workers) with zero findings that are soundness bugs, run from the campaign brief `docs/plans/windows-compute.md` on WSL2 Ubuntu on the owner's Windows machine — the "never on the reference machine" clause of §17.225 (4a) is kept, since that machine is the Mac; "on GitHub-hosted runners" is replaced, since the hours are hours wherever the cores are, and the ledger records the host so a reader can tell. The ledger is a dated table in `compiler/fuzz/README.md` (the one §17.301 (3a) named): one row per run with the date, the commit, the target, the host, the workers, the wall seconds, the CPU-hours they multiply to, the corpus size after, and the findings (none, or an issue number each); the per-target totals are the sum of rows at or after beta.2's preparation commit `611dae4f` (the first commit with every §17.285 (2a) fix, `V0017`, `MIN % -1` and the permissions fix, so a crash found there is a crash in what ships), and a row at an older commit does not count. A finding is a libFuzzer `crash-`, `timeout-`, `oom-` or `leak-` artefact that reproduces on the row's commit; the Windows session minimises it, files it as a `soundness` issue (the label is created first; the repository lacks it today) with the minimised input, the target and the commit, and the fix lands with a `tests/ui` or `tests/semantics` regression as §17.225 (4) says. **After a target's fix lands, that target runs at least 4 further CPU-hours at the fix's commit or later with no finding before its total counts**; the other targets' hours are unaffected (one target's finding does not restart the rest — the seven nights were the thing that restarted, and they are gone). A `timeout-` or `oom-` artefact from `exec` that the README already describes (a program allocating without bound within the reference evaluator's step bound) is recorded in the row as a limit hit, not a finding, once the session has read it as such. **(3) What stays**, verbatim from §17.291 (4) and §17.301 (3): no P1 defect open at the tag; zero open `soundness` issues at the tag; `verify-published.yml` green on every `targets.json` row for the last beta and again for `v1.0.0`; the envelope read at each beta and at 1.0.0 with misses carried under named decisions; the dogfood upgrades, the agent-DX bar of §17.301 (3c), the spec's semantics with `gaps.md` as §17.303 (5) left it; and **1.0.0 is cut from a commit whose only difference from the last beta is the preparation commit**. That last rule is not changed, and the reason is the campaign itself: the hours are run on `main` between beta.2's preparation commit and the last beta's, so the code the hours covered is the code 1.0.0 ships, give or take the fixes the hours found, which beta.3 (or a beta.4 for a defect fix, §17.301 (2)) carries; a 1.0.0 that differed from its last beta by anything but the preparation commit would ship code no hour had touched. A contract change after beta.3 is still a new beta (the §17.291 (4) (ii) clause minus its seven days). **(4) The remaining code before 1.0.0**, in the order it lands: row 3 (library entries, ABI 1.16.0, §17.301 (1), §17.304's amendments) and row 21 (the parser's stack margin, §17.305 (7)) in beta.3; the four S fixture rows of §17.303 (5) (the defect record's `spans` `.jsonl`, the referenced-names-only cycle, the prelude's one non-prelude name, and the fourth as §17.303 lists it) in lane C after row 21; the eval transcript determinism fix (the Core evaluator's transcript must be byte-identical across runs for the parity matrix and `exec` to compare it — a divergence there is noise the campaign cannot tell from a finding, so it lands before `exec`'s hours are read as final; `exec`'s rows run before it are re-run, not discarded, only if it changes `exec`'s comparison); then beta.3's preparation commit, its blessed baseline, the tag and the channels; then the campaign's final rows at or after beta.3, the notes, `v1.0.0`'s preparation commit, the bless, the tag, `verify-published.yml`. **(5) The rest of the owner's compute moves to the same machine** under `windows-compute.md`: the native sanitizer lanes (Miri, ASan + LSan, Memcheck) run there at each beta's commit as `native-sanitizers.yml` runs them, the `exec` differential is the campaign's own, the offline agent-DX harness and the dogfood rounds against each published beta are optional extras the brief gives commands for; the repository has no soak or stress loop beyond these and the brief says so rather than inventing one. **What must stay on the reference Mac**: the blessed instruction-count baselines of release.md §2 (host id `d88970189598`), one per baseline release, about an hour each — a count from another host is another host's baseline and compares to nothing. **Why.** The gate measures hours on the code, which the Windows machine produces in a day; the nights and days measured the calendar, which the owner has said twice is not the thing being waited for. The ledger is in the README because that is where §17.225 (4a) and §17.301 (3a) already put it; a `soundness` issue per finding is the §17.225 (4) exit's own form. Rejected: hours on the hosted runners as well (allowed, counted in the same ledger if dispatched, but not required: the six-hour dispatch is the slow path the decision replaces); a restart of every target's hours on any finding (that is the seven nights by another name); a 1.0.0 with the campaign's fixes landing after the last beta (breaks the last-beta rule, (3)); counting hours run before `611dae4f` (`V0017` and the permissions fix changed what the `check` and `exec` targets see). Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and intro (306); `road-to-1.0.md` stage 6 and its timeline; `docs/release.md` §5's sentence on what `v1.0.0` waits for; `compiler/fuzz/README.md`'s campaign paragraph (the ledger table's header and rule are added here; the Windows session appends the rows); §17.291 (4) (i)–(ii) and §17.301 (3a)–(3b) read under (1)–(2). Impact — small: no crate changes; Sol's morning reading becomes a glance; the Windows session does the hours. The owner: open the Windows session with `docs/plans/windows-compute.md`; no other decision waits.

307. **The import-cycle rule is the compiler's: an `import` is an edge of the module graph whether or not the module uses what it binds, so an unused import that closes a cycle is `V1030` beside `W1003`, and §9's "counting only names a module actually references" is withdrawn; a `D020` record carries the call span of every call the compiler resolves to a def, a local bound once to a def included, and no call span only for a call it cannot resolve, so `let f = positive` then `f(0)` reporting the call is the rule and not an exception to §17.115; `v1.0.0-beta.3`'s preparation commit is unblocked — row 3, row 21, the §17.303 (5) fixtures and the eval replay fix are on `main` at `802f469b`, lane W's fourteen readings for library entries stand, and nothing in §17.301, §17.305 or §17.306 is owed before it (§9; §17.115; §17.301 (1)–(3); §17.302 riders; §17.303 (5); §17.304 (B1); §17.305 (7); §17.306 (4); `docs/spec/gaps.md` Modules; `docs/spec/errors.md` ER22's note; `docs/spec/modules.md` MO06; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` lane W 2026-10-21; round 59, 2026-10-21; owner's delegation).** Facts, read at `802f469b`. *Cycles.* `sakura_hir/src/lower.rs` resolves import targets and walks them depth-first before any name resolves (step 2 of its pipeline), reporting `V1030` on the import that closes the cycle ("imports must form a DAG"); the modules are then ordered dependencies-first and bound. `W1003` is reported per module after binding, one warning per name an import binds that no lookup resolved (§17.294 RQ-5). So `a.sak` importing `main/b` and calling `b.two()`, `b.sak` importing `main/a` and using nothing, is `V1030` on `b`'s import and `W1003` on the same line — checked at `1.0.0-beta.2` by lane C (`772d84cc`), which found no fixture could pin §9's sentence and left the entry in `gaps.md`. The existing fixture `tests/ui/V1030_import_cycle/` uses both imports. §9's clause has stood since the first draft and no §17 entry built on it; `modules.md` MO06 says "importing in a cycle is `V1030`" and nothing about use. Under (a) the graph that orders the modules would be built after resolution, which needs the modules bound, which needs the order: the resolver would classify each import's names as referenced in a first pass over every module's export list before binding, and a module's `V1030` would then appear or vanish when a *body* elsewhere in the cycle started or stopped using a name. *Call-site blame.* §17.115's `$site` is `-1` "for a call through a function value or from the runtime". `contract_site_blame_value.sak` binds `let f = positive` and calls `f(0)`; the lowering resolves the local to the def and emits the call with its span, so the `D020` record names the call as `primary` and the clause as `definition`, the direct-call shape; `contract_site_blame_callback` (a parameter called inside another function) carries the clause alone, `primary`. ER22 pins the two ends (`772d84cc`); `errors.md`'s note records the let-bound case as outside ER22. The record has a clause span in every case; what varies is whether a call span stands beside it and which is `primary`. *Readiness.* On `main` at `802f469b`: row 3 (`013bb3bc`, ABI 1.16.0, §17.304 (B1) inside it; `2382ccfd`'s consumer; `0ac1d325`'s recipe), row 21 (`78e07bea`), the §17.303 (5) fixtures but the cycle one (`772d84cc`: `minItems`/TY22, spans/ER22, the prelude/MO18; `0961d96e`: CC20), §17.302's riders (a) and (c) (with row 3), and `802f469b`, which is the "eval transcript determinism fix" §17.306 (4) named: the agent-eval harness's `offline.checked` (§17.297) put whole `check --json` rows, snapshot hash included, into a verdict's reason, so a recorded `.repair.jsonl` could not replay byte for byte; the reason now carries codes, exit and holes, and a second replay is identical. §17.306 (4)'s parenthetical called it the Core evaluator's transcript for the parity matrix and `exec`; that was a mislabel — the Core evaluator's determinism is §17.194's, landed in round 17, and `exec`'s comparison is untouched, so no ledger row is re-run on its account. `spec_docs.py --check`: 170/170 labelled rules cite fixtures; `gaps.md` has one semantics entry left, the cycle. Not on `main`: §17.302 rider (b)'s three native-worker sentences (stdlib page, `std/INDEX.md`, the skill) — docs, native experimental, "none a gate" by §17.302's own words; a parcel-quotes consumer step in `dogfood.yml` (§17.301 (3d): "joins the run at beta.3"), which runs against the *installed* beta.3 and so can only be read after the tag; `rt/tests/fixtures/abi/1.16.0/`, owed after the tag by lane W's reading 8. Decision. **(1) Cycles: (b). The compiler's rule is ratified and §9 is amended; `V1030` counts every `import`.** The graph that decides whether a program compiles is the graph of its import lines, readable from the heads of its files without their bodies; an edge that appears when a body elsewhere starts using a name is a non-local error, and the agent-first principle is that a diagnostic points at the line to change — here it does: the import that closes the cycle, which is also the `W1003` line whose fix (remove the import) removes the cycle. Both records stay: `V1030` says why the build stops, `W1003`'s fix says what to do; folding one into the other is a hint, additive, 1.x if a program asks. In for beta.3, as docs: the behaviour is what `1.0.0-beta.1` and beta.2 shipped, so ratifying it changes no contract, where (a) would have been the contract change and the new beta. The §17.303 (5) cycle row becomes a positive fixture, lane C, S, no gate: `tests/ui/V1030_import_cycle_unused/` — `a.sak` imports `main/b` and calls `b.two()`; `b.sak` imports `main/a` and uses nothing — expecting `V1030` and `W1003` on `b`'s import line, under the ui harness's directives as lane C finds them; `modules.md` MO06 then cites it beside the existing one with the words "whether or not the import is used" (the informative sentence placed after MO06 here moves into the rule when the citation exists); `gaps.md`'s entry is resolved here, since the rule needs no fixture to be stated and the fixture only pins it. **(2) Call-site blame: ratified as the rule; §17.115 reads under it.** A `requires` failure's record carries the call span of every call the compiler resolves to a def — a direct call, a call through a local bound once to a def, and any call a later resolution reaches — and no call span for a call it cannot resolve: a parameter, a field, a value a call returned, a closure. The clause span is always present; `primary` is the call when there is one, else the clause. The set of resolved calls may grow in any release (a MINOR improvement in blame, as `proved` obligations grow under §17.305 (6)) and is not a program's contract; it does not shrink, since a span lost is a regression the value fixture catches once pinned. §17.115's "-1 for a call through a function value" reads "-1 for a call whose callee the compiler does not resolve to a def"; `errors.md`'s informative paragraph is rewritten to say so (done here); lane C, S, no gate: `contract_site_blame_value.jsonl` beside the `.sak` (call `primary`, clause `definition`) joins ER22's citations, and ER22's sentence then reads "for a call the compiler resolves to a def" in place of "for a direct call". No code changes. **(3) Readiness: nothing blocks the preparation commit.** Every item §17.306 (4) placed before it is on `main`; the cycle row is closed by (1) without code; the three items not on `main` are, by the entries that named them, after the tag or no gate: rider (b) lands in lane D's phase-12 pass whenever it runs; the consumer step goes into `dogfood.yml` before `v1.0.0`'s dogfood run is read — Opus, S: one step after `round.sh` that builds `dogfood/parcel-quotes` on `wasm` and `js` with the installed `sakura`, runs `consumer/consumer.mjs` against each under the full permissions table, and fails on its exit code, no new dependency; the 1.16.0 capture follows the tag as reading 8 says. The sequence from here is §17.306 (4)'s: beta.3's preparation commit, its blessed baseline, the tag, the channels, `verify-published.yml`; then the campaign's rows at or after it. **Lane W's fourteen readings stand as built**: 1 (the 1-tuple return — a word on every target), 2 (the `(code, nparams)` table and `start_entry`'s arity refusal), 3 (both hosts check the arguments before they cross, refinements at any depth, one message, `HostFault` on WASM and `TypeError` on JS), 4 (§17.304 (B1) as ruled), 5 (the root module's reading; "`src/lib.sak`" was a module path, not a loader), 6 (`@external` functions and externally declared types excluded, `@llm` functions in), 7 (entries lower last; no id moves), 8 (the capture after the tag), 9 (host tests in `wasm_host.test.js`), 10 (no native table; layout 5), 11 (a trap replaces the instance), 12 (the two stale 1.14.0 assertions), 13 (closed by §17.304 (A) at `6e0e87d7`, which the consumer's `{}` case now shows), 14 (lane D's page). Reading 3 is the one that tightens a ruling (§17.301 (1e) gave JS no check) and is right: the host is the caller, and a refined parameter's `where` must hold at the boundary or the refinement is a lie inside the library. The implementer adds the dated review line to `REQUESTS.md` with the next push, as §17.299 and §17.302 had it. Why: (1) because a rule stated on import lines is local, stable and the one every reader of a file's head (an agent, `sakura doc`, the formatter) can compute, and the sentence it replaces was never built on; (2) because a record that names more of the truth is not a contract break, and a rule phrased as "what the compiler resolves" says honestly whose set it is; (3) because the list is the list, and each absent item was placed after the tag by the entry that created it. Rejected: (a), the resolver change — non-local errors, a two-pass resolver on the critical path to a tag, and a new beta for a case `W1003` already fixes; suppressing `W1003` under `V1030`, or a `V1030` hint naming the removable import — additive, unasked; pinning "no call span through a value" as a rule — it would freeze a limitation; a `.jsonl` for the callback case saying the record must *lack* a call span — ER22's callback fixture pins today's shape and the rule lets it gain one; holding the preparation commit for rider (b) or the consumer step — docs off every gate, and a step that cannot run before the binary it tests exists. Performance: none. Changed: this entry; the §17 heading and intro (307); §9's import sentence; `docs/spec/gaps.md` (the Modules entry resolved); `docs/spec/errors.md` ER22's informative paragraph; `docs/spec/modules.md` an informative sentence after MO06; §17.115 and §17.306 (4)'s parenthetical read under (2) and the facts. Impact — docs now; lane C, S, no gate: the `V1030_import_cycle_unused` fixture and `contract_site_blame_value.jsonl`, each moving its spec sentence; Opus, before `v1.0.0`'s dogfood run: the consumer step; lane D: rider (b) in its pass. The owner: the beta.3 preparation commit can be made; no decision waits; an objection to (1) or (2) is one revert of the sentences.

308. **M5 finishes now, all of it, under the owner's direction that native is "our own main thing": `--target native` ships as an experimental flag in release binaries from the next beta (§17.175 (6)'s condition holds: the A half of the matrix and the §17.173 lanes are green), and N1b's remainder, N2f, the wide-function split, native on platforms B and C, N3, N4 and N5 run as parallel file-bounded lanes with the acceptance below; none of them moves `v1.0.0`'s gate, which stays §17.306's ledger — a row on `main` at the last beta's preparation commit ships in 1.0.0, a row that lands after it ships in the 1.x minor it lands in, and both fit RFC 0001 as written: `W8001` is a new warning (permitted in any minor; reserved since round 13), reuse tokens and the borrowed convention are ABI MINORs allocated at landing, a representation change is a new profile, and native stays outside every compatibility row until the stabilization conditions of (1e) are met; the §17.177 windows are counted baselines on the reference Mac that agents run, the owner blesses and the designer reads; the native performance targets are §17.109's M5 ceilings, measured and never promised, and "faster than" is a sentence for a blessed ratio below 1.0 on a named program and lane (§17.109; §17.152; §17.153; §17.172–§17.178; §17.225 (8); §17.229; §17.240 (3); §17.241; §17.245 (2); §17.247; §17.261 (G25); §17.264; §17.271; §17.285; §17.288 (7); §17.289 (11); §17.291 (3); §17.306; §17.307 (2); RFC 0001's source, diagnostic and ABI sections; STABILITY.md's Native and ABI rows; `compiler/diagnostics/codes.txt`; `compiler/REQUESTS.md` N2a and N2b/c (2026-10-19) and N5 (2026-10-21, in its lane); plans `m5-native.md` and `road-to-1.0.md`; `docs/research/16-native-and-agent-competitiveness.md` (Astra, `c37024d2`); owner's direction, 2026-10-21; round 60, 2026-10-21).** Facts, read at `5b1f9430` (`main`'s head: N1b's `Http.host()` on the native host). Its `ci.yml` run 39643338437 finished red while this was written: every `Rust` partition and the MSRV job fail on `test_host_handlers_fail_closed_without_record` (`sakura_cli/tests/cli.rs`), which runs the `secrets` example that commit edited and now meets Node's `ERR_ACCESS_DENIED` for a filesystem read; the `native` and `parity` jobs are not among the failures. Not started: N2f's numbers; the exact-i64 and `deep_recursion_gauge` cases in the matrix; the wide-function split (§17.240 (3): about 30 s at 16,384 guarded rows, 115 s at 32,768, phase unattributed); row M's native bench lane; N3; N4; native on B and C; every §17.177 window. Release binaries are built without `native` (STABILITY's Native row); the driver staticlib is found through `SAKURA_NATIVE_LIB_DIR`, else `lib/sakura/native` beside the binary's directory (REQUESTS N2b (2)); a native `main` declaring `Serve`, `Llm` or `WebSocket` exits 75 at startup, `Http` having left that list in `5b1f9430` (ABI §1b). *Contracts.* RFC 0001: a program on stable features "must compile unchanged on 1.3 ... the compiler may produce faster code or new warnings"; "a new warning is permitted; making that warning an unconditional error is not; a user-requested warnings-as-errors mode may fail on new warnings"; ABI MINOR "adds tags, imports, section fields, or layouts while leaving old ones" and a host refuses a greater MINOR with `V8003`; a retired code is reserved forever and a different failure needs a new code. `codes.txt` keeps every assignment with status `active`, `reserved` (not yet emitted) or `retired`; `W8001 reserved copy_on_write` has stood since round 13; `V8007` is unassigned. §17.306 (3): 1.0.0 is cut from a commit whose only difference from the last beta is its preparation commit, a contract change after the last beta is a new beta, and the gate is the campaign's ledger; §17.306 (4) and `road-to-1.0.md` stage 6 already say "beta.N for anything additive that lands meanwhile (... native if its matrix is green, still experimental)". §17.264: no quiet windows; a baseline is a counted run (instructions retired) on the reference Mac (host `d88970189598`) in `../sakura-counted`; agents may run it, only the owner blesses. ABI is 1.16.0; nothing above it is in flight. *The owner's direction (2026-10-21).* Finish all of M5 including M5b (N5, N3, N4), native on B and C, and ship `--target native` as an experimental flag in release binaries; Sakura is to be better than any other language; 1.0.0 stays gated on the Windows ledger alone and is cut from the last beta plus its preparation commit; the 1.0 contracts do not break. **Decision.** **(1) What ships where; the contracts hold either way.** (a) §17.306 (3)'s rule, applied to M5: a row on `main` at the last beta's preparation commit is in 1.0.0; a row that lands after it is in the next 1.x minor (1.1.0, 1.2.0, ...), never in a 1.0.x patch (a patch is fixes); no row holds a beta and no beta waits for a row; a new beta is cut for each beta-worthy set on `main` while the ledger fills, as §17.306 (4) already permits. The ledger's hours run on `main` between betas and the seven targets fuzz the frontend, the LIR, the JS and WASM backends and the evaluator, none of which emits native code, so a native commit between betas neither invalidates a row nor is covered by one; native's own safety evidence is (2e) and the §17.173 lanes. (b) **`W8001`.** A new warning in a beta or a 1.x minor is compatible by RFC 0001's own sentence; `reserved` → `active` is the transition the inventory exists for, and the forbidden transitions are reuse and silent retirement. A user's warnings-as-errors mode may start failing, which the RFC states and the CHANGELOG entry names. `W8001` ships in the first beta whose preparation commit contains N5 (beta.4 on the order in (2)); it is never promoted to an error, and its reason allowlist (§17.172 (1)) and its set of proven sites widen only as proofs widen, under §17.307 (2)'s rule: a diagnostic that names more of the truth is not a contract break and a lost warning is a regression. (c) **ABI.** N3's reuse tokens and N4's borrowed convention each change what generated code asks of the runtime (new runtime entry points, or a second convention for existing ones), so each is one ABI MINOR allocated at landing from the next free number — 1.17.0 to whichever of the two lands first, 1.18.0 to the second, never pre-allocated, never two in one commit (§17.289 (11)'s one-at-a-time rule) — with `sakura_abi_version` moved in the same commit and `rt/tests/fixtures/abi/<version>/` captured after it; `stats()` gains no field (§17.247 (2): miss reasons are a debug-only export). A 1.16 host refuses a 1.17 module with `V8003` and loads every older module, which is the ABI MAJOR contract RFC 0001 names, and the native driver's refusal of a newer MINOR (N2d) is the same rule on the other target. A representation change under §17.177 is a new profile and its own MINOR; none is decided here. (d) **Native stays experimental through 1.0.0** (§17.225 (8)): STABILITY's Native and ABI rows keep `experimental` with "—"; `sakura build --help` labels the target; a native build prints one line naming the target, profile and ABI (§17.175 (6), built in (2d)). Experimental promises what §17.245 said — the flag and the driver may change or be absent in a later release without a migration — and permits what it never permitted: a native program observing different semantics from `js` and `wasm`. Parity is the matrix and a divergence is a defect at every stage. Diagnostic codes, the JSON records and the exit codes are one contract on every target: a native build emits the same `check --json` rows as a JS build by construction (the frontend is shared) and `sakura test --target native` emits the same test records (N1b's test-mode acceptance in (2a)); exit 75 for an unavailable service stays until (2a) empties the list for everything but `WebSocket`, whose native rows are the web lane's. No item addressed to the designer is open after this entry. **(4) "Better than any other language", measurably.** The claim is per workload and lane or it is nothing (§17.109). *Speed.* The targets are §17.109's M5 ceilings, unchanged and not renumbered: numeric kernels (`fib`, `countdown`, `sieve`, `nbody`, `spectral_norm`) at most 1.5× Rust matched and 1.0× Go; allocation kernels (`binary_trees`, `rbtree`, `pipeline`, `shapes`, `map_set`) at most 1.2× OCaml native and 1.2× Koka C on both of Koka's lanes; `handled` at most 1.0× Koka C; `tokenizer` and `json_validate` at most 1.5× Rust matched — ceilings on medians of the metric the baseline counts (instructions retired since §17.264; wall time beside as information), against the panel at `bench/toolchains.toml`'s pins, semantics-matched as §17.109 defines it, on row M's native lane of a blessed baseline. "Within the envelope" is the 1.0-era claim once the numbers exist; "faster than X on Y" is a sentence the site may print only for a program and lane whose blessed ratio is below 1.0 (§17.153: the site prints no unblessed number), and the ceilings at 1.0 that would make it true are Go on the numeric kernels and Koka on `handled`, so those are where "faster" is first falsifiable. The three ceilings §17.152 carried (`sieve`, `nbody`, `spectral_norm`) stay carried until §17.177 (1)–(2)'s baseline. No number is written here; the first native number is beta.5's baseline on the order in (2). *Compile time.* N2f's blessed report sets the budget (§17.175 (4)); the target it is read against is research/10 §6's: compile-to-object for a 10k-line program within the 500 ms build budget on the reference Mac, link reported beside and not inside it; the wide-function curve linear after N2g. *Safety.* Already the bar and measurable: the four §17.173 lanes green with their controls on every beta's commit (A now, B and C as they land); `exec-native` hours in the ledger; parity across three backends on every corpus and example program as a CI gate, which no language in the panel runs; exact `Int` on native and WASM where the JS backend is `D003` (the exact-i64 lane). *Footprint.* RSS on the allocation kernels, the native executable's size and its process startup are recorded in row M's records beside OCaml's and Koka's, reported and carried under §17.177 (1)–(2); no target until a baseline exists. *Not a claim:* anything measured on a loaded machine, under emulation, or on a commit without a blessed baseline. *Backend.* Cranelift stays the one backend (research/16 §3: a second backend, PGO or custom SIMD lowering is a later decision after N3, N4 and the scalar window, and only if profiles show machine-code costs remaining); no LLVM row exists in M5, and research/16's ten ranks map onto this entry's lanes — 1 to N1 and F, 2 to row M and N2f, 3 to N3, 4 to the §17.177 windows, 5 to N4, 10 to N2g — with 6 to 9 outside M5. **Why.** The owner has asked for all of M5 and for native to be the thing Sakura is known for; the gate for 1.0.0 was set one round ago to the ledger alone and has not moved, so the two are reconciled by §17.306 (3)'s own rule rather than by holding either. RFC 0001 was written so that warnings, ABI MINORs and new targets arrive in minors, and this round uses it as written. The windows were already counted baselines; naming who blesses and who reads is the division the owner set on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21. The descriptor is the compiler–driver contract shipped as one artefact and not ABI text (§17.308 (3), N2a (4)); a release binary's compiler and driver are built together, and `sakura test` sets the empty permissions table (§5.8) so the check it skips would admit nothing anyway. (b) **A missing `tests/fixtures`, or no project, gives `Test.fixtures()` an empty in-memory `Dir`**: ratified; the WASM host reads the same directory, so the answer is the same on every host and no spec sentence changes. (c) **Header names.** Ruled otherwise, in the smallest way: a served `Request.headers` carries ASCII-lowercased names on every host. `hyper` gives them so; the JS host passes Node's `rawHeaders` case through (`sakura_runtime.js`'s serve loop), which §17.308 (1d) forbids as a native-only difference once a program can observe it — and a program can, with no fixture today. The fix is on the JS host (lowercase the name as it is pushed; one line, `runtime/js`, Opus, before beta.4's preparation commit) because the lowercase name is what `std/http`'s own code compares (`String.to_lower(h.0)`) and what RFC 0002 §2.3's `Headers` already presents. The list's order is not a contract on either host: `hyper` groups a repeated name at its first position and Node keeps arrival order; a program that needs an order or a join reads the list through `Headers` (lowercase, sorted, combined), which is the same on both. One served fixture pins the lowercase names and the `Headers` view on both hosts and prints neither host's raw order. CHANGELOG under Changed, as a fix: a program matching a served header name case-sensitively on JS already matched Node's case and matches now. (d) **A listen error's text** maps the OS classes Node names (`EADDRINUSE`, …) to Node's text, other errors carrying Rust's: ratified under §17.229 (5)'s one errno-class table on both hosts; an error outside the table has no pinned text, and a class a fixture needs joins the table on both hosts, never one. (e) **`SAKURA_MAX_SOCKETS` is not enforced natively**: ratified as nothing to enforce. The variable bounds WebSocket sockets of both roles on the JS host (`runtime/js/ABI.md`, 1,024 by default, 503 over it) and is not a Serve limit on any host — neither host bounds open HTTP connections today, and each request is bounded by the 1 MiB cap and the copy budget. Native reads it when the native WebSocket row lands (the web lane's; the row's acceptance includes the limit and its `D091` on an invalid value, as the JS test holds). An open-connection bound for Serve on every host is a 1.x row with its own entry if a program asks; the native page states that no host has one. (f) **Property tests** (`prop_*`) stay `rt_code_unsupported` natively until their own slice: ratified. `KNOWN_NATIVE_TESTS` is the list of what is not native while N1 runs, and §17.308 (2a)'s "`KNOWN_NATIVE` is empty" reads as both lists empty at the lane's close. N1 took property tests first (`propertySteps`: generation, shrinking, regressions, the `property` records byte-equal to JS under a seed) and the exclusion table as ABI §1b's table, which §17.170 (2) already placed there, read by `parity.rs` so that a row whose program agrees, or that names no program, fails: ratified ahead of its code reaching `main` — a table the parity test enforces is better than one on a page, and the order is the lane's. The CLI page's native section cites that table and adds what is not a program row: `WebSocket` (the web lane) and the Serve connection bound of (e). Llm (§17.308 (3), unchanged) is N1's last item and empties the table; empty, or each row a named lane, is also what (1e) of §17.308 reads at stabilization. **(2) N3's five readings (2026-10-22, ABI 1.17.0).** (a) **Pairs inside one block**: ratified for 1.17.0 as §17.176 (3)'s region read strictly; the token never crosses a call, so restart and cancel free it as any word and the landing pads need no case. The cost is the one the lane measured: `rbtree`'s recursive arm (`T(c, ins(l, k), y, r)`) splits the reset from the `Alloc` by a direct call, so `rbtree` gains only its root's `blacken` (10/9 → 1,010/1,009 attempts/hits on the lane's run) and the rebuilt nodes stay fresh allocations. §17.176 (3) forbids a suspension point, a `Perform`, a host call, an unknown call or an escaping closure between creation and consumption and does not forbid a direct twin call, so **tokens across direct calls are N3b's third item**, after (e)'s two, built as follows: the token crosses the call as an ordinary object word in a frame slot — it is one: `rt_check_token`'s own definition, a live, unshared object of the tag with every slot zero — so a restart or cancel pad frees it as it frees any held word, with no new slot kind and no ABI change; the callee may do anything, since what the token holds is storage whose children were already dropped at the reset, and holding it across the call delays one free by one call; the validator's linearity rule is unchanged (consumed or freed exactly once on every path, the pad's free included). If the frame protocol turns out to need a distinct slot kind for it, that is an ABI MINOR allocated at landing with the reason in REQUESTS, never folded into another row's number (§17.289 (11)). The default the lane named ("wait for a frame slot kind") is replaced by this, because the object-word reading needs none. (b) **"Matching class" is the same `Shape`**: the same record row, or the same variant row and the same constructor; two constructors of one type with equal slot counts are not paired, and tuples are not paired (no `Proj` names their row as a constructor would): ratified for 1.17.0. §17.176 (3)'s words (class, layout row, slot kinds, child count) also permit a pair across two constructors of one variant type with the same layout row, slot kinds and child count, the tag rewritten at the reuse; it is built only if the first native baseline's debug miss reasons (§17.176 (1): `incompatible_layout`) show it worth a row on a named program, and is otherwise not revisited. Tuples stay unpaired. (c) **"Poisons token consumption" is a check at consumption**: `rt_check_token` under `--native-checks` stops the process unless the token is `Unit` or a live, unshared object of the tag, large enough, with all slots zero; nothing else holds the token, so there is nothing later to poison: ratified; §17.173's table row ("poison on free and token consumption") reads as this check, and N2e's deferred clause is closed. (d) **A reset that misses costs a drop and a counter** (`shapes`: 5,000 attempts, no hit, its objects shared): ratified. An attempt is one count test on a path that already tests the count (§17.176's performance line), the counter is the honest number (§17.176 (1): a candidate is never a hit), and §17.177's rule stands — nothing switches on the counters; no heuristic skips the attempt. (e) **Not built**: `List.map` leaf/tail reuse (the row's §17.176 (5) acceptance, with the failing-closure-at-element-two fixture under `audit_owned`) and the `m5-stress` set under the lanes are **N3b's first two items**, Opus, now, before N4 (N4 shares the validator files and starts after N3b lands); the timing deltas are row M's at the baseline (§17.308 (2h): advisory until then); `abi/1.17.0` is captured after beta.4's tag, as 1.16.0 was (lane W's reading 8). Beta.4 does not wait for N3b (§17.308 (1a): no beta waits for a row): reuse is on the shipping WASM backend, and the evidence it ships on is `e55977f8`'s own — the parity corpus, the validator, `audit_owned` over the LIR corpus, and `native-sanitizers.yml` green on that commit (Memcheck over the compiled corpus, ASan over the in-process corpus, Miri over the runtime). Why now: WASM is a stable target and the program's `Int` is exact there, so an encoder that prints a different number prints a wrong one with no diagnostic, where JS is `D003` by §4.1 and native is exact; §17.306 (3)–(4) carry fixes in betas. (4) **Limits** ratified and stated: a function whose only cut places would enter more than four blocks, or blocks with an open `with`/`try` region or an `Id` parameter, stays whole (a 16,384-arm `Switch` fans out to every arm; `deep_ir.rs`'s `sparse` is compiled whole), and a cut function and its direct callers run on frames, never direct twins; both go on the native page's limits table beside §17.240 (3)'s line, which now reads as this entry; no corpus function (417 blocks at most) or benchmark function (119) is cut. `PIECE` = 1,024 and `ENTRIES` = 4 are the pass's constants, read from the curve at 512–4,096, and move only with a counted reason in REQUESTS. **(4) N5 (2026-10-21)** was answered by §17.308 (3) (1)–(5) and N5.5 has landed at 54 ms on every edit; the entry gets its `Answered` line now, and nothing of N5 is open. **(5) The Llm port**: no follow-up was raised; §17.308 (3)'s ruling stands unchanged and it is N1's next item under (1f). **(6) §17.308 (2) amended for what landed.** Beta.4 carries, on today's reading of `main`: `W8001` with the LSP and MCP reporting it; `--target native` in the A release binaries with the staticlib, `V8007` and the native smoke in `verify-published.yml`; native test mode, serve, `V8004` and `log_json`; the exact-i64 lane; N2g's split; constructor-site reuse on WASM and native; **ABI 1.17.0**. 311. **Milestone P starts now, under the owner's direction of 2026-10-22 ("start doing them all right now"), with its research and plan written first as §17.225 (7) required (round 63).** Decision: packages are researched in [research/17](research/17-packages.md), specified in [RFC 0003](rfcs/0003-packages.md) (Draft; its FCP gates no lane, as RFC 0001's gated no beta) and executed by [`docs/plans/packages.md`](plans/packages.md), whose lane P1 is startable at this commit. The fixed answers, each with its rejected alternative in the RFC: MVS within a major with one version per name per build (a major conflict is `V8036` naming both requirement paths; multiple majors rejected because the import's first segment is the package name); `sakura.lock` `version = 2` with SHA-256 of a canonical tarball per entry, authoritative for every compiler command, which never resolve or fetch (only `add`, `update`, `sync`, `vendor`, `deps search` and `publish` reach the network); a static signed index in a GitHub repository served by GitHub Pages with tarballs on that repository's Releases, published by pull request through the publisher's own `gh` identity and built, checked and attested by the registry's workflow (no paid infrastructure; a hosted service, URL-only dependencies and npm-as-transport rejected); the Elm rule from `InterfaceDelta` extended to effect rows, error unions, contracts, `Schema` shapes and the effect ceiling, applied by `publish` and by the registry; and the differentiator: a package's **effect ceiling** (`[package] effects`, the std effects its public rows may require, checked by the effect checker as `V3030`, recorded by `sakura add` in the consumer's entry and enforced on upgrade as `V8032`) and the **authority gate** (`V6020`: a dependency may not call a `host()` constructor or declare `@external` unless the consumer marks it `trusted`), so a dependency's authority is exactly what its public rows require and what the consumer's handlers provide.
