313. **The JS ownership and code-shape lane (`61b3d338`..`6e9248d8`) is ratified rule by rule — the sink rule, the scalar-reader rule, read hoisting, adopted literals, the fresh-record and owned-record sites and the conditional-expression join — each with the condition that makes it sound; read hoisting moves from the JS backend's private copy into the shared Core pipeline, so the WASM and native backends stop copying where JS no longer does and `W8001` is computed on the module every backend emits, which closes the question of where `W8001` runs (extends §17.149 (1)–(2), §17.172 (1), §17.201 (3), §17.273 (1) (c), §17.290 (6); `bench/deltas.md` row "JS ownership and code shape"; CHANGELOG Unreleased; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: seven commits after `v1.0.0` (`61b3d338` the sink rule, `7a2e22c7` the scalar reader, `0e98675a` read hoisting, `d318cfda` adopted literals, `65cc44e6` the fresh-record site, `42d47b13` the conditional join, `6e9248d8` the owned-record site) move the quick suite's geometric mean of Sakura/hand-JS instructions from 2.72 to 2.46 on Node and 4.01 to 3.49 on Bun, `awfy_sieve` 23.1 → 2.97, `bg_nbody` 11.3 → 5.13, `awfy_richards` 13.6 → 7.32, with no cell worse beyond the flag but `rbtree` on Node at n = 10,000 (+4.1%, cause not found). Every rule is an emission-time fact in `sakura_core::opt::owned` that only the JS backend acts on; the LIR recomputes the same facts for `--dump owned` (§17.176 (2)); the committed Core snapshot is unchanged; read hoisting (`opt::owned::hoist_reads`) rewrites the JS backend's *copy* of the module and `--dump owned`/`--dump core`, while `W8001`'s witnesses are computed on the original Core (`sakura_analysis::copy_warnings`), so a `W8001` can name a read that JS has moved and whose copy JS no longer makes; the evaluator's ownership audit passes on every benchmark; JS/WASM parity is green. Decision: **(1) The sink rule stands (amends §17.149 (1)'s consuming summary).** A top-level def whose result type holds no collection, carrier or closure *sinks* an ownable parameter when, with the parameter owned at entry, the analysis finds no retaining use of it (no `borrowed-after`, `captured`, `stored`, `escapes-call`, `join`) and at least one more site is owned; it gains the owned entry `f$o`, which a caller calls only with an owned argument at its last use. Sound because the only ways a value leaves a def are its result (excluded by the result type), a `fail` payload, handler state, a capture, a store or a perform argument, each of which the analysis counts as retaining; recursion is the existing greatest fixpoint (`owned_sink` pins owned, retained, twice-used and recursive sinks). **(2) The scalar-reader rule stands (amends §17.273 (1) (c)).** A call of a def that borrows the list at every position it receives it, whose row is pure (no effect, no failure, no open tail) and whose result is `Unit`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Float`, `String` or `Bytes` keeps a chain's elements owned: such a def can keep an element only in its result, a failure or handler state, and it has none of the three (`owned_elements_reader` pins the effectful reader and the tuple-returning reader as `shared(elements)`). **(3) Read hoisting stands and moves into the shared pipeline.** The rule as landed: in a `Let` chain, a total read of a tracked local (a field or tuple projection, `list_len`, `map_len`, `set_len`) that follows a call receiving that value or a part of it is bound just before the call; a read whose result is itself tracked moves only when all its uses are reads that move; a projection every arm of an `if` or `match` binds at its start is bound once before the branch. It is semantics-preserving on every backend because values are immutable and these reads cannot fail or perform, and it is the same win on WASM and native: an unhoisted `s.current_task` after `put_task(s, …)` keeps `s` live across the call, so the LIR passes `s` with a `Dup`, the callee sees count 2 and §17.126's dynamic path copies, exactly the path copy JS made. So `hoist_reads` becomes a pass of `sakura_core::opt` that runs for every backend before `owned`'s facts and before the snapshot is committed; the snapshot and LIR corpus diffs are reviewed as "reads moved, nothing else"; `--dump core` shows the hoisted module as it does now; the differential run gains the toggle `SAKURA_DIFF_HOIST=0` beside `SAKURA_DIFF_ELEMENTS` so hoisting is A/B'd against the evaluator. **`W8001` is then computed on the hoisted module** without any other change to §17.172 (1): the warning keeps meaning "this update copies on every execution", and it no longer names a read that was moved. Until that lands, `W8001` stays as built: correct for WASM and native, conservative on JS; it is not moved after hoisting on the JS copy alone, because `sakura check` is target-independent and a warning that is false on WASM is worse than one that is conservative on JS. **(4) Adopted literals stand.** `list_of` adopts its fresh array (a literal with elements is a `fresh` origin, as §17.149 (1) lists it); `[]` is the empty singleton and is not fresh (an owned push onto it allocates, as every owned entry tests, ABI §7). **(5) The fresh-record site stands (extends §17.290 (6)).** A record allocated in the def (or a join parameter only fresh records reach), every use of which is a read, a return or a jump into joins none of whose code (nor that of any join they jump on to) encloses the rebuild, is reused by the next rebuild that projects it and after which it is dead, with no guard. Sound because a read copies a field out, a return ends the def, and a jump is a terminator, so the object can only be seen again through the parameter of a join that holds the rebuild, which the condition excludes; the condition is exactly what CE2 and CE4 of §17.290 violated, so both counterexamples are re-run under this site and pinned as allocating in `owned_record_fresh` (a one-commit addition if they are not already there). **(6) The owned-record site stands.** `T {..p, f: …}` where `p` is an owned carrier dead after the rebuild — the consumed parameter of an owned entry, or a join parameter every jump moves an owned record into — writes into `p`. Sound by the ownership proof itself: no other reference to the object exists, so the write is unobservable whatever the rebuild flows to; an element read (`at(bs, j)`, class `Elem`) is never an owned carrier, so the §17.273 (2) guards are untouched. **(7) The conditional-expression join stands**, JS codegen only: a join of two pure arms (single-use bindings that inline; no CPS call, exit, contract entry, unproved overflow check or site mark) is `c && B`, `c || B` or `c ? A : B`; only the taken arm runs, which is the §4.1/§5.7 semantics (`short_circuit_pure`). **(8) Placement restated.** Ownership facts stay emission-time and out of the snapshot (§17.149 (2)); the JS backend acts on the record sites and owned entries; the LIR recomputes every fact for parity and acts on none of the record sites because N3's reuse tokens and §17.126's counts do the same dynamically; the one shared rewrite is (3). **(9) `rbtree` +4.1%** on Node at n = 10,000 is an attribution item for the lane's next compare (the JS differs only in `[]` and the runtime file: start from `list_empty()`'s singleton and the `list_of` adoption), not a gate. Why: each rule is a static proof of the same property (no other reference, or no retained element) that §17.149 and §17.273 already rest on, and the lane's own oracle (`audit_owned`) and parity runs are the evidence; moving hoisting into Core is the one place the lane under-delivered, since the WASM and native backends pay the same copy for the same unhoisted read. Rejected: `W8001` after hoisting on the JS copy only (target-dependent warning); a per-backend hoisting flag (one Core, §17.118); any of the rules as source annotations (§17.117, §17.126). Performance: as the lane measured; (3) is expected to move `awfy_richards` on WASM and native as it did on JS (counted at the next baseline, never claimed before). Changed: §13.2 (hoisting a Core pass), §13.4 (pointer), §17.149 (1) (the sink and literal rules), §17.172 (1) (computed on the hoisted module), §17.273 (1) (c), §17.290 (6); plan `performance-r1.md` §4.1 rows. Impact: Opus (the hoisting move: `sakura_core/src/opt`, snapshot fixtures, `sakura_lir` corpus, `sakura_analysis::copy_warnings`; CE2/CE4 pins); CODEOWNERS review as semantics-adjacent for (3)'s snapshot diff.

314. **WASM runtime ABI 1.19.1, the in-place object paths erratum (`9546140b`..`dde47a40`), is ratified as a PATCH on 1.8.2's precedent, with the conditions under which compiled code and the linker's synthesised functions may do the runtime's work inside the module (the owed entry; ABI §0, §3.1, §10; RFC 0001 "ABI versioning"; `bench/deltas.md` row "WASM inline object paths"; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: five commits move into the emitted code what the runtime did per call: scalar memory access without the wasm32 `Mem` bounds re-check, `Dup`/`Lend`/`TupleGet` and constructor reset, small-object allocation from the free lists (the internal symbol `rt_heap_cell` gives the main pool's free-list heads, the §10 counters and the emergency pool's start, which never move), the last `Drop` of a tuple, record or variant whose row owns at most one slot when that child survives (the synthesised `sakura$drop`), and list element and `Option` payload reads; the quick suite's Sakura/JS geometric mean on Node falls 21.08 → 13.11, 81 of 92 cells by more than 10%, none worse; every program's output and §10 counters equal the baseline compiler's but `requested`, which grows by the emitter's static tables (120–272 bytes); `sakura_abi_version` stays `0x011300`; the `bench_counters` test enforces the counter values. Decision: **(1) PATCH, ratified.** No byte layout, tag, import, export signature, outcome or counter value changes, and 1.8.2 already let compiled code decrement a count in place and count it in a module global the `stats` export adds in; 1.19.1 extends that permission to the increment, the free-list allocation, the single-child release, the reset and the reads, each counted where its runtime call would have counted. **(2) The conditions, now part of §3.1's permission:** (a) only a *counted* object (static flag clear) is written in place; a static object's `rc` is never touched, and the increment stops below `u32::MAX` with the runtime's `rt_dup` as the cold path (`D092` as before); (b) the inline last-drop path applies only outside the emergency pool, to a row owning at most one slot, and only when the child's decrement does not reach zero; every other release, and every `String` or `Bytes` (the `wipe` flag of 1.19.0), goes through the `drop` export's worklist; (c) a free-list allocation writes the header exactly as `Heap::alloc` and `new_object` do, and falls back to the runtime when the class's list is empty; (d) `rt_heap_cell` is a link-time symbol between the runtime object and the emitted code, as `rt_dup_candidate` is, not a module export a host may call; if the linker leaves it in the export list, §9 names it internal and the optional-export probe (§17.222) ignores it — a test asserts one or the other; (e) §10's definition of `requested` reads "bytes requested from the allocator, the static block and the emitter's tables included", so the counter's growth is its definition, not a drift. **(3) Housekeeping.** ABI §0's "its design §17 entry is owed" becomes "design §17.314" at the next touch of the file (the native lane's rebase, §17.318, carries it); STABILITY.md's ABI row reads the current version (1.19.1 now; 1.20.0 when §17.318 lands); the CHANGELOG's Unreleased line stands. Why: the erratum changes what the module does for itself, not what it asks of its host, which is the line 1.8.2 drew; the counters are the proof that nothing semantic moved, and the test holds them. Rejected: a MINOR (it would make 1.19 hosts refuse modules that need nothing new of them); an unconditioned permission (the static flag, the emergency pool and `wipe` are each a byte the runtime guards). Performance: as measured, advisory until the next counted baseline. Changed: ABI §0 (1.19.1 cites this entry), §3.1 (the conditions), §10 (`requested`). Impact: the native lane's rebase (the §0 and STABILITY lines), Opus small (the export test (2d), the `requested` sentence).

315. **Edit ownership in the JS runtime (WS-P22): a statically linear segment of a list, map or set chain that starts from a shared value gets an *edit token*, and the runtime writes in place every node that token stamped and copies every other node once — the per-node reference-count test the WASM and native runtimes already make (§17.126's dynamic path, §17.149 (2)) carried to a runtime without counts; allowed in 1.x because the JS runtime's representation is internal and value semantics are unchanged (STABILITY.md's ABI rows; RFC 0001 "What is not covered"; §8.1; §17.117, §17.126, §17.149, §17.201 (3), §17.217, §17.265 (6), §17.275 (3), §17.290; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: `bg_fannkuch_redux` is 22.6× hand JS on Node and 17.7× on Bun after the lane, unchanged, because `var perm = perm1` aliases the list and every later `List.set` on `perm` (up to n/2 per flip) copies its tail, where the hand-written program copies `perm1` into `perm` once per permutation and writes in place; `map_set`'s `let snapshot = mi` makes every later `Map.update` and `Map.remove` on `mi` persistent (§17.275's facts: 845 M against 135 M); in both, every version after the alias is linear (consumed once, read only by borrows) and only the origin is shared, so §17.149's proof stops at `origin` and the whole chain copies forever, while on WASM and native the first write after the alias copies the path (count 2) and the next writes find count 1 and write in place. The JS runtime has no counts; its only in-place path is the static proof. Decision: **(1) Allowed in 1.x.** STABILITY.md lists the JS ABI v0, the generated JS and the runtime representations as `internal`; `sakura_runtime.js` is emitted beside the modules by the same compiler, so no two revisions of it ever meet and there is nothing to negotiate or shim; the one host-visible surface, `__entries__.js`'s values, is documented as the runtime's own with no promised shape (ABI §6 "Library entries"), and RFC 0001 names generated code text as not covered. What is promised and may not move: §8.1 value semantics (no program, under any handler, in direct or `--no-direct` mode, on any backend, can observe a write), `Show`, `Eq`, `Ord`, `Hash` and JSON, the §17.80 trace, determinism and the memory bound (a stamp is one field, never a retained reference). **(2) The mechanism, by constraints.** (a) A *segment* of a chain is a maximal run of versions between *retaining uses* (an alias live after, a store, a capture, a return, a perform argument, a call that neither consumes nor borrows, a join one of whose incoming jumps passes a non-owned value: the existing reasons `borrowed-after`, `stored`, `captured`, `escapes-call`, `join`, `param`, `field`, `tuple`). A segment is *edit-eligible* when its origin is not fresh, it holds at least one consuming site, and every one of §17.149's other conditions holds inside it (its sites would all be `owned` if the origin were). (b) The emitter binds `x$e = list_edit(x)` (`map_edit`, `set_edit`) at the segment's start — after the retaining use, or on the jump that carries the shared value into the segment's join — an O(1) operation: a new wrapper with a fresh token (an object, never a reused integer) over the same nodes, its leaf cache empty. (c) Every consuming site of the segment calls the `_edit` entry (`list_set_edit`, `list_push_edit`, `map_insert_edit`, `map_update_edit`, `map_remove_edit`, `set_insert_edit`, `set_remove_edit`; the same arguments as `_owned`): on the path, a node stamped with the wrapper's token is written in place; any other node (unstamped, or stamped by another token) is copied, stamped and linked, building exactly what the persistent operation builds; the wrapper is updated in place; the leaf cache is refreshed when the leaf it points at is replaced. (d) The `_owned` entries and fully fresh chains are unchanged: no stamp test on the proven path; nodes they create are unstamped. (e) Stamps are never cleared and never reused: a segment's end makes its token unreachable to compiled code, and a later `list_edit` of any wrapper over those nodes gets a fresh token, so they copy once more. The invariant the static proof gives and the oracle checks: an `_edit` entry runs only on a wrapper made by its own segment's `list_edit` or returned by an `_edit` entry of the same segment. (f) `Map` and `Set`: the log is a `List` and rides the same token; the index's branch nodes (`HNode`, the integer trie's branches and 32-slot leaves, `HLeaf`, `HColl`) stamp the same way; an update of an existing key touches the log only, as now (§17.275 (3)). (g) The flat `List<Bool>` (§17.265 (6)) under an edit converts as the persistent write converts it, then stamps; one O(n) copy per segment, as a persistent write costs today. (h) Entries: `$entry$<name>`'s parameters are never owned or edit-eligible (their call sites are the host's), and a value an entry returns is never written again by the program; a host test passes a previous result back as an argument and reads the first value intact. **(3) Tooling.** `--dump owned` prints `edit` for such a site, naming the retaining use that starts the segment (`edit(after <reason> at <pos>)`), beside `owned` and `shared(<reason>)`; the LIR's `--dump owned` prints the same (both call `display`; the LIR acts on none of it, counts do its work); `W8001` does not fire on an `edit` site, because its message ("copies on every execution") would be false — the copy is bounded to one per node per segment entry — and fires on `shared` sites as before; `audit_owned` treats every `_edit` entry as it treats `_owned` (the consumed version is dead after) and `list_edit` as a non-consuming read of its argument, so a read of an edited version after a later write of its segment stops the evaluator; the differential generator gains the alias-then-update and snapshot-then-update shapes (§17.290's lesson: the generator was blind to the shapes it did not write). **(4) Fixtures** (`tests/semantics`, trace, `--no-direct` and WASM parity): fannkuch's shape with `perm1` read after `perm`'s writes and `perm`'s elements read after `perm1`'s next-permutation writes; the snapshot shape (a map retained, updated and removed from after); a segment ended by a store (a record holding the list) and a second segment after it; a retained middle version (`let keep = xs` between two writes in a loop) intact; a segment whose loop runs zero times (one wrapper, no copy); `Map<Int, _>`, `Map<String, _>`, `Map<(Int, Int), _>` and `Set<Int>`; the flat `List<Bool>`; the §17.149 invariants re-run through an edit (closure capture before the write, a list stored in a `Map` value, the same loop run twice, an update inside `with` and after a `Perform`, a generic def). **(5) Protocol and exit (WS-P13a's).** First the ablation: the emitted `bg_fannkuch_redux` module hand-edited to copy `perm1` once at the alias and call `_owned` entries after (the bound the mechanism can reach), its count recorded; then the lane, which lands when `bg_fannkuch_redux` at the largest quick size on Node is within 10% of that bound, `map_set` and `map_set:int` fall on Node and Bun, and `awfy_sieve`, `sieve`, `bg_nbody`, `rbtree`, `pipeline` and every other quick cell stay within the compare flag (the persistent workloads must not pay for the test). Why: the owner's goal is speed by default against hand-written JS, and the alias-then-update loop is the commonest shape in ported programs (every Benchmarks Game port does it); the mechanism is Clojure's transient discipline with the compiler holding the discipline instead of the programmer, and it is the same per-node test the other two runtimes make with counts, so the three backends keep one cost model; per-node stamps cost O(path) whatever the list's size, which an explicit copy at the alias does not. Rejected: a mutable array, builder value or ownership annotation in the language (§17.117, §17.126); an O(n) spine copy at the alias (`list_fresh`), which pays n when the segment makes no write and loses to one path copy on a large trie; a JS reference count (every bind and drop would pay); switching representation on the fact (§17.217 (1)); stamp tests in the `_owned` entries (a cost on the proven path); a JS `Map` or array behind the alias (§17.275's rejection stands, §17.317). Performance: one identity compare per path node on edit sites, one wrapper per segment start; nothing on `owned` or `shared` sites. Changed: §13.4 (`List`, `Map`/`Set` rows: the edit path), ABI §7 "Owned entries" (the edit entries and the invariant), §17.149 (2) (the JS backend now has a dynamic path), §17.172 (1) (no `W8001` on `edit`), plan `performance-r1.md` §4.1 row WS-P22. Impact: Opus (`sakura_core/src/opt/owned` segments and verdict, `sakura_codegen_js` emit, `sakura_runtime.js` entries and stamps, `tools/sakura_eval` audit and generator, the host entries test); the CODEOWNERS review §17.149 named, as a semantics-adjacent change.

316. **Variants on JS become one object each, fields as own properties (WS-P23), and `Option` gets a dynamic niche, `None` as `null` and `Some(x)` as `x` unless `x` is `null` or already nested (WS-P24, gated by its A/B); both are allowed in 1.x for the reason §17.315 (1) gives, with neither an ABI MINOR nor a shim, since the JS runtime has no independently versioned host; on WASM and native the tagged `Option` and boxed words stay, answering the §17.177 (2) and (5) questions of 2026-10-22 (ABI §7; §13.4; §17.99; §17.151; §17.177; §17.199 (1); §17.275 (4); REQUESTS 2026-10-22 items 2–4; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: a `Some(x)` on JS is `new Option(1, [x])`, two allocations (the instance and its `fields` array), and every variant constructor with fields pays the same; `Result`'s `Ok`/`Err` likewise; `Show`, `Eq`, `Ord`, `keyOf`, the JSON codecs, property generation and `conforms` read `{ tag, fields }` structurally with the type descriptor `$t`; §17.151 and §17.275 (4) already fuse the `Option` away at `List.get`/`Map.get` consumed at once, so the remaining `Some`s are the ones that escape fusion (iterators, `find`, `parse_int`, the std returns). Natively, at `shapes` 100,000 the `Some` wrappers are 518,091 objects, 17.7% of `requested` and 7.9% of the instructions, `map_set` 3.6% of bytes, nothing elsewhere; the scalar-leaf bound is ≤ 11.8% on `spectral_norm` and +13.6% on WASM; the regions trigger is not met; each default has held since 2026-10-22. Decision: **(1) Allowed in 1.x, and how.** As §17.315 (1): the layout is internal, the runtime is co-shipped, so there is no version to bump and nothing to shim; the change is a CHANGELOG Changed line, ABI §7's variant and `Option` rows, and one sentence in ABI §6 "Library entries": a host that needs a stable shape for an entry's result uses `json_encode` with the entry's result schema, and nothing else about the values is promised. "Deferred to 2.0" would be a misreading of RFC 0001, which covers no representation of the JS runtime. **(2) WS-P23, one object per variant.** An emitted `class T extends $rt.Variant` holds `tag` and the payload as own properties `f0 … fk` in constructor order (`Option`'s `Some` is `{ tag: 1, f0 }`, `Result`'s both constructors likewise), one allocation; nullary constructors stay frozen singletons; the arity of a constructor comes from `$t.ctors[tag].h.length`, which `show`, `eq`, `cmp`, `keyOf`/`ser`, the JSON codecs, property generation, shrinking and `conforms` read instead of `fields.length`; Core payload projection `i` emits `.f<i>`; `Switch` reads `.tag` as now. No semantic change; parity and the differential run are the oracle. Lands when no quick cell is worse than the flag and the variant-heavy cells move (`shapes`, `awfy_json`, `awfy_list`, `awfy_cd`, `rbtree`, `json_validate`). **(3) WS-P24, the `Option` niche on JS, the dynamic universal form.** Representation: `Rep(None) = null`; `Rep(Some(v)) = Rep(v)` unless `Rep(v)` is `null` or an instance of the runtime's `Nest` class, in which case `new Nest(Rep(v))`; `is_some(o)` is `o !== null`; the payload is `o instanceof Nest ? o.v : o`; `Some` construction tests the two excluded shapes. Sound for `Option<Option<T>>` to any depth by induction (the two shapes a payload may not take are recognisable at run time, so no schema table is needed, which is what made the universal form costly on WASM, §17.199 (1)); `Unit`'s `undefined` stays distinct from `null`, so `Some(())` is `undefined` and `None` is `null`. Every structural routine gains its `null` arm before any property read (`ser(null)` is a new serialisation, `cmp(null, x)` is less, `eq` by identity, `show`/JSON schema-directed as now; `conforms` accepts `null` for `None`; a missing record field of `Option` type decodes as `null`); `Result` keeps (2)'s layout (both constructors carry a payload; no niche). Limit, documented: `show` of a value whose schema is unsolved (`null`, the existing lossy edge of ABI §7) prints the payload for a `Some`. Gate: lands only when the quick geometric mean moves at least 2% or an `Option`-heavy cell at least 10%, with no cell worse than the flag; otherwise (2) alone stands and the measurement is recorded. **(4) WASM and native: tagged `Option` and boxed words stay; the regions counter stays bench-only; §17.177 (2) and (5) are closed as decided, not carried.** A 7.9% instruction saving on one program and a ≤ 11.8% bound on another, with nothing elsewhere, do not pay for an ABI MINOR across the LIR, `rt` and both codegens, the per-field schema table, the §17.99 parity gate and the fuzz streams' clean hours after a layout change (`lir`, `exec`, ≥ 4 CPU-hours each). Re-opened only at a later native window on a program whose `Some` wrappers exceed 20% of `requested` or whose scalar leaves bound more than 15% of its instructions; the JS niche's A/B records the `Some` count per quick program as that evidence. Why: one allocation is the floor a variant can have on a JS engine, and the niche is the floor an `Option` can have; the JS backend's freedom here is exactly what STABILITY's `internal` row bought, and spending it where the native backend cannot (no schema table on a self-describing heap) is the right asymmetry. Rejected: a MINOR with a compat shim (nothing to version); deferring to 2.0 (nothing promised); the known-type niche (§17.199 (1): rejected for the same reason on JS, a type-directed emitter special case generic std code would miss); a `fields` array kept beside the properties (two shapes, two allocations on the old path). Performance: (2) halves the allocations of every variant with fields; (3) removes the `Some` allocation except for nested `None`/`Nest` payloads, at one compare per construction and per projection. Changed: §13.4 (variant and `Option` rows), ABI §6 (entries sentence), ABI §7 (variant and `Option` rows, the `null` arms), §17.177 (2), (5) (closed), plan `performance-r1.md` §4.1 rows WS-P23, WS-P24. Impact: Opus (`sakura_codegen_js` classes and projections, `sakura_runtime.js` structural routines and codecs, `runtime/js/test`), after WS-P22 (both edit `sakura_runtime.js`).

317. **The Bun-only gaps (`map_set:int` 12.6× against 3.1× on Node, `handled_fwd` 16.0× against 4.6×): no JS `Map` behind Sakura's `Map`, because the contract is persistence after sharing and not only order; the `map_set` gap is re-read after WS-P22, whose copy-once-then-in-place is what the hand-JS control pays; `handled_fwd`'s lever is WS-P10 as §17.181 (2) specified it, never built; the rest is attributed on a JSC profile before anything is built, and no engine-specific path enters the runtime (§17.152 (3), §17.181 (2), §17.201, §17.265 (5), §17.275 (1)–(2), §17.283; `bench/results/2026-10-23-6e9248d8-js-quick-compare.txt`; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: at n = 10,000 `map_set:int` is 12.64× on Bun and 3.06× on Node (8.5× and 2.3× at n = 1,000), `map_set:string` 2.3× on Bun (the JSC string-hashing share §17.152 (3) named), `handled_fwd` 16.0× on Bun and 4.6× on Node; Bun is advisory in a counted compare (§17.265 (5)), with spreads of 10–18% on `handled_fwd`'s Bun cells. The `map_set` control keeps a JS `Map` per key kind and copies `mi` once for the snapshot; Sakura's map after `let snapshot = mi` copies a log path and index nodes on every later update and remove (§17.275's facts), which is where the two engines diverge most (JSC's `slice` of 32-slot arrays and its `instanceof` chains are the suspects, not the hash: an `Int` key is not hashed). §17.275 (2) rejected a JS `Map` index because a remove after a snapshot would copy it whole. `handled_fwd` wraps every operation in `Handler<Tick, {Tick}>` whose clause is `Tick.next()`: an unbound perform per operation inside a CPS clause, two `find`s, a `cctx` and a continuation per hop; §17.181 (2) specified WS-P10 (identity forwarders marked `forwards` in Core and skipped by `find` when tracing is off, so the §17.80 trace is identical in every mode), and no `forwards` exists in Core or either runtime today. Decision: **(1) No JS `Map` or `Object` as the index for `Int` or `String` keys.** Determinism is not the obstacle — a JS `Map` is insertion-ordered and SameValueZero, which is Sakura's order and equality (§17.275 (1)) — persistence is: a retained version makes every later update O(n), so `rbtree`-style and snapshot workloads go quadratic, and §17.275's rejection stands. **(2) `map_set:int` is re-read after WS-P22.** The snapshot pattern then copies each node once and writes in place after, which is the control's one copy; if the Bun cell is still above twice its Node cell, (4) runs on it. **(3) WS-P10 is scheduled as specified**, engine-agnostic, on both runtimes (the WASM `find` takes the same flag), the lever for `handled_fwd` on Node too. **(4) WS-P25, the Bun attribution** (Astra or Opus, after WS-P22 and WS-P23): Bun's CPU profiler on `map_set:int` and `handled_fwd` at n = 10,000, the ten top frames by self time, testing the named hypotheses — the 32-slot arrays' storage mode under JSC (holey against contiguous, `int32` against `double`, from how the arrays are created), `instanceof` polymorphism over `HNode`/`HLeaf`/`HColl`, `Array.prototype.slice` on 32-element arrays in the persistent path, and for `handled_fwd` the `cctx` and continuation allocations and the `ret` bounce — in a `research/10-evidence` note; a fix lands by §17.201's rule, a number before a mechanism, when it moves the Bun cell at least 20% and leaves every Node cell within the flag. **(5) One runtime.** No `typeof Bun`, `process.versions` or engine test in `sakura_runtime.js` or the emitter; a shape that helps one engine lands only when it costs the other nothing beyond spread, because the output, trace and counts must be the engine-independent contract they are. Why: the gap is on an advisory engine, so it buys no mechanism on its own; what it buys is attribution, and the two structural causes (the shared snapshot and the forwarding clause) already have decided, engine-agnostic fixes. Rejected: a per-map key kind (WS-P11b, measured flat, §17.201 (1)); a dense array behind `Map<Int, _>` (§17.217: dense ids are a `List`); copy-once-then-in-place as a representation switch (§17.275, measured +21%; WS-P22 is the proof-driven form of it). Performance: none until measured. Changed: plan `performance-r1.md` §4.1 (WS-P10 scheduled, row WS-P25). Impact: Opus (WS-P10), Astra (WS-P25).

318. **The native lane's ABI 1.20.0 (`d5485441`, `eb95c1e5`, `4dcfaaa9`, `c5e092d8` on `b00877f9`, unpushed): ratified as a MINOR with the rebase conditions below — the §0 history lists 1.19.1 first, the in-place `Dup` tests the static flag, the checked lowering reads the defect flag after every builtin so the `total` table has an oracle, the thread precondition is written into §1b — and pushed now, the §17.312 freeze having ended with the `v1.0.0` tag (ABI §0, §1b, §3.1, §10; STABILITY.md's ABI and Native rows; §17.169, §17.171, §17.176, §17.287 (3), §17.312 (1), §17.314; plan `m5-native.md`; round 65, 2026-10-23).** Facts: the four commits decode each layout row once through a 256-entry direct-mapped cache reset by `set_layout` and zero small blocks with stores (no counter changes); skip `rt_take_defect` after the 18 `total` builtin rows; give the native context six `u64` counters at +16 (`dups`, `drops`, `reuse_attempts`, `reuses`, `borrow_candidates`, `borrows`) that compiled code adds to and `stats()` adds in, and make the `Dup` (in place below `u32::MAX`, `rt_dup` the cold path), the `Drop` above count 1, the `Lend`/`DupCandidate` counts, the reuse of a token's block and the `reuse_reset` of a row owning no slot at count 1 in place; and test a step by a nonzero constant for overflow with one compare (`x + c` overflowed iff the sum is below `x` for `c > 0`, above for `c < 0`; `i64::MIN` subtracted and non-constant operands keep the flag form). Native instructions, advisory: `awfy_list` −28.8%, `awfy_bounce` −20.8% then −11.2%, `countdown` −17.8%, `awfy_json` −15.1%, `nbody` −13.1% then −5.9%; every counter keeps its value on five benchmarks and in the corpus's `--no-direct` comparison. The lane's `sakura_abi_version` is `0x011400`; since it branched, `main` took 1.19.1 (§17.314) in the same §0 list; 1.17.0, 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 were each a MINOR by 1.3.0's rule for a change internal to the linked module; STABILITY lists the WASM ABI stable and the native profile experimental; the native driver staticlib ships beside the `sakura` that built it, so no native executable meets another revision's runtime. Decision: **(1) MINOR, ratified.** By §0's letter a layout addition is a MINOR (the context prefix's +16..+64 is a layout the profile fixes), and by 1.3.0's rule the counters a module writes are part of what it requires; a 1.19 host's refusal of a 1.20 WASM module is the cost every MINOR has carried and the Node host ships with the compiler. Recorded as a ponytail, not built: a profile-scoped revision for `offset32-v1`, so a native-only change stops bumping the shared MINOR; decided when a second native-only MINOR arrives. **(2) Rebase conditions.** (a) §0 lists 1.19.1 (citing §17.314) before 1.20.0 (citing this entry); `sakura_abi_version` is `0x011400`; the beta.6 release module fixture (`5f1bfbb0`, 1.19.0) still loads on the 1.20 host (host MINOR ≥ module MINOR), pinned by the ABI fixtures; the Node host's `ABI_VERSION` and the `bench_counters` snapshot (which 1.19.1 moved) are regenerated and reviewed; STABILITY.md's ABI row reads 1.20.0. (b) The in-place `Dup` writes only a counted object: the emitted code tests the static flag (or the emitter proves the word counted at that site), as 1.19.1 requires of wasm32; a fixture dups a literal in a loop under `--native-checks` and a plain build. (c) The in-place `Drop` only while the count is above 1; the last decrement goes through `sakura_drop` (the worklist, `wipe`, the counters) — as written. (d) The in-place `reuse_reset` only for a row owning no slot at count 1, leaving the header word for word as the runtime's reset does (a test compares the two); otherwise `rt_b_reuse_reset`. (e) §1b states the precondition that makes non-atomic in-place counts sound: one OS thread owns an instance and nothing reachable from it (§17.171), and no object is reachable from two instances (`std/worker` messages are copied text); a shared heap (§13.5's promotion to atomic on cross-thread send) revisits every inline path before it exists. (f) The `total` table's oracle: `--native-checks` keeps every runtime call *and* reads the defect flag after every builtin, aborting with the builtin's name when a `total` row raised; if the checked lowering does not read the flag today, the lane adds it; the parity job's checked build runs the corpus under it. (g) The constant-step compare is ratified on its identity (for `c ≠ i64::MIN`, `x − c` is `x + (−c)`), the fixture at `i64` `MAX` and `MIN` from both sides stands, and the JS backend's `D003` at the literal is the documented difference (§17.44). (h) The row cache is ratified: deterministic, reset on `set_layout`, Miri-covered; a collision re-decodes. (i) The six counters are read by the next counted native baseline at a release's preparation commit (row M's rule); the commits' numbers stay advisory. (j) CHANGELOG: one Changed line for the native backend (experimental) and one for the ABI MINOR. **(3) The freeze.** §17.312 (1)'s "a change there is a beta.7" ended with the `v1.0.0` tag; compiler changes now land on `main` for 1.1.0 under RFC 0001, and the lane pushes by the CI push gate (local gates, fetch, rebase, re-run the affected quick gates, push). Why: the inline paths are 1.19.1's permission applied on the other target with the counters as the same proof, and the rebase conditions are the three places the commit messages do not say what §3.1 requires (the static flag, the header after a reset, the thread precondition) plus the one oracle the `total` table lacks. Rejected: renumbering as a PATCH (§0's letter; and a 1.19 host would then run a module whose `stats()` it could not read); splitting the version constant now (a new concept for one change on an experimental profile); holding the push for a window (nothing waits for one). Performance: as measured, advisory. Changed: ABI §0 (1.20.0 cites this entry), §1b (the counters, the precondition), §3.1 (native in-place paths), §10; STABILITY.md ABI row; CHANGELOG. Impact: Opus (the native lane's rebase and push, `t3/optimize-native-backend`), small beyond the rebase.

319. **The hand-out after round 65, ranked, with file sets so two lanes run at once only when the sets are disjoint (§17.285's rule; §17.313–§17.318; round 65, 2026-10-23).** (1) **The native lane's rebase and push** (§17.318; Opus, now, its worktree): native crates, `runtime/rt` (`ABI.md` §0/§1b/§3.1/§10 and the §17.314 citation), `abi.rs`, the Node host's version constant, `bench_counters`, STABILITY's ABI row, CHANGELOG. (2) **WS-P22, edit ownership** (§17.315; Opus, now, disjoint from (1)): `sakura_core/src/opt/owned` (segments, the `edit` verdict, `display`), `sakura_codegen_js` (the `list_edit` binds and `_edit` calls), `sakura_runtime.js` (stamps, the `_edit` entries, the cache refresh), `tools/sakura_eval` (`audit_owned`, the generator shapes), the fixtures and the host entries test; the fannkuch ablation first. (3) **WS-P10, forwarding clauses** (§17.317 (3), §17.181 (2); Opus, now, disjoint from (2): `sakura_core` `MakeHandler` and `--dump core`, the runtime's `find` in `sakura_runtime.js`'s handler section and `rt`'s `find`, `--no-direct` and trace fixtures). (4) **WS-P23, one object per variant** (§17.316 (2); Opus, after (2): `sakura_codegen_js` classes and projections, `sakura_runtime.js` structural routines and codecs, `runtime/js/test`). (5) **Read hoisting into Core and `W8001` after it** (§17.313 (3); Opus, after (2): `sakura_core/src/opt`, the snapshot fixtures, the `sakura_lir` corpus, `sakura_analysis::copy_warnings`, the differential toggle), with the CE2/CE4 pins of §17.313 (5) and the `rbtree` attribution of §17.313 (9) in the same lane. (6) **WS-P24, the `Option` niche on JS** (§17.316 (3); Opus, after (4), gated by its A/B). (7) **WS-P25, the Bun attribution** (§17.317 (4); Astra, after (2) and (4); no compiler code). (8) **§17.314 (2d)** (the `rt_heap_cell` export test) and **(2e)** (the `requested` sentence): small, ride with (1). Order of value: (2) moves the largest remaining class of programs (every alias-then-update loop) on both engines; (1) is ready and native is the owner's main benchmark; (3) is specified and small; (4)–(6) are the allocation floor; (7) decides whether anything Bun-specific remains after the structural fixes. Nothing here changes a stable surface: every change is under STABILITY's `internal` or `experimental` rows or is a semantics-preserving optimisation whose oracle is parity, the differential run and the counters.

320. **In-place small-object allocation from the free lists in native code: ratified as an ABI MINOR (the next free number at landing; 1.21.0 if it lands before WS-P10), because the native context's prefix gains the two addresses compiled code needs; allocation only, no inline release; the sanitizer builds hide the free lists so every allocation under ASan and Memcheck stays the runtime's; and §17.318 (1)'s ponytail is closed: no profile-scoped revision (ABI §0, §1b, §3.1, §3.5, §10; STABILITY.md's ABI row; §14.3; §17.171, §17.173, §17.181 (2), §17.314, §17.318, §17.319; `9bc4fde0`, `084276df`..`18b8fb0b`; round 66, 2026-10-23).** Facts: on wasm32 since 1.19.1 (`9bc4fde0`) compiled code pops the class's free list itself for a tuple, record, variant or closure whose size it knows: the head takes the block's link (`+4`), `requested` grows by the requested size, `live` by the class size, `live_objects` by 1, `free_list_bytes` shrinks by the class size, `peak` is raised to `live` when below it, the header word is written as `tag | class << 16 | 1 << 32` (flags 0, `rc` 1) and every byte after it is zeroed with stores; an empty head is `rt_alloc`. The three addresses it needs (the main pool's sixteen heads, the `Stats` block, the emergency pool's start) come once, at `sakura$init`, from the internal link-time function `rt_heap_cell` into three module globals, which is why 1.19.1 was a PATCH. Natively every `Alloc` is still `rt_alloc` (three sites in `sakura_codegen_native/src/func.rs`) through the context, `Heap::alloc`'s class search, counters and fill and `new_object`'s header; the native lane's 1.20.0 made the count changes in place with the six counts at +16 (§17.318). Four facts differ from wasm32. (a) A process may hold any number of instances and one thread may own several (§1b), so a module global cannot hold an instance's addresses, and the heap's `Pool` and `Stats` live inside `Rt` behind the prefix's "+64 private" line: the addresses can come only from `ctx`, which is a layout. (b) The sanitizer lanes of §17.173 run the *plain* lowering: the ASan job runs the in-process corpus (`the_corpus_runs_natively`, `two_instances_close_in_one_process`, …) with `sakura_rt/asan`, and the Memcheck job runs the compiled corpus nightly with `sakura_rt/valgrind`; under both `Heap::free` poisons the whole freed block, `Heap::alloc` unpoisons the link and then the block (`mem.rs` `link`, `init`), and the freed-object-read control depends on that poison. A free-list pop in compiled code reads a poisoned link and writes a poisoned block: both lanes turn red at the first allocation, or the poison is weakened and the control means nothing. (c) `Heap::alloc` tries the main pool before the emergency pool even while unwinding (`small(c)`, then `emergency_small(c)` on failure), so a main-list pop made by compiled code during unwinding takes exactly the block the runtime would have taken; the emergency pool, chunk carving, growth and `D096` are reached only through the runtime. (d) The native emitter already depends on `sakura_rt` (`native::is_total`, `bf47743f`), so the class table and the `Stats` offsets need no copy and no equality test, and its `sakura$tuple_kinds` table lives in the object file, so `requested` does not move (unlike wasm32, §17.314 (2e)). Decision: **(1) MINOR, ratified, under the rule that closes §17.318 (1)'s ponytail.** The prefix gains two fields and the private region moves: `+64 uint32_t *`, the main pool's sixteen free-list heads (`Pool.free`, heap offsets, in §10's class order); `+72 uint64_t *`, the §10 counters (`Stats`, `repr(C)`; §1b lists the byte offsets of the five compiled code updates); private from `+80`. A layout addition is a MINOR by §0's letter, as 1.20.0's counts were; the number is the next free MINOR at landing, 1.21.0 if this lands before WS-P10 and 1.22.0 after. The rule, so that no lane waits on a number again: a native-only change that adds to §1b's prefix or to the counter set is a MINOR of the shared number; a native-only change in what compiled code does for itself with no layout change is a PATCH, as 1.19.1 was; a profile-scoped revision (`offset32-v1`'s own number) is **not built**, and is re-opened only when a WASM host ships apart from the compiler (then a MINOR's refusal costs a real user) or when the native profile stabilises under RFC 0001 (then it gets its own row anyway). Today a MINOR's whole cost is the version-bump set (ABI §0's line, `abi.rs`, the Node host's constant, the `bench_counters` snapshot, STABILITY's ABI row, a CHANGELOG line), an hour once, and a second number is a concept every reader of §0 would carry for a refusal nobody meets. **(2) The permission, in §3.1's words: native code may take a block from a small class's free list of the main pool and write it as `Heap::alloc` and `new_object` do, when the class's head is nonzero; everything else about allocation stays the runtime's.** Conditions: (a) *Exactness.* The block and the counters end byte-identical to the runtime's, step by step as the facts list them; a runtime test allocates each class once through the inline path and once through `Heap::alloc` + `new_object` and compares the block and the `Stats` byte for byte, as §17.318 (2d)'s reset test does for the header. The lane may bound the classes it inlines (the zeroing is `class − 8` bytes of stores) and send the rest to `rt_alloc`; the bound is the commit's, not the ABI's. (b) *The emergency pool.* Compiled code reads neither `emergency` nor `em_exhausted` and never allocates from the emergency pool: an empty head is `rt_alloc`, which carves, grows, serves the emergency pool while unwinding, or raises `D096` from the allocating site as today. Fixture: `oom_while_unwinding`'s shape compiled natively under a small `SAKURA_MAX_HEAP`, a finalizer allocating small objects during unwinding, the same outcome, output and counters plain and checked. (c) *No inline release.* The last decrement, the release and the free stay `sakura_drop`'s on native, 1.19.1 (b)'s single-child path included: a compiled free would push an unpoisoned block onto a list the sanitizers believe closed, and §17.173 (5) lets no lane be cited without its control. `wipe` is therefore untouched: a fresh block's flags byte is 0, and the flag is set and read only on the runtime's release path (§3.5). Re-opened only with a design that keeps the freed-block poison exact (a runtime-drained inbox, or a sanitizer-build lowering that keeps the call), as its own entry. (d) *The thread precondition.* §1b's sentence extends from the counts to the free lists and the §10 counters: one OS thread owns an instance and everything reachable from it, nothing is reachable from two instances, and a shared heap revisits this path with the others before it exists. (e) *Sanitizer builds.* Under the `asan` and `valgrind` features the heads the prefix points at are a sixteen-word zero array the runtime never fills, and the real lists stay private, so every allocation in those builds is `rt_alloc` with its unpoison, and the counters are the plain build's (the runtime pops the block compiled code would have popped). The ASan in-process corpus and the nightly Memcheck corpus keep covering every other in-place path of 1.20.0 and this change's cold path; §14.3's sentence gains "in sanitizer builds compiled code allocates through the runtime"; Miri covers the runtime only, as before. (f) *Checked lowering.* `--native-checks` keeps every `rt_alloc`, as it keeps every in-place path; `the_corpus_runs_clean_under_native_checks` stays the reference run. (g) *Oracles.* Every `stats()` counter, `requested` and `committed` included, is byte-identical to the parent commit's for the corpus under both toggles and for the quick benchmark set, and identical between the plain and checked builds; outputs, defects and exit codes identical (the parity job's `native_` set); the §7.5 live-object baseline at exit in the M5 stress set; the `--no-direct` comparison with the evaluator; `two_instances_close_in_one_process` and a new sibling with two instances on one thread allocating in alternation, each instance's counters its own. A heap-resident emitter table, should the lane ever need one, comes back here first (`requested` would move). (h) *Reuse tokens.* `Alloc … reuse t` with a non-pointer token takes the inline path, as on wasm32; a pointer token's block is reused as 1.20.0 says. (i) *Addresses.* The two pointers are written after the instance is in its final place (`Box::leak`, `native/mod.rs`) and never change; `Instance::stats` reads the runtime's `Stats` through the same pointer under a debug assertion. (j) *The version-bump set.* §0 lists the new version citing this entry; `sakura_abi_version` is the next constant; the beta.6 fixture (1.19.0) and a 1.20.0 fixture still load (host MINOR ≥ module MINOR), pinned by the ABI fixtures; the Node host's `ABI_VERSION` and the `bench_counters` snapshot are regenerated and reviewed; STABILITY's ABI row reads the new version; CHANGELOG: one Changed line for the native backend (experimental) and one for the MINOR. wasm32 is unchanged but for its version. **(3) Ordering against WS-P10.** §17.181 (2)'s `forwards` mark on `MakeHandler` is read by the runtime's `find`, so where the module stores it decides its class: a bit in a heap object's header, a handler layout row or any byte the runtime reads is a MINOR of the shared number (1.3.0's rule, and it touches wasm32); a Core-only mark the emitter resolves into existing bytes is none. The two lanes' code sets are disjoint (this one: `sakura_codegen_native/src/func.rs`, `rt/src/native/mod.rs`, `rt/src/heap.rs`; WS-P10: `sakura_core`'s `MakeHandler` and `--dump core`, `rt`'s handler search, `sakura_runtime.js`), and they share only (2j)'s version-bump set; numbers are allocated in landing order, the second lane to land rebases that set, and nothing else in either entry changes. This lane is expected first: it is specified to the byte and the WASM commit is its template. Why: the free-list pop is the one runtime call left on the allocation path after 1.20.0 and the WASM lane measured what removing it buys (`binary_trees` 5.45× → 4.56×, `awfy_bounce` 47.6× → 40.9×, `rt_alloc` and `Heap::alloc` leaving the profile); the two addresses can come only from `ctx`, which makes the number a MINOR and not a matter of taste; and the sanitizer lanes are the only coverage generated native code has besides its counters, so they are kept exact by moving the fast path out of their builds rather than the poison out of the runtime. Rejected: a PATCH on 1.19.1's precedent (there the addresses were link-time symbols into module globals; here they are a layout, and §0's letter is what keeps the version readable); embedding `Pool.free` and `Stats` in the prefix (one load fewer per allocation, at the cost of moving the heap's state out of `Rt`, which wasm32 shares); a thread-local for the addresses (one thread may own several instances); a compiler flag for sanitizer builds (`--native-checks` exists, and the sanitizer corpus runs the plain lowering on purpose, §17.173 (2)–(3)); inline release now ((2c)); a profile-scoped version now ((1)); `rt_heap_cell(ctx, k)` per allocation (a call, the thing removed). Performance: wasm32's numbers are the expectation; native instructions per call are advisory until the next counted native baseline at a release's preparation commit (row M's rule). Changed: ABI §0 (the new version citing this entry), §1b (the two fields, the private offset, the thread sentence, the sanitizer-build note), §3.1 (the native allocation permission and (2c)'s exclusion), §10 (the native sentence names allocation); STABILITY.md's ABI row; §14.3 (the sanitizer-build sentence); §17.318 (1)'s ponytail, closed by (1). Impact: Opus (the native lane, its worktree: `sakura_codegen_native/src/func.rs`, `rt/src/native/mod.rs`, `rt/src/heap.rs`, the tests of (2a), (2b) and (2g), the version-bump set); the WS-P10 lane applies (3) and asks only if its mark fits neither case.
